52842.q: Which big predatory fish was released into Lake Victoria in the 1950s and pushed out many cichlid species?
52842.e: The Nile perch was brought in for fishing and ate many native fish. As a result, hundreds of cichlid species have become rare or died out.
52842.m: The Nile perch greatly changed the wildlife of Lake Victoria.

52843.q: Which introduced plant at times covered large areas of water on Lake Victoria?
52843.e: The water hyacinth comes from South America and spreads very fast. Its thick mats block boats and take light and oxygen from the water.
52843.m: The water hyacinth is a dangerous pest on Lake Victoria.

52845.q: Which three countries share Lake Victoria?
52845.e: Most of the lake belongs to Tanzania and Uganda. Kenya has a small share in the north-east.
52845.m: Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya share Lake Victoria.

52846.q: Roughly how big is Serengeti National Park compared with Switzerland?
52846.e: The national park covers about 14,800 km², Switzerland about 41,300 km². That is a little more than a third.
52846.m: Serengeti National Park is about a third the size of Switzerland.

52848.q: Why is the Serengeti a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
a: Because of its huge animal migrations
Because of its old temple ruins
52848.e: Every year more than a million wildebeest and many zebras move through the Serengeti. Because of these unique migrations, UNESCO added it to the World Heritage list in 1981.
52848.m: The Serengeti is World Heritage because of its great animal migrations.

52849.q: Why do almost only short grasses and hardly any trees grow on the plains in the south of the Serengeti?
a: There is a hard layer of lime under the ground
The soil is as salty as seawater
The Maasai cut down all the trees
52849.e: Volcanic ash from the nearby highlands has formed a hard, lime-rich layer in the soil there. Tree roots can hardly get through, but grasses grow well.
52849.m: A hard layer in the soil makes the south of the Serengeti a treeless grassy plain.

52850.q: Which big cat, the fastest land animal in the world, hunts on the open grassy plains of the Serengeti?
52850.e: The cheetah reaches more than 90 kilometres per hour when sprinting. On the wide plains of the Serengeti it mainly hunts gazelles.
52850.m: The cheetah is the fastest land animal.

52851.q: What do lions in the Serengeti like to use the big rocks rising out of the flat plain for?
a: As a lookout and resting place
52851.e: The granite rocks rise out of the grassland like islands. From up there, lions can see far across the plain and find shade and hiding places.
52851.m: Lions use the rocks of the Serengeti as a lookout.

52852.q: Why do the wildebeest in the Serengeti move around in huge herds every year?
a: They follow the rain and the fresh grass
They are fleeing from the snow
They are looking for caves to spend the winter
They go to the sea to swim
52852.e: Where rain falls, fresh grass grows. So the wildebeest move in a circle through the Serengeti and the Maasai Mara, always following the food.
52852.m: The wildebeest follow the rain and the grass.

52853.q: Which small gazelle with a black stripe on its side is very common in the Serengeti?
52853.e: Thomson’s gazelle has a clear black stripe along its side. Very many of them live in the Serengeti, and they are important prey for cheetahs.
52853.m: You can recognise Thomson’s gazelle by its black side stripe.

52854.q: Which country ruled Kenya as a colony until Kenya became independent in 1963?
52854.e: Kenya was a British colony. The country became independent on 12 December 1963.
52854.m: Kenya was a British colony until 1963.

52856.q: Which city is Kenya’s most important seaport?
52856.e: Mombasa lies on the Indian Ocean and is Kenya’s second largest city. Its port is one of the most important in East Africa.
52856.m: Mombasa is Kenya’s big port on the Indian Ocean.

52857.q: For which farm product is Kenya one of the world’s biggest exporters?
52857.e: Large tea plantations grow in Kenya’s cool, rainy highlands. Kenya exports tea to many countries, including in Europe.
52857.m: Kenya is a big tea exporter.

52858.q: What did the Kenyan Wangari Maathai become famous around the world for?
a: She had millions of trees planted
She was the first to climb Mount Everest
She won Olympic gold in the marathon
52858.e: Wangari Maathai founded the Green Belt Movement, which planted millions of trees. In 2004 she became the first African woman to receive the Nobel Peace Prize.
52858.m: Wangari Maathai planted trees and received the Nobel Peace Prize.

52859.q: Which Kenyan runner became the first person to run a marathon in under two hours, in Vienna in 2019?
52859.e: Eliud Kipchoge ran 1:59:40 hours in Vienna. Because it was a special race with rotating pacemakers, the time does not count as an official world record.
52859.m: Eliud Kipchoge was the first to run a marathon in under two hours.

52860.q: Roughly how many people lived in Nairobi at the 2019 census?
52860.e: At the 2019 census, Nairobi had about 4.4 million people. This makes it the largest city in Kenya.
52860.m: With more than four million people, Nairobi is Kenya’s largest city.

52861.q: What is there right on the edge of Nairobi that is very rare for a big city?
a: A national park with lions and giraffes
A sandy beach by the sea
52861.e: Nairobi National Park is only a few kilometres from the city centre. Lions, giraffes, zebras and rhinos live there, with skyscrapers in the background.
52861.m: Nairobi has a national park with wild animals right outside the city.

52862.q: What nickname do the Ethiopian Highlands have because of their height?
52862.e: The highlands are the largest connected area above 1500 metres in Africa. That is why they are often called the “Roof of Africa”.
52862.m: The Ethiopian Highlands are called the Roof of Africa.

52863.q: Roughly how high are the highest mountains in the Ethiopian Highlands?
52863.e: Ethiopia’s highest mountain, Ras Dashen, is just over 4500 metres high. That is about as high as the highest peaks of the Swiss Alps.
52863.m: The Ethiopian Highlands have mountains of about 4500 metres.

52864.q: Geladas are monkeys that live in the Ethiopian Highlands. What do they eat almost exclusively?
52864.e: Geladas live in large groups on the high pastures. They pluck grass with their hands and eat hardly anything else.
52864.m: Geladas are the grass-eaters of the Ethiopian Highlands.

52865.q: Which animal from the Simien Mountains is a close relative of the Alpine ibex?
52865.e: The Walia ibex lives only in the Simien Mountains and is critically endangered. Like the Alpine ibex, it is a type of ibex.
52865.m: The Walia ibex is a relative of our Alpine ibex.

52866.q: Where does most of the water come from that makes the Nile swell in summer?
52866.e: In the rainy season, a great deal of rain falls in the highlands. The Blue Nile and other rivers carry this water into the Nile and used to cause the Nile flood in Egypt.
52866.m: The Nile flood comes mainly from the Ethiopian Highlands.

52867.q: What is the big dam called with which Ethiopia holds back the Blue Nile?
52867.e: The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam lies near the border with Sudan and was opened in September 2025. Its power station is the largest in Africa, and the dam is disputed between the Nile countries.
52867.m: Ethiopia holds back the Blue Nile with a huge dam.

52868.q: Roughly how high above sea level is Addis Ababa?
52868.e: Addis Ababa lies at about 2350 metres in the highlands. It is one of the highest capital cities in the world.
52868.m: Addis Ababa is one of the highest capital cities in the world.

52869.q: Which tiny-grained cereal is grown in the highlands for the flatbread injera?
52869.e: Teff is a very small grain that grows well in the highlands. Its flour is used to bake the slightly sour flatbread.
52869.m: In Ethiopia, injera is made from teff.

52870.q: Which country is part of the Horn of Africa?
52870.e: The Horn of Africa includes Somalia, Ethiopia, Eritrea and Djibouti. The peninsula sticks out into the Indian Ocean like a horn.
52870.m: Djibouti lies on the Horn of Africa.

52871.q: Which country has the longest coastline on the African mainland?
52871.e: Somalia’s coast is more than 3000 kilometres long. It stretches from the Gulf of Aden far down along the Indian Ocean.
52871.m: Somalia has the longest mainland coastline in Africa.

52872.q: Which country forms the tip of the Horn of Africa?
52872.e: Somalia lies right at the tip of the Horn. Ras Hafun, the easternmost point of the African mainland, is also there.
52872.m: Somalia lies at the tip of the Horn of Africa.

52873.q: Why do many big ships sail past the Horn of Africa?
a: They are on their way to the Suez Canal
They collect ice there for Europe
They are sailing to the North Pole
They are looking for gold in the sea
52873.e: Through the narrow strait of Bab-el-Mandeb, ships reach the Red Sea and then the Suez Canal. This is the shortest sea route between Asia and Europe.
52873.m: An important sea route to the Suez Canal passes the Horn of Africa.

52874.q: What is special about Lake Assal in Djibouti?
a: It is the lowest point in Africa
It is the highest lake in the world
It is Africa’s largest freshwater lake
52874.e: Lake Assal lies about 155 metres below sea level. Its water is extremely salty.
52874.m: Lake Assal is the lowest point in Africa.

52875.q: Which depression in north-eastern Ethiopia is one of the hottest areas on Earth?
52875.e: The Danakil Depression lies partly below sea level. There are salt flats, colourful hot springs and average temperatures of over 30 degrees.
52875.m: The Danakil Depression is one of the hottest places in the world.

52876.q: Which natural hazard hits people on the Horn of Africa especially hard again and again?
52876.e: When the rainy seasons fail, fields and pastures dry up. Many people live from keeping livestock and then face famine.
52876.m: Droughts are a great danger on the Horn of Africa.

52877.q: What do you see a lot of in Asmara, the capital of Eritrea?
a: Modern buildings from the Italian colonial period
52877.e: Eritrea used to be an Italian colony. Many modern buildings went up in Asmara in the 1930s, and since 2017 the city has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
52877.m: Asmara is famous for its modern architecture.

52878.q: Why do so many animal species live on Madagascar that are found nowhere else?
a: The island has been isolated for a very long time
The animals were bred by people
52878.e: Madagascar separated from Africa many millions of years ago and later from India. Since then its animals and plants have developed separately.
52878.m: Long isolation makes Madagascar’s nature unique.

52879.q: What is the strait between Madagascar and the African mainland called?
52879.e: At its narrowest point the Mozambique Channel is more than 400 kilometres wide. It separates Madagascar from Mozambique.
52879.m: The Mozambique Channel separates Madagascar from Africa.

52880.q: Where did many of the first people who settled Madagascar come from?
52880.e: The first settlers came by boat mainly from the area of present-day Indonesia, and later people also came from East Africa. The Malagasy language is related to languages on Borneo.
52880.m: Many ancestors of the Malagasy people came from South-East Asia.

52881.q: From which country did Madagascar become independent in 1960?
52881.e: Madagascar was a French colony. It became independent on 26 June 1960.
52881.m: Madagascar has been independent from France since 1960.

52882.q: What is the famous road near Morondava lined with huge baobab trees called?
52882.e: Along the Avenue of the Baobabs stand trees that are up to 30 metres tall and several hundred years old. It is one of the best-known photo spots in Madagascar.
52882.m: The Avenue of the Baobabs is near Morondava.

52883.q: In the Tsingy de Bemaraha on Madagascar, sharp limestone needles rise up. What shaped these points?
52883.e: Rainwater slowly dissolves limestone. Over a very long time this has created razor-sharp points. The area is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
52883.m: Rainwater shaped the limestone of the Tsingy into needles.

52884.q: Roughly how many times bigger than Switzerland is Madagascar?
52884.e: Madagascar has about 587,000 km², Switzerland about 41,300 km². 587,000 divided by 41,300 is about 14.
52884.m: Madagascar is about fourteen times as big as Switzerland.

52885.q: Which animals are Madagascar’s lemurs related to?
52885.e: Like monkeys, lemurs are primates. In the wild they live only on Madagascar.

52886.q: Which explorer was the first European to reach the Victoria Falls, in 1855?
52886.e: The Scottish missionary David Livingstone saw the falls in 1855. He named them after Queen Victoria.
52886.m: David Livingstone made the Victoria Falls known in Europe.

52887.q: Why are the Victoria Falls often called the largest waterfall in the world, even though they are neither the highest nor the widest?
a: They form the largest single curtain of water
They lie highest above sea level
52887.e: Width and height together give the Victoria Falls the largest falling wall of water. No other waterfall has such a large unbroken curtain.
52887.m: The Victoria Falls have the largest curtain of water in the world.

52888.q: What daring activity do many tourists do on the bridge at the Victoria Falls?
52888.e: The bridge over the gorge connects Zambia with Zimbabwe. Many people jump from it on a bungee cord more than 100 metres down.
52888.m: People go bungee jumping from the bridge at the Victoria Falls.

52889.q: Why do you often see a rainbow over the Victoria Falls?
a: The tiny water droplets split the sunlight
52889.e: The waterfall throws a cloud of tiny droplets into the air. When the sun shines on it, the light is split into its colours.
52889.m: The spray of the Victoria Falls often makes rainbows.

52890.q: What do you call a deep, narrow valley with steep rock walls, like the one below the Victoria Falls?
52890.e: Below the Victoria Falls, the Zambezi has dug a deep gorge into the rock over time. It runs in a zigzag.
52890.m: Below the Victoria Falls, the Zambezi flows through a gorge.

52891.q: Which list of especially valuable places do the Victoria Falls belong to?
52891.e: The Victoria Falls have been UNESCO Natural Heritage since 1989. Zambia and Zimbabwe protect them together.
52891.m: The Victoria Falls are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

52892.q: When do the Victoria Falls carry the most water?
a: At the end of the dry season
In the middle of the dry season
52892.e: After the rainy season, most water reaches the Zambezi, roughly from February to May. At the end of the dry season the water level is much lower.
52892.m: After the rainy season the Victoria Falls thunder most strongly.

52893.q: In which country is the huge Central Kalahari Game Reserve?
52893.e: The Central Kalahari Game Reserve in Botswana is one of the largest protected areas in the world. It is even bigger than Switzerland.
52893.m: The largest protected area in the Kalahari is in Botswana.

52894.q: What do sociable weavers, small birds in the Kalahari, build?
52894.e: Sociable weavers build large nests of grass with many chambers, where many pairs live together. Inside, it stays cool during the day and warm at night.
52894.m: Sociable weavers build huge shared nests in the Kalahari.

52895.q: How were the huge salt pans in the Kalahari formed?
a: The sea brought salt onto the land
52895.e: The Makgadikgadi salt pans in Botswana are the remains of a large lake that dried up long ago. The salt was left behind.
52895.m: The salt pans of the Kalahari are the remains of an ancient lake.

52896.q: What is special about the Kgalagadi park in the Kalahari?
52896.e: Botswana and South Africa run the park together. Animals such as lions and antelopes can roam between the two countries without fences.
52896.m: The Kgalagadi park connects Botswana and South Africa.

52897.q: Which antelope with long, straight horns can go a long time without drinking in the Kalahari?
52897.e: The oryx, also called gemsbok, gets a lot of moisture from plants. It can also let its body temperature rise and so save water.
52897.m: The oryx is adapted to the dryness of the Kalahari.

52898.q: What does the wild tsamma melon in the Kalahari provide for people and animals?
52898.e: The tsamma melon consists mostly of water. It is a wild relative of the watermelon.
52898.m: The tsamma melon is a water store in the Kalahari.

52899.q: Why is the Kalahari often not called a true desert?
a: More rain falls than in a full desert
52899.e: In large parts of the Kalahari, more than 250 millimetres of rain fall each year. That is why it is better described as a dry savannah or semi-desert.
52899.m: The Kalahari is more a dry savannah than a full desert.

52900.q: What was the system of state racial segregation in South Africa called, which ended in the early 1990s?
52900.e: Under apartheid, people were separated and treated unfairly according to the colour of their skin. In 1994 the first free elections for everyone took place.
52900.m: Apartheid was an unjust system of racial segregation in South Africa.

52901.q: What is the highest mountain range in South Africa called?
52901.e: The Drakensberg reaches more than 3400 metres. Part of it is called uKhahlamba in Zulu and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
52901.m: The Drakensberg is the highest mountain range in South Africa.

52902.q: Which precious stones were found in large numbers near Kimberley in South Africa from 1871?
52902.e: In Kimberley thousands of people dug for diamonds. This created the “Big Hole”, one of the largest hand-dug holes in the world.
52902.m: Kimberley is the city of diamonds.

52903.q: Why did the Dutch set up the station in 1652 that grew into Cape Town?
a: To supply ships to Asia with water and food
To build a fortress against the Romans
52903.e: Jan van Riebeeck came on behalf of the Dutch East India Company. Ships on the long journey to Asia needed fresh water and food on the way.
52903.m: Cape Town began in 1652 as a supply station for ships.

52904.q: What danger threatened Cape Town in 2018 as “Day Zero”?
a: The tap water would have had to be turned off
A power cut because of snow
52904.e: After several dry years the reservoirs were almost empty. Strict water saving prevented the day without tap water.
52904.m: In 2018 Cape Town prevented Day Zero by saving water.

52905.q: What is special about the plant life around Cape Town?
52905.e: The bush vegetation at the Cape is called fynbos. Many of its plant species are found nowhere else in the world.
52905.m: Many plants grow at the Cape that are found only there.

52906.q: Why do people in Cape Town call the strong south-east wind the “Cape Doctor”?
a: Because it blows the air clean
Because it only blows at night
52906.e: The strong south-east wind blows mainly in summer and blows smoke and dust out of the city.
52906.m: The Cape Doctor is Cape Town’s cleansing wind.

52907.q: Which Portuguese sailor was the first European to sail round the Cape of Good Hope, in 1488?
52907.e: Bartolomeu Dias was driven round the Cape by a storm. This showed that you could sail east around Africa.
52907.m: Bartolomeu Dias rounded the Cape in 1488.

52908.q: Which sailor passed the Cape of Good Hope in 1497 and became the first European to reach India by sea?
52908.e: Vasco da Gama reached the city of Calicut in India in 1498. This meant the sea route from Europe to India had been found.
52908.m: Vasco da Gama found the sea route to India.

52909.q: Is the Cape of Good Hope the southernmost point of Africa?
a: No, another cape lies further south
No, it is in South America
52909.e: Many people believe this, but Cape Agulhas lies about 150 kilometres to the south-east and is the southernmost point of Africa.
52909.m: Cape Agulhas is the southernmost point of Africa.

52910.q: What name did Bartolomeu Dias first give the Cape?
52910.e: Because of the dangerous storms, Dias called it the “Cape of Storms”. The Portuguese king later gave it the more hopeful name, because it opened the way to India.
52910.m: The Cape of Good Hope was first called the Cape of Storms.

52911.q: What is the seawater like off the west coast of South Africa?
52911.e: The Benguela Current brings cold water from the south northwards. On the east coast, by contrast, a warm current flows.
52911.m: The sea off the west coast of South Africa is cold.

52912.q: Which big city lies near the Cape of Good Hope?
52912.e: The Cape Peninsula stretches south from Cape Town. Its southern end belongs to Table Mountain National Park.
52912.m: The Cape of Good Hope lies south of Cape Town.

52913.q: Which legendary ghost ship is said to wander the sea off the Cape of Good Hope?
52913.e: According to the legend, a captain must sail back and forth off the Cape for ever with his ship, because he refused to give up. Richard Wagner turned it into an opera.
52913.m: The Flying Dutchman is a sailors’ legend from the Cape.

52914.q: Which famous waterfall is on the Zambezi?
52914.e: The Victoria Falls lie on the border of Zambia and Zimbabwe. There the Zambezi plunges more than 100 metres into a gorge.
52914.m: The Victoria Falls are on the Zambezi.

52915.q: Into which sea does the Zambezi flow?
52915.e: The Zambezi flows east and reaches the Indian Ocean in Mozambique through a delta. It is the largest African river flowing into this ocean.
52915.m: The Zambezi flows into the Indian Ocean.

52916.q: In which country does the Zambezi rise?
52916.e: The source of the Zambezi lies in a forest area in the north-west of Zambia. The country is named after the river.

52917.q: What are the big dams on the Zambezi mainly used for?
52917.e: The Kariba Dam between Zambia and Zimbabwe holds back a huge lake. Its power station supplies both countries with a lot of hydroelectric power.
52917.m: Dams on the Zambezi supply electricity.

52918.q: Which big animal on the Zambezi usually spends the day in the water?
52918.e: Hippos spend the day in the water so that their skin does not dry out. At night they go on land and eat grass.
52918.m: Hippos live in the water during the day.

52919.q: In which part of Africa does the Zambezi flow?
a: In the west on the Atlantic coast
52919.e: The Zambezi flows through southern Africa, including Zambia, Zimbabwe and Mozambique. It flows into the Indian Ocean.
52919.m: The Zambezi is a river in southern Africa.

52920.q: Which country is named after the Zambezi?
52920.e: Zambia bears the name of the Zambezi River, which rises there. Zimbabwe, by contrast, is named after ancient stone buildings.
52920.m: Zambia is named after the Zambezi.

52921.q: Before there were bridges, how did people and lorries cross the Zambezi in many places?
52921.e: In many places there were only ferries. At Kazungula a bridge has connected Botswana and Zambia since 2021.
52921.m: Bridges are replacing old ferries on the Zambezi.

52922.q: Which country replaced China as the most populous country in the world in 2023?
52922.e: According to United Nations estimates, India overtook China in 2023. Both countries have more than 1.4 billion people each.
52922.m: Since 2023 India has had more people than China.

52923.q: What did farmers in China discover in 1974 while digging a well?
52923.e: Near Xi’an, farmers came across thousands of life-size clay figures of soldiers. They guard the tomb of the first emperor of China.
52923.m: The Terracotta Army was discovered in 1974.

52924.q: Which language is the official language of China?
52924.e: Standard Chinese, also called Mandarin, is the standard language and is taught in schools across the country. There are also many other Chinese languages and dialects.
52924.m: The official language of China is Standard Chinese.

52925.q: What is the man-made waterway, more than 1000 years old, that connects Beijing with Hangzhou called?
52925.e: The Grand Canal is about 1800 kilometres long and the longest man-made canal in the world. In the past it was used mainly to carry rice from the south to the north.
52925.m: The Grand Canal connects Beijing with Hangzhou.

52926.q: What is the large tropical island that forms China’s southernmost province called?
52926.e: Hainan lies in the South China Sea and is a province of China in its own right. Because of its warm beaches it is often called the “Hawaii of China”.
52926.m: Hainan is China’s tropical island province in the south.

52927.q: Which large sand desert lies in the Tarim Basin in western China?
52927.e: The Taklamakan lies in the Xinjiang region in north-western China. It is one of the largest sand deserts on Earth.
52927.m: The Taklamakan is a huge sand desert in western China.

52928.q: What is the imperial park with Kunming Lake in the north-west of Beijing called?
52928.e: The emperors spent the hot months at the Summer Palace. The site with its lake, hill and pavilions is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
52928.m: The emperors relaxed at the Summer Palace on Kunming Lake.

52929.q: What are the narrow, traditional alleys with courtyard houses in Beijing’s old town called?
52929.e: Hutongs are narrow alleys between old courtyard houses. Many were demolished, but some are protected today as part of the city’s history.
52929.m: Beijing’s old town has narrow alleys called hutongs.

52930.q: What nickname does the National Stadium in Beijing have because of its interwoven steel beams?
52930.e: The stadium was built for the Olympic Games. Its steel beams are so interwoven that it looks like a giant bird’s nest.
52930.m: Beijing’s National Stadium is called the Bird’s Nest because of its shape.

52931.q: Which burial site of 13 Chinese emperors lies north of Beijing?
52931.e: Thirteen emperors of the Ming dynasty are buried in the Ming Tombs. A long “Spirit Way” lined with stone figures leads to the tombs.
52931.m: The tombs of the Ming emperors lie north of Beijing.

52932.q: What is the big square in front of the entrance to the Forbidden City in Beijing called?
52932.e: Tiananmen Square means “Square at the Gate of Heavenly Peace”. It is one of the largest city squares in the world.
52932.m: Tiananmen Square lies in front of the Forbidden City.

52933.q: Which city of millions lies at the mouth of the Yangtze where it meets the sea?
52933.e: Shanghai lies in the Yangtze delta. Its port is one of the largest in the world.
52933.m: Shanghai lies at the mouth of the Yangtze.

52934.q: Into which sea does the Yangtze flow?
52934.e: The Yangtze flows east right across China. Through a large delta it flows into the East China Sea, part of the Pacific.
52934.m: The Yangtze flows into the East China Sea.

52935.q: Which is the longest river in China?
52935.e: The Yangtze is more than 6000 kilometres long. It is the longest river in Asia.
52935.m: The Yangtze is the longest river in China.

52936.q: What does the Chinese name of the Yangtze, “Chang Jiang”, mean?
52936.e: “Chang” means long and “Jiang” means river. The name suits China’s longest river.

52937.q: Which city of millions in central China lies on the Yangtze?
52937.e: Wuhan lies on the Yangtze in Hubei province. The city is an important transport hub in central China.

52938.q: Which animal from the Yangtze has been considered probably extinct since a search in 2006?
52938.e: A large expedition in 2006 did not find a single Chinese river dolphin (baiji). The causes were fishing, shipping and pollution.
52938.m: The Chinese river dolphin from the Yangtze is probably extinct.

52939.q: Why is the water of the Yellow River yellowish?
a: It carries a lot of loess
It contains a lot of sulphur
52939.e: The river flows through the Loess Plateau and picks up huge amounts of fine yellow loess there. It is one of the rivers carrying the most silt in the world.
52939.m: Loess makes the Yellow River yellow.

52940.q: What sad nickname does the Yellow River have because of its floods?
52940.e: Throughout history the Yellow River has often caused devastating floods and has changed its course several times. That is why it is called “China’s Sorrow”.
52940.m: Because of its floods, the Yellow River is called China’s Sorrow.

52941.q: The sea into which the Yellow River flows belongs to which ocean?
52941.e: The Yellow River flows into the Bohai Sea, part of the Yellow Sea. This belongs to the Pacific.
52941.m: The Yellow River flows into a marginal sea of the Pacific.

52942.q: Why is the area along the Yellow River seen as the cradle of Chinese culture?
52942.e: Along the middle and lower Yellow River, farming and the first Chinese kingdoms developed early. The fertile loess made farming possible.
52942.m: Chinese culture began on the Yellow River.

52943.q: After the Yangtze, which river is the second longest in China?
52943.e: The Yellow River, Huang He in Chinese, is about 5500 kilometres long. This makes it the second longest river in China.
52943.m: The Huang He is China’s second longest river.

52944.q: Roughly how long is the reservoir behind the Three Gorges Dam?
52944.e: When full, the reservoir stretches about 600 to 660 kilometres upstream. That is almost twice the length of Switzerland from west to east.
52944.m: The Three Gorges reservoir is about 600 kilometres long.

52945.q: What record does the power station at the Three Gorges Dam hold?
a: Largest hydroelectric power station in the world
Highest dam wall in the world
52945.e: With a capacity of about 22,500 megawatts, it is the most powerful hydroelectric power station on Earth. It supplies as much power as many large nuclear power stations together.
52945.m: The largest hydroelectric power station in the world is at the Three Gorges Dam.

52946.q: Which river does the Three Gorges Dam hold back?
52946.e: The Yangtze is the longest river in China. The dam holds it back to form a huge lake.
52946.m: The Three Gorges Dam holds back the Yangtze.

52947.q: Why is electricity from the Three Gorges Dam better for the climate than electricity from coal?
a: Hardly any CO2 is produced while it runs
It is switched off at night
52947.e: A hydroelectric power station uses the force of flowing water. Unlike a coal power station, it burns nothing and so gives off hardly any CO2 while running.
52947.m: Hydropower produces electricity with almost no CO2.

52948.q: Roughly how many people had to be moved because of the Three Gorges reservoir?
52948.e: The reservoir flooded towns, villages and fields. So well over a million people had to find a new home.
52948.m: More than a million people were moved for the Three Gorges reservoir.

52949.q: How can ships get past the Three Gorges Dam?
a: With locks and a ship lift
Not at all, the river is closed
Through a tunnel in the mountain
52949.e: Large ships pass through a staircase of locks with five steps. Smaller ships are raised in a ship lift, just like in a lift.
52949.m: Ships get past the dam using locks or a ship lift.

52950.q: Apart from generating electricity, what important purpose does the Three Gorges Dam have?
52950.e: The reservoir can hold back a lot of water during heavy rain. This is meant to protect the cities downstream from floods.
52950.m: The Three Gorges Dam is also meant to protect against floods.

52951.q: What was the Great Wall of China mainly meant to protect the empire against?
a: Armies with elephants from the south
52951.e: Nomadic horse-riding peoples such as the Xiongnu and later the Mongols attacked China from the north again and again. The wall was meant to make these attacks harder.
52951.m: The Great Wall of China was meant to keep out horse-riding peoples from the north.

52952.q: From which period do most of the well-preserved sections of the Great Wall of China date?
52952.e: The emperors of the Ming dynasty (1368 to 1644) had the wall greatly extended with bricks and stones. These are the parts tourists usually visit today.
52952.m: The well-known parts of the Great Wall date from the Ming period.

52953.q: Who had older sections of wall joined into one long wall around 220 BC?
52953.e: Qin Shi Huang was the first emperor of a united China. He had the existing defensive walls of the earlier states joined together.
52953.m: The first emperor of China joined the old walls together.

52954.q: Roughly how long is the Great Wall of China with all its sections?
52954.e: A survey in 2012 added up all the sections of wall from different periods. They are more than 21,000 kilometres long.
52954.m: With all its parts, the Great Wall of China is more than 20,000 kilometres long.

52955.q: What does the Chinese name of the Great Wall, “Changcheng”, mean?
52955.e: “Chang” means long and “Cheng” means wall or city wall. So the Chinese simply call the structure the Long Wall.

52956.q: What are the well-preserved sections of the Great Wall of China mainly made of?
52956.e: Under the Ming dynasty the wall was greatly extended with bricks and stones. Older parts were often made only of rammed earth.
52956.m: The well-known parts of the wall are made of bricks and stones.

52958.q: Shanghai lies at the mouth of which big river?
52958.e: Shanghai lies where the Yangtze flows into the East China Sea. The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia.
52958.m: Shanghai lies at the mouth of the Yangtze.

52959.q: Which building is even taller than the Shanghai Tower, the tallest building in China?
a: Empire State Building in New York
52959.e: The Shanghai Tower is about 632 m tall. Only the Burj Khalifa in Dubai, at about 828 m, is clearly taller.
52959.m: The Shanghai Tower is one of the tallest buildings in the world.

52960.q: What record does the port of Shanghai hold?
a: Largest container port in the world
52960.e: Since 2010 more containers have been handled in the port of Shanghai than in any other port in the world.
52960.m: Shanghai has the largest container port in the world.

52961.q: Which special train has connected Pudong Airport with the city of Shanghai since 2004?
52961.e: The line uses German Transrapid technology. The train floats above the track on magnetic fields.
52961.m: In Shanghai a maglev train runs to the airport.

52962.q: What shapes the look of the Pudong district in Shanghai?
52962.e: About 40 years ago Pudong was almost undeveloped. Today some of the tallest buildings in the world stand there.

52963.q: Which big international exhibition took place in Shanghai in 2010?
52963.e: Expo 2010 in Shanghai had about 73 million visitors. Switzerland was also there with its own pavilion.
52963.m: Shanghai hosted the World Expo in 2010.

52964.q: In which year did Great Britain hand Hong Kong back to China?
52964.e: On 1 July 1997 British colonial rule ended and Hong Kong became part of the People’s Republic of China. Both countries had signed the agreement in 1984.
52964.m: Hong Kong has been part of China again since 1997.

52965.q: Under which principle has Hong Kong been governed since it was returned to China?
52965.e: Hong Kong is a special administrative region with its own currency, its own laws and its own border controls. This principle was agreed for 50 years.
52965.m: Hong Kong follows the principle of one country, two systems.

52966.q: Which currency do people pay with in Hong Kong?
52966.e: As a special administrative region, Hong Kong has its own currency, the Hong Kong dollar. It is closely tied to the US dollar.
52966.m: In Hong Kong people pay with the Hong Kong dollar.

52967.q: What is Hong Kong especially known for?
a: Very many skyscrapers in a small space
52967.e: More than seven million people live in a small area in Hong Kong. That is why there are especially many high-rise buildings, for example on the Kowloon peninsula.
52967.m: Hong Kong has very many skyscrapers.

52969.q: Which Chinese language do most people in Hong Kong speak in everyday life?
52969.e: In Hong Kong and Guangdong province, Cantonese is the everyday language. The official languages are Chinese and English.
52969.m: In Hong Kong people mostly speak Cantonese in everyday life.

52970.q: Which city has been linked to Hong Kong and Zhuhai since 2018 by a bridge and tunnel connection about 55 km long?
52970.e: The Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge crosses the mouth of the Pearl River. Part of it runs through a tunnel under the sea so that ships can pass.
52970.m: A long sea bridge connects Hong Kong with Macau and Zhuhai.

52971.q: What is the capital of Taiwan?
52971.e: Taipei lies in the north of the island and is the seat of government. Kaohsiung in the south is the most important port city.
52971.m: The capital of Taiwan is Taipei.

52972.q: Which building in Taiwan was the tallest in the world from 2004 to 2010?
52972.e: The skyscraper Taipei 101 is 508 metres tall and has 101 floors above ground. In 2010 it was overtaken by the Burj Khalifa in Dubai.
52972.m: Taipei 101 was the tallest building in the world from 2004 to 2010.

52973.q: What is the strait between Taiwan and mainland China called?
52973.e: At its narrowest point the Taiwan Strait is about 130 kilometres wide. It connects the East China Sea with the South China Sea.
52973.m: The Taiwan Strait separates Taiwan from the mainland.

52974.q: Under which name was Taiwan once known in Europe?
52974.e: Portuguese sailors called the island “Ilha Formosa”, which means “beautiful island”. The name was used on European maps for a long time.
52974.m: Taiwan used to be called Formosa, the beautiful island.

52976.q: Taiwan is especially important worldwide for making which products?
52976.e: Taiwanese companies make a large share of the world’s most advanced semiconductor chips. They are found in mobile phones, computers and cars.
52976.m: Taiwan is an important maker of computer chips.

52977.q: Roughly what does Japan’s name for itself, “Nihon” or “Nippon”, mean?
52977.e: The characters mean “sun” and “origin”. That is why Japan is also called the “Land of the Rising Sun”.
52977.m: Nippon means origin of the sun.

52978.q: Roughly how many people lived in Japan in 2024?
52978.e: Japan had about 124 million inhabitants in 2024. The population has been falling for many years because few children are born.
52978.m: Japan has about 124 million inhabitants and is shrinking.

52979.q: What stands in the Tōdai-ji temple in the Japanese city of Nara?
a: A huge bronze statue of Buddha
52979.e: In the 8th century Nara was the capital of Japan. The Great Buddha in Tōdai-ji is one of the largest bronze statues in the world.
52979.m: The Great Buddha stands in Tōdai-ji in Nara.

52980.q: Why are there so many earthquakes and volcanoes in Japan?
a: It lies on the Pacific Ring of Fire
It lies in the middle of a plate
52980.e: Several tectonic plates meet under Japan. The Pacific Ring of Fire is the belt with the most volcanoes and earthquakes in the world.
52980.m: Japan lies on the Pacific Ring of Fire.

52981.q: Which nuclear power station was badly damaged by an earthquake and a tsunami in 2011?
52981.e: On 11 March 2011 a strong undersea earthquake and a tsunami caused a nuclear disaster at the Fukushima Daiichi power station. Afterwards Switzerland also decided to phase out nuclear energy step by step.
52981.m: In 2011 the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear power station was badly damaged.

52982.q: What title does Japan’s head of state have?
52982.e: Japan is a constitutional monarchy with an emperor, the Tennō. His duties are mainly ceremonial; the country is governed by parliament and the prime minister.
52982.m: Japan’s head of state is the Tennō.

52983.q: What is mainly traded at the huge Toyosu wholesale market in Tokyo?
52983.e: In 2018 the famous Tsukiji fish market moved to the new Toyosu wholesale market. Fresh fish, such as tuna, is auctioned there every morning.
52983.m: Tokyo has one of the largest fish markets in the world.

52984.q: Which religion does Sensō-ji, the oldest temple in Tokyo, belong to?
52984.e: Sensō-ji is a Buddhist temple in the Asakusa district. In Japan, Buddhism and Shinto are the most important religions.
52984.m: Sensō-ji in Tokyo is a Buddhist temple.

52985.q: What is Shinjuku station in Tokyo known for?
a: It is the busiest station in the world
It is the oldest station in the world
52985.e: Every day millions of people get on, off and change trains at Shinjuku station. Guinness World Records lists it as the busiest station in the world.
52985.m: Shinjuku is the busiest station in the world.

52986.q: Which city was the seat of the Japanese emperor for over 1000 years before he moved to Tokyo?
52986.e: Kyōto was the emperors’ residence from 794 to 1868. With the Meiji era, the emperor moved to Tokyo.
52986.m: Before Tokyo, the Japanese emperor lived in Kyōto.

52988.q: What does the syllable “san” in the Japanese name “Fuji-san” mean?
52988.e: The character 山 is read “san” here and means mountain. So it is not the polite “san” used when talking to people.

52989.q: How do most people get to the summit of Mount Fuji?
a: By car all the way to the top
52989.e: Buses and cars only go up to about halfway, to the fifth station. From there most people climb to the summit on foot.
52989.m: You reach the summit of Mount Fuji on foot.

52990.q: In which months is Mount Fuji mainly climbed?
52990.e: In July and August the mountain huts are open and there is hardly any snow on the summit. From October to May people are advised not to climb it.
52990.m: Mount Fuji is mainly climbed in July and August.

52991.q: Which big city lies about 100 kilometres from Mount Fuji?
52991.e: Mount Fuji lies about 100 kilometres south-west of Tokyo. In clear weather you can even see it from the capital.
52991.m: Mount Fuji can be seen from Tokyo.

52992.q: Why is Mount Fuji especially important to many people in Japan?
a: It is seen as a holy mountain and a symbol of Japan
It is the highest mountain in the world
The imperial palace stands on it
52992.e: Mount Fuji is a holy place and has inspired many artists. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2013.
52992.m: Mount Fuji is a holy mountain and a symbol of Japan.

52993.q: Which Japanese artist created the famous series of pictures “Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji”?
52993.e: Katsushika Hokusai made the woodblock prints around 1830. The best-known picture from the series is “The Great Wave off Kanagawa”.
52993.m: Hokusai created the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji.

52994.q: Which is the largest of Japan’s main islands?
52994.e: Honshū is the largest island in Japan. Most Japanese people live there, and Tokyo, Osaka and Kyōto are there too.
52994.m: Honshū is the largest island in Japan.

52995.q: Which of Japan’s main islands lies furthest north?
52995.e: Hokkaidō has cold, snowy winters. Its largest city is Sapporo, where the 1972 Winter Olympics took place.
52995.m: Hokkaidō is Japan’s northernmost main island.

52996.q: Which is the smallest of Japan’s four main islands?
52996.e: Shikoku lies south of Honshū. It is known for a pilgrimage route with 88 temples.
52996.m: Shikoku is Japan’s smallest main island.

52997.q: Which of Japan’s main islands lies furthest south-west?
52997.e: Kyūshū is closest to Korea and China. The island has cities such as Fukuoka and Nagasaki and several active volcanoes.
52997.m: Kyūshū is Japan’s south-westernmost main island.

52998.q: What is the railway tunnel under the sea that connects the islands of Honshū and Hokkaidō called?
52998.e: The Seikan Tunnel is about 54 kilometres long and opened in 1988. A large part of it lies under the seabed of the Tsugaru Strait.
52998.m: The Seikan Tunnel connects Honshū and Hokkaidō under the sea.

52999.q: What is the climate like on the island of Okinawa in southern Japan?
52999.e: Okinawa is one of the Ryūkyū Islands, which stretch almost to Taiwan. It is warm there all year.

53000.q: Which is the second largest city and most important port city in South Korea?
53000.e: Busan lies on the south-east coast of South Korea and has about 3.3 million inhabitants. Its port is one of the largest container ports in the world.
53000.m: Busan is the second largest city in South Korea.

53001.q: Along which line of latitude was Korea divided into a northern and a southern part in 1945?
53001.e: After the Second World War the USA and the Soviet Union divided Korea at the 38th parallel. Two states emerged from this in 1948.
53001.m: Korea was divided at the 38th parallel.

53002.q: With which country did South Korea jointly host the Football World Cup in 2002?
53002.e: The 2002 World Cup was the first in Asia and the first with two host countries. South Korea even reached the semi-final.
53002.m: South Korea and Japan jointly hosted the 2002 Football World Cup.

53003.q: What is Hallasan, South Korea’s highest mountain?
53003.e: Hallasan is a volcano on the island of Jeju and almost 1950 metres high. Jeju lies in the south of South Korea and is a popular holiday destination.
53003.m: South Korea’s highest mountain is a volcano.

53004.q: Seoul is the capital of which country?
53004.e: Seoul is the capital of South Korea. The capital of North Korea is Pyongyang.
53004.m: Seoul is the capital of South Korea.

53005.q: Which big sporting event took place in Seoul in 1988?
53005.e: Seoul hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 1988. They were only the second Summer Games in Asia, after Tokyo in 1964.
53005.m: Seoul hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 1988.

53006.q: What is the largest royal palace in Seoul called?
53006.e: Gyeongbokgung was built in 1395 for the kings of the Joseon dynasty. Today it is one of the best-known sights in Seoul.
53006.m: Gyeongbokgung is the largest palace in Seoul.

53007.q: Roughly what share of South Korea’s population lives in the Seoul metropolitan area?
53007.e: About 26 million of South Korea’s roughly 51 million people live in the Seoul metropolitan area, including the city of Incheon and Gyeonggi province (as of 2023).
53007.m: About half of South Koreans live in the Seoul metropolitan area.

53008.q: What is the strip of land about 4 km wide along the border between North and South Korea called?
53008.e: No troops may be stationed in the Demilitarised Zone. It is about 250 kilometres long and is one of the most heavily guarded borders in the world.
53008.m: North and South Korea are separated by the Demilitarised Zone.

53009.q: How did the fighting in the Korean War end in 1953?
53009.e: The Korean War lasted from 1950 to 1953. Only a ceasefire was signed; there is still no peace treaty today.
53009.m: The Korean War ended in 1953 with only a ceasefire.

53010.q: Which neutral country has had officers on the supervisory commission at the inter-Korean border since 1953?
53010.e: Together with Sweden, Switzerland is a member of the Neutral Nations Supervisory Commission in Panmunjom. It checks that the ceasefire is kept.
53010.m: Swiss officers have served at the border in Korea since 1953.

53011.q: Which large country borders North Korea to the north?
53011.e: To the north, North Korea shares a long border with China. The Yalu and Tumen rivers form this border. In the far north-east there is also a short border with Russia.
53011.m: To the north, North Korea borders China.

53012.q: Which two countries does Mongolia border?
53012.e: Mongolia is squeezed between Russia to the north and China to the south. It has no access to the sea.
53012.m: Mongolia borders only Russia and China.

53013.q: Which grandson of Genghis Khan founded the Yuan dynasty in China?
53013.e: Kublai Khan conquered China and founded the Yuan dynasty in 1271. He made present-day Beijing his capital.
53013.m: Kublai Khan founded the Yuan dynasty in China.

53014.q: What is the round felt tent that many Mongolian nomads live in called?
53014.e: A yurt consists of a wooden frame covered with felt. It can be taken down in a few hours and carried along.

53015.q: Which script is the Mongolian language mostly written in today?
53015.e: Under the influence of the Soviet Union, Cyrillic script was introduced in Mongolia from the 1940s. Today more people are learning the old Mongolian script again.
53015.m: Mongolian is mostly written in Cyrillic letters today.

53016.q: What record does Mongolia hold among the independent countries of the world?
53016.e: In Mongolia, on average only about two people live on each square kilometre. In Switzerland it is more than 200.
53016.m: Mongolia is the most thinly populated country in the world.

53017.q: Which animal with two humps still lives wild in the Gobi Desert?
53017.e: The wild camel is closely related to the tame Bactrian camel and, like it, has two humps. It is very rare and critically endangered.
53017.m: Wild camels with two humps still live in the Gobi.

53018.q: Roughly how many Gobi bears still live in the wild?
53018.e: The Gobi bear, Mazaalai in Mongolian, is a form of brown bear. Only about 30 to 50 animals still live in the wild, and it is threatened with extinction.
53018.m: The Gobi bear is one of the rarest bears in the world.

53019.q: Roughly what does the Mongolian word that the name “Gobi” comes from mean?
53019.e: The Mongols called the area “Govi”, which means something like waterless place. Today experts also use “gobi” generally for a desert of rubble and gravel.
53019.m: Gobi means something like waterless place.

53020.q: Which big cat with thick grey fur lives in the mountains of the Gobi?
53020.e: The snow leopard lives in cold, rocky mountains of Central Asia, including the Mongolian Gobi. Its thick fur and long tail protect it from the cold.
53020.m: The snow leopard lives in the mountains of the Gobi.

53021.q: Which city is the capital of India?
53021.e: New Delhi is the capital of India and the seat of government. Mumbai is the country’s biggest business city.
53021.m: New Delhi is the capital of India.

53022.q: Which animal do many people in India regard as sacred?
53022.e: In Hinduism the cow is considered sacred. That is why cows walk freely on the streets in many Indian cities.
53022.m: In India the cow is sacred to many people.

53023.q: Which desert lies in north-western India on the border with Pakistan?
53023.e: The Thar Desert lies mainly in the Indian state of Rajasthan and reaches into Pakistan. It is also called the Great Indian Desert.
53023.m: The Thar Desert lies in north-western India.

53024.q: Which sea lies west of the Indian peninsula?
53024.e: West of India lies the Arabian Sea, east of it the Bay of Bengal. Both are part of the Indian Ocean.
53024.m: West of India lies the Arabian Sea, east of it the Bay of Bengal.

53025.q: What is shown in the middle of the Indian flag?
53025.e: In the middle of the saffron, white and green flag is the blue Ashoka Chakra. This wheel has 24 spokes.
53025.m: India’s flag shows a blue wheel with 24 spokes.

53026.q: Which high mountain range lies in the north of India?
53026.e: The Himalayas rise in the north of India. India’s highest mountain, Kangchenjunga, is there too.
53026.m: The Himalayas lie in the north of India.

53027.q: Which world-famous tomb stands in Agra, not far from New Delhi?
53027.e: The white marble Taj Mahal lies about 200 kilometres south of Delhi. A Mughal emperor had it built for his late wife.
53027.m: The Taj Mahal stands in Agra, not far from Delhi.

53028.q: Who lives today in the former palace of the British viceroy in New Delhi?
53028.e: The huge building is now called Rashtrapati Bhavan. It was finished in 1929, and the President of India has lived there since 1950.
53028.m: India’s president now lives in the former viceroy’s palace.

53029.q: Which large archway monument in New Delhi remembers fallen Indian soldiers?
53029.e: India Gate is a war memorial to Indian soldiers who died in the First World War. It stands on New Delhi’s grand avenue.
53029.m: India Gate in New Delhi remembers fallen soldiers.

53030.q: Who had the Red Fort in Delhi built?
53030.e: The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan had the Red Fort built of red sandstone. He also had the Taj Mahal built.
53030.m: The Red Fort in Delhi was a palace of the Mughal emperors.

53031.q: What was Mumbai’s official name in the past?
53031.e: The city was officially renamed from Bombay to Mumbai in 1995. Madras is now called Chennai.
53031.m: Mumbai used to be called Bombay.

53032.q: What is Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus in Mumbai?
53032.e: The station was completed in 1888 and used to be called Victoria Terminus. Because of its magnificent architecture, it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2004.
53032.m: Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus in Mumbai is a World Heritage railway station.

53033.q: What is the big film industry with its centre in Mumbai called?
53033.e: The name Bollywood combines Bombay, the old name of Mumbai, and Hollywood. A great many films are made in Mumbai every year.
53033.m: Bollywood films are made in Mumbai.

53034.q: Which large archway stands at the harbour in Mumbai?
53034.e: The Gateway of India was built to mark the visit of the British King George V and was finished in 1924. It stands right by the water.
53034.m: The Gateway of India stands at Mumbai’s harbour.

53035.q: What do the dabbawalas in Mumbai do?
53035.e: The dabbawalas collect hot meals in metal tins from people’s homes and take them to offices by train and bike. Their delivery system is famous because it is so reliable.
53035.m: In Mumbai the dabbawalas deliver lunch to offices.

53036.q: Which big cat lives in the mangrove forests at the mouth of the Ganges?
53036.e: The Sundarbans, one of the largest mangrove areas in the world, lie in the Ganges delta. The Bengal tiger lives there and can even swim well.
53036.m: The Bengal tiger lives in the mangroves of the Ganges delta.

53037.q: Which mammal lives in the water of the Ganges and is almost blind?
53037.e: The Ganges river dolphin lives in murky river water and can hardly see. It finds its way using echolocation.
53037.m: The Ganges river dolphin finds its way in murky water using echolocation.

53038.q: Why do millions of Hindus bathe in the Ganges every year?
a: They see it as a holy river
It is the cleanest river in India
There are no beaches by the sea
53038.e: For Hindus the Ganges is holy. At big pilgrimage festivals such as the Kumbh Mela, millions of people bathe in the river.
53038.m: For Hindus the Ganges is a holy river.

53039.q: Through which country does most of the Indus flow?
53039.e: The Indus rises in Tibet, flows briefly through India and then through the whole of Pakistan. It is Pakistan’s longest river.
53039.m: The Indus is Pakistan’s most important river.

53040.q: Into which sea does the Indus flow?
53040.e: The Indus flows into the Arabian Sea near Karachi. There it forms a large delta.
53040.m: The Indus flows into the Arabian Sea.

53041.q: Which early civilisation arose on the Indus about 4500 years ago?
53041.e: The Harappan or Indus civilisation had large, planned cities such as Harappa and Mohenjo-daro. It is one of the oldest civilisations in the world.
53041.m: The Harappan civilisation flourished on the Indus about 4500 years ago.

53042.q: Which ancient city of the Indus civilisation already had sewers and a great bath?
53042.e: Mohenjo-daro lies in present-day Pakistan. The city had straight streets, sewers and a large public bath.
53042.m: Mohenjo-daro was a well-planned city on the Indus.

53043.q: Which country takes its name from the Indus River?
53043.e: The Greeks called the land on the Indus River “India”. So the name of the river became the name of the whole country.
53043.m: India takes its name from the Indus River.

53044.q: What does the name of the Punjab region, through which tributaries of the Indus flow, mean?
53044.e: Punjab means “five waters” or “five rivers”. This refers to five tributaries of the Indus.
53044.m: Punjab means land of the five rivers.

53045.q: In which highland does the Brahmaputra rise?
53045.e: The Brahmaputra rises on the Tibetan Plateau north of the Himalayas. There it is called the Yarlung Tsangpo.

53046.q: Through which Indian state does the Brahmaputra flow in a wide valley?
53046.e: The Brahmaputra flows through Assam in north-east India. Assam is known for its tea.
53046.m: The Brahmaputra flows through Assam, the land of tea.

53047.q: After India, which country does the Brahmaputra flow into?
53047.e: After India the Brahmaputra flows into Bangladesh, where it is called the Jamuna. There it joins the Ganges.
53047.m: The Brahmaputra flows from India into Bangladesh.

53048.q: What often happens to the Brahmaputra during the monsoon?
53048.e: During the monsoon there is very heavy rain and the snow in the Himalayas melts. The Brahmaputra then carries so much water that it often floods large areas.
53048.m: During the monsoon the Brahmaputra often floods.

53049.q: Which one-horned animal lives in Kaziranga National Park on the Brahmaputra?
53049.e: Kaziranga National Park has the largest population of Indian rhinos in the world. The Indian rhino has only one horn.
53049.m: Many Indian rhinos live in Kaziranga park.

53050.q: Which mountain range does the Brahmaputra cut through in one of the deepest gorges in the world?
53050.e: At the eastern end of the Himalayas, the river has carved an enormous gorge. It is seen as one of the deepest gorges on Earth.
53050.m: The Brahmaputra cuts a deep gorge through the Himalayas.

53051.q: In which part of India does the summer monsoon usually begin first?
a: In the north in the Himalayas
In the desert in the north-west
53051.e: The monsoon comes with moist air from the Indian Ocean. It first reaches the state of Kerala at the south-western tip of India, usually around 1 June.
53051.m: The monsoon reaches India first in the south-west.

53052.q: Why is the summer monsoon so important for farmers in India?
a: It brings water for the fields
53052.e: A large part of the year’s rain falls during the monsoon. Without it, rice and other crops grow badly. If it comes too late, the harvest may fail.
53052.m: Monsoon rain is vital for India’s farming.

53053.q: Where in India is the Deccan Plateau?
a: In the south of the peninsula
In the north-west by the desert
53053.e: The Deccan Plateau covers a large part of the southern Indian peninsula. The name comes from the Sanskrit word for “south”.
53053.m: The Deccan is the plateau in southern India.

53054.q: Which mountain ranges border the Deccan Plateau to the west and east?
53054.e: To the west rise the Western Ghats, to the east the lower Eastern Ghats. The plateau lies in between.
53054.m: The Western and Eastern Ghats frame the Deccan.

53055.q: What rock are the Deccan Traps in the north-west of the plateau made of?
53055.e: The Deccan Traps are huge sheets of basalt lava. They formed about 66 million years ago through enormous volcanic eruptions.
53055.m: The Deccan Traps are made of solidified lava, that is basalt.

53056.q: In which direction do most of the big rivers of the Deccan, such as the Godavari and Krishna, flow?
53056.e: The plateau slopes towards the east because the Western Ghats are higher. That is why the Godavari and Krishna flow into the Bay of Bengal.
53056.m: The rivers of the Deccan flow east to the Bay of Bengal.

53057.q: Which city on the Deccan is known as the centre of India’s IT industry?
53057.e: Bangalore (Bengaluru) is often called the “Silicon Valley of India”. Many software companies are based there.
53057.m: Bangalore is India’s centre for computing.

53058.q: Which fertile dark soil on the Deccan is especially good for cotton?
53058.e: The dark regur soil formed from weathered basalt. It holds water well and is good for growing cotton.
53058.m: Good cotton grows on dark regur soil.

53059.q: What is the capital of Pakistan?
53059.e: Islamabad was planned and built as a new capital in the 1960s. Karachi is the largest city, but not the capital.

53060.q: Which is the largest city in Pakistan?
53060.e: Karachi lies on the Arabian Sea and is the country’s most important port and business city. It was also the capital until 1959.
53060.m: Karachi is the largest city in Pakistan.

53061.q: Apart from English, which language is an official language in Pakistan?
53061.e: Urdu is Pakistan’s national language. Many people also speak Punjabi or other languages in everyday life.
53061.m: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan.

53062.q: Which famous mountain pass connects Pakistan with Afghanistan?
53062.e: The Khyber Pass was an important route for trade and armies centuries ago. It connects the area around Peshawar with Afghanistan.
53062.m: The Khyber Pass leads from Pakistan to Afghanistan.

53063.q: Which mountain, the second highest in the world, lies on the border between Pakistan and China?
53063.e: K2 is 8611 metres high and lies in the Karakoram. Only Mount Everest is higher.
53063.m: K2 in northern Pakistan is the second highest mountain in the world.

53064.q: From which territory was Pakistan created in 1947?
53064.e: When British rule in India ended in 1947, the territory was divided. This created India and Pakistan.
53064.m: Pakistan was created from British India in 1947.

53065.q: Which large country almost completely surrounds Bangladesh?
53065.e: Bangladesh is almost entirely surrounded by India to the west, north and east. To the south lies the sea, and to the south-east it borders Myanmar.
53065.m: Bangladesh is almost entirely surrounded by India.

53066.q: Which language is mainly spoken in Bangladesh?
53066.e: Bengali (Bangla) is the national language. The name Bangladesh means “land of the Bengalis”.

53067.q: In which big river delta does Bangladesh lie?
a: In the delta of the Ganges and Brahmaputra
53067.e: Large parts of Bangladesh lie in the delta of the Ganges and Brahmaputra. The country is flat and often flooded.
53067.m: Bangladesh lies in the huge delta of the Ganges and Brahmaputra.

53068.q: Which plant fibre was long Bangladesh’s most important export?
53068.e: Jute grows well in the humid delta and is made into sacks and ropes. It is also called the “golden fibre”.
53068.m: A lot of jute for sacks and ropes comes from Bangladesh.

53069.q: What was Sri Lanka called until 1972?
53069.e: Under British rule the island was called Ceylon. In 1972 the country took the name Sri Lanka.
53069.m: Sri Lanka used to be called Ceylon.

53070.q: Which drink is Sri Lanka world-famous for?
53070.e: Sri Lanka is one of the biggest tea producers in the world. The tea is still sold as Ceylon tea today.
53070.m: Sri Lanka is famous for Ceylon tea.

53071.q: Which large country lies north of Sri Lanka, separated only by a narrow strait?
53071.e: The Palk Strait lies between southern India and Sri Lanka. At its narrowest point it is only about 50 kilometres wide.
53071.m: Sri Lanka lies just south of India.

53072.q: Which is the largest city in Sri Lanka?
53072.e: Colombo is the largest city and the business centre. The official capital is neighbouring Sri Jayewardenepura Kotte.
53072.m: Colombo is the largest city in Sri Lanka.

53073.q: Which religion has the most followers in Sri Lanka?
53073.e: About two thirds of the people in Sri Lanka are Buddhists. There are also Hindus, Muslims and Christians.
53073.m: Most people in Sri Lanka are Buddhists.

53074.q: Which rock fortress with wall paintings stands on a rock about 180 metres high in Sri Lanka?
53074.e: Sigiriya, the “Lion Rock”, was used as a palace by King Kashyapa in the 5th century. Today the rock is a World Heritage Site and attracts many visitors.
53074.m: Sigiriya is a rock fortress in Sri Lanka.

53075.q: Which decorated animals parade through the streets at the big temple festival in Kandy?
53075.e: At the Esala Perahera festival, dozens of decorated elephants parade through Kandy every year. It honours the Tooth of the Buddha, which is kept in the Temple of the Tooth.
53075.m: Decorated elephants parade through Kandy at the temple festival.

53076.q: In which mountain range are Nepal’s eight-thousanders?
53076.e: The highest mountains in the world are in the Himalayas. Eight of the fourteen eight-thousanders lie wholly or partly in Nepal, including Mount Everest.
53076.m: Nepal’s eight-thousanders are in the Himalayas.

53077.q: What did two Swiss mountaineers achieve in 1956 on Lhotse, the fourth highest mountain on Earth?
a: The first flight over the summit
53077.e: On 18 May 1956 Ernst Reiss and Fritz Luchsinger became the first people to reach the summit of Lhotse in Nepal.
53077.m: Two Swiss climbers were the first on top of Lhotse in 1956.

53078.q: What form of state has Nepal had since 2008?
53078.e: In 2008 the monarchy in Nepal was abolished. Since then Nepal has been a republic, and a federal republic since the 2015 constitution.
53078.m: Nepal has been a republic since 2008.

53079.q: In which country is Kathmandu, with its famous “Monkey Temple”?
53079.e: Kathmandu is the capital of Nepal. Many monkeys live at the Swayambhunath temple on a hill above the city, which is why it is also called the Monkey Temple.
53079.m: Kathmandu is the capital of Nepal.

53080.q: What is the Kumari in Kathmandu?
a: A girl who is worshipped as a living goddess
53080.e: The Kumari is a girl who is seen as the embodiment of a goddess until she grows up. She lives in her own temple house in the old town.
53080.m: In Kathmandu a girl is worshipped as the living goddess Kumari.

53081.q: What is painted on the dome of the great Boudhanath stupa in Kathmandu?
53081.e: The Boudhanath stupa is an important centre of Tibetan Buddhism. The eyes of the Buddha are painted on all four sides of its tower.
53081.m: The Boudhanath stupa has the painted eyes of the Buddha.

53082.q: What is the capital of Bhutan?
53082.e: Thimphu is the capital and largest city of Bhutan. The international airport, however, is in nearby Paro.

53083.q: Instead of only economic output, what does Bhutan measure as the goal of its policies?
53083.e: With Gross National Happiness, Bhutan also measures well-being, culture and the environment. The idea comes from the fourth king, Jigme Singye Wangchuck.
53083.m: Bhutan measures the happiness of its people.

53084.q: Which famous monastery in Bhutan clings to a steep cliff?
53084.e: The Taktsang monastery, the “Tiger’s Nest”, lies high above the Paro valley. It is one of Bhutan’s best-known landmarks.
53084.m: The Tiger’s Nest monastery hangs on a cliff in Bhutan.

53085.q: Between which two large countries does Bhutan lie?
53085.e: Bhutan borders China (Tibet) to the north and India everywhere else. The country has no access to the sea.
53085.m: Bhutan lies between India and China.

53086.q: What form of state does Bhutan have?
53086.e: Bhutan is ruled by a king whose power has been limited by a constitution since 2008. There is an elected parliament.
53086.m: Bhutan is a kingdom with a constitution.

53087.q: Which part of the economy is most important for the Maldives?
53087.e: Many tourists visit the Maldives for the beaches and coral reefs. Fishing is also important.
53087.m: The Maldives live mainly from tourism.

53088.q: Switzerland is divided into cantons. What are the large areas that India is divided into called?
53088.e: India is a federal country with 28 states. There are also 8 union territories, which are run directly by the central government.

53089.q: Which country ruled India when New Delhi was built as the new capital?
53089.e: From 1911 New Delhi was planned by the British as the capital of their colony of India. The architect Edwin Lutyens designed wide avenues and large government buildings.
53089.m: New Delhi was built by the British as a capital.

53090.q: What is special about the Lotus Temple in New Delhi?
a: It is shaped like a flower
It is made entirely of gold
It is the tallest building in India
53090.e: The Lotus Temple consists of 27 petals covered in marble. This house of worship of the Bahá’í faith is open to people of all religions.
53090.m: The Lotus Temple in New Delhi looks like a lotus flower.

53091.q: What can you find on Elephanta Island off Mumbai?
a: Cave temples carved into the rock
53091.e: The caves on Elephanta Island contain large sculptures of the god Shiva. They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and can be reached by boat.
53091.m: There are cave temples on Elephanta Island.

53092.q: Through which two countries does the Ganges mainly flow?
53092.e: The Ganges flows through northern India and then through Bangladesh, where it is called the Padma. There it flows into the Bay of Bengal.
53092.m: The Ganges flows through India and Bangladesh.

53093.q: Roughly how long is the Ganges?
53093.e: The Ganges is about 2500 kilometres long. That makes it about twice as long as the Rhine.
53093.m: The Ganges is about 2500 kilometres long.

53095.q: Which big Indian city lies on one of the mouth branches of the Ganges?
53095.e: Kolkata (Calcutta) lies on the Hooghly, a branch of the Ganges in the state of West Bengal. Mumbai and Chennai lie on other coasts, Bangalore inland.
53095.m: Kolkata lies on a branch of the Ganges.

53096.q: Why does the summer monsoon happen in South Asia?
a: Because the land heats up more than the sea
Because the sea heats up more than the land
Because volcanoes give off warm air
Because the moon pulls the air
53096.e: In summer the land gets hotter than the ocean, and warm air rises over the land. Moist sea air flows in to replace it and brings rain.
53096.m: The hot land draws in moist sea air.

53097.q: What is the dry wind that blows over India in winter called?
53097.e: In winter the land cools down more than the sea, so the wind blows from the land to the sea. This north-east monsoon brings little rain to most areas.
53097.m: In winter the dry north-east monsoon blows.

53098.q: In which season does the monsoon bring especially heavy rain to India?
53098.e: The summer monsoon brings moist air from the sea from about June to September. Then it rains very heavily in large parts of India.
53098.m: The summer monsoon brings India a lot of rain.

53099.q: Which mountain range stops the monsoon clouds in the north of India?
53099.e: The high mountains of the Himalayas form a barrier. The clouds rain out on the southern side, while to the north, in Tibet, it is dry.
53099.m: The Himalayas hold back the monsoon clouds.

53100.q: Which city is the second largest in Pakistan and lies near the border with India?
53100.e: Lahore is the capital of Punjab province. The city is known for its buildings from the Mughal period.
53100.m: Lahore is the second largest city in Pakistan.

53101.q: Which sea does Bangladesh border to the south?
53101.e: The Bay of Bengal is part of the Indian Ocean. The very long sandy beach of Cox’s Bazar is there too.
53101.m: Bangladesh lies on the Bay of Bengal.

53102.q: Which goods make up most of Bangladesh’s exports today?
53102.e: Bangladesh is one of the biggest clothing exporters in the world. Millions of people work in its textile factories.

53103.q: What did a Swiss expedition achieve on Dhaulagiri in Nepal in 1960?
a: The building of a cable car
53103.e: In May 1960 the Swiss expedition led by Max Eiselin was the first to reach the summit of Dhaulagiri, which is about 8167 metres high.
53103.m: A Swiss expedition made the first ascent of Dhaulagiri in 1960.

53104.q: What is the Swiss Toni Hagen known for in Nepal?
a: He explored the country on foot
He was the first to climb Everest
He founded the city of Kathmandu
He was the pilot of the first airline
53104.e: In the 1950s the geologist Toni Hagen covered about 14,000 kilometres on foot in Nepal and explored the country. Later he worked for development aid.
53104.m: The Swiss Toni Hagen explored Nepal on foot.

53106.q: In which year did a severe earthquake in Nepal destroy many houses and temples?
53106.e: On 25 April 2015 there was a very strong earthquake in Nepal. Thousands of people died, and many old buildings in the Kathmandu Valley were damaged.
53106.m: In 2015 Nepal was hit by a severe earthquake.

53107.q: What used to stand on the Durbar Squares in the old cities around Kathmandu?
53107.e: Durbar means “court” or “palace”. Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur each have a Durbar Square with palaces and temples.
53107.m: The royal palaces stood on the Durbar Squares.

53108.q: Which religion does the great Pashupatinath temple in Kathmandu belong to?
53108.e: Pashupatinath is the most important temple of the god Shiva in Nepal. On the bank of the Bagmati River there, the dead are cremated.
53108.m: Pashupatinath is Kathmandu’s great Hindu temple.

53109.q: In which mountain range does Bhutan lie?
53109.e: Bhutan lies in the eastern Himalayas. In the north, mountains rise more than 7000 metres high.
53109.m: Bhutan is a mountain country in the Himalayas.

53110.q: What does Bhutan even protect in its constitution?
53110.e: Bhutan’s constitution requires at least 60 per cent of the land to remain forested. Today even more of the land is covered with forest.
53110.m: Bhutan protects its forest in its constitution.

53111.q: Which religion is the state religion of the Maldives?
53111.e: The Maldives have been Muslim since the 12th century. Islam is the state religion.
53111.m: Islam is the state religion of the Maldives.

53114.q: Under the protection of which European country were the Maldives until 1965?
53114.e: The Maldives were a British protectorate for a long time. In 1965 they became fully independent.
53114.m: The Maldives were under British protection until 1965.

53115.q: Why was an artificial island of sand built up near the capital, Malé?
a: Because there is too little room to live in Malé
Because people want to drill for oil there
Because a ski resort is being built there
Because people want to watch volcanoes there
53115.e: A great many people live on the small capital island. The artificial island of Hulhumalé creates new living space and also lies a little higher.
53115.m: An island was built up near Malé for new homes.

53116.q: Where was the emperor who had the Taj Mahal built buried after his death?
a: In the Taj Mahal next to his wife
In the Red Fort in Delhi
53116.e: The emperor died in 1666 and was buried in the Taj Mahal next to his favourite wife. The legend of a second, black Taj Mahal for him is not proven.
53116.m: The builder of the Taj Mahal is buried in it himself.

53117.q: Which empire did the ruler who had the Taj Mahal built belong to?
53117.e: The Mughal emperors ruled large parts of India from the 16th to the 19th century. Their buildings combine Persian, Islamic and Indian elements.
53117.m: The Taj Mahal is a building from the Mughal Empire.

53118.q: On which list of places especially worth protecting is the Taj Mahal?
a: List of the largest railway stations
53118.e: UNESCO added the Taj Mahal to the World Heritage list in 1983. It is seen as a masterpiece of Mughal architecture.
53118.m: The Taj Mahal is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

53119.q: Why do the minarets of the Taj Mahal lean slightly outwards?
a: So that they would not fall onto the tomb if they collapsed
So that the wind can pass through better
Because the ground under them has sunk
So that they look bigger from far away
53119.e: The builders deliberately tilted the towers slightly outwards. If they fell, for example in an earthquake, they would fall away from the main building.
53119.m: The minarets lean outwards to protect the tomb.

53120.q: How is the garden in front of the Taj Mahal laid out?
a: As a rock garden without water
53120.e: The garden is a Persian charbagh. Water channels divide it into four equal parts, which is meant to recall paradise.
53120.m: The garden of the Taj Mahal is divided into four parts.

53121.q: On which island is Jakarta, the capital of Indonesia?
53121.e: Jakarta lies on the north coast of the island of Java. More than half of Indonesia’s people live on Java.
53121.m: Jakarta is on the island of Java.

53122.q: What big problem does Jakarta have because a lot of groundwater is pumped out?
53122.e: Because so much groundwater is taken out, the ground is sinking. Parts of the city already lie below sea level and are often flooded.
53122.m: Jakarta is sinking because too much groundwater is pumped out.

53123.q: Why is Indonesia building a new capital on the island of Borneo?
a: Jakarta is overcrowded and partly sinking
Jakarta is too small and has too few people
There is no drinking water on Java
53123.e: Jakarta is very crowded, has a lot of traffic and is partly sinking. That is why Indonesia is building the new capital Nusantara on Borneo.
53123.m: Indonesia is building a new capital on Borneo.

53124.q: Which huge Buddhist temple from the 9th century stands on the island of Java?
53124.e: Borobudur is one of the largest Buddhist temple complexes in the world. It is decorated with more than 2,600 reliefs and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
53124.m: The Borobudur temple stands on Java.

53125.q: What is the currency of Indonesia called?
53125.e: In Indonesia people pay with the Indonesian rupiah. Its name is related to the word rupee, the currency of India.
53125.m: In Indonesia people pay with the rupiah.

53126.q: In which country do the most Muslims in the world live (as of 2025)?
53126.e: Indonesia is the country with the largest Muslim population in the world. The great majority of its people follow Islam.
53126.m: Indonesia has the largest Muslim population in the world.

53127.q: Which Indonesian island is the most populous island in the world?
53127.e: More than 150 million people live on Java (as of 2020), more than on any other island on Earth.
53127.m: Java is the most populous island in the world.

53128.q: On which Indonesian island are most people Hindus?
53128.e: Bali is the only island in Indonesia with a Hindu majority. Its temples and festivals attract many tourists.
53128.m: Most people on Bali are Hindus.

53129.q: Which is the largest island that belongs entirely to Indonesia?
53129.e: Borneo and New Guinea are bigger, but they belong only partly to Indonesia. Sumatra is the largest island that is entirely Indonesian.
53129.m: Sumatra is the largest island that is entirely Indonesian.

53130.q: Why are there so many active volcanoes in Indonesia?
a: It lies on the Pacific Ring of Fire
It lies in the middle of a continental plate
53130.e: Indonesia lies where several tectonic plates collide. This belt around the Pacific is called the Ring of Fire and has a great many volcanoes and earthquakes.
53130.m: Indonesia lies on the Pacific Ring of Fire.

53131.q: Which is the largest island of the Philippines?
53131.e: Luzon is the country’s largest and most populous island. The capital, Manila, is there too. Mindanao in the south is the second largest.
53131.m: Luzon is the largest island of the Philippines.

53132.q: Which religion is most widespread in the Philippines?
53132.e: Because of the long Spanish colonial period, the great majority of the population is Roman Catholic. The Philippines is the largest Catholic country in Asia.
53132.m: Most people in the Philippines are Catholic.

53133.q: Which country took over the Philippines from Spain as a colony in 1898?
53133.e: After the Spanish-American War of 1898, the Philippines became a colony of the USA. It only became independent in 1946.
53133.m: After Spain, the USA ruled the Philippines.

53134.q: Which volcano in the Philippines had one of the biggest eruptions of the 20th century in 1991?
53134.e: In 1991 Pinatubo on Luzon threw huge amounts of ash into the air. Afterwards the whole world was slightly cooler for a short time.

53135.q: What is special about Thailand compared with its neighbouring countries?
a: It was never a European colony
53135.e: All its neighbouring countries were ruled by Europeans. Thailand was the only country in South-East Asia that always stayed independent.
53135.m: Thailand was never a European colony.

53136.q: In which Swiss city did the Thai king Bhumibol spend his youth?
