53136.e: Bhumibol grew up partly in Switzerland and studied at the University of Lausanne. Later he became King of Thailand.
53136.m: King Bhumibol spent his youth in Lausanne.

53137.q: Which Thai island was hit by an enormous tsunami in 2004?
53137.e: On 26 December 2004, after an undersea earthquake near Sumatra, a tsunami hit many coasts around the Indian Ocean, including Phuket. People from Switzerland were also among the dead.
53137.m: The 2004 tsunami also hit Phuket in Thailand.

53138.e: The Chao Phraya flows right through Bangkok into the Gulf of Thailand. Many ferries and boats travel on it.
53138.m: Bangkok lies on the Chao Phraya River.

53139.q: Bangkok is the capital of which country?
53139.e: Bangkok is the capital and by far the largest city of Thailand. Thai people call it Krung Thep, “City of Angels”.
53139.m: Bangkok is the capital of Thailand.

53140.q: What are Bangkok and its surroundings known for, because traders sell goods from boats there?
53140.e: In the past Bangkok was criss-crossed by many canals. At floating markets traders sell fruit and food straight from their boats.

53141.q: For which product is Vietnam the second biggest producer in the world after Brazil?
53141.e: Vietnam mainly grows robusta coffee. Only Brazil produces more coffee.
53141.m: Vietnam is the second biggest coffee producer in the world.

53142.q: Which script is used for the Vietnamese language today?
53142.e: Vietnamese used to be written with Chinese characters. Today it uses Latin letters with many extra marks for the tones.
53142.m: Vietnamese is written with Latin letters.

53143.q: Which big river forms a huge delta in the south of Vietnam?
53143.e: The Mekong flows through several countries in South-East Asia and reaches the sea in Vietnam. A great deal of rice is grown in its delta.
53143.m: The Mekong Delta lies in the south of Vietnam.

53144.q: Which river is the longest river in South-East Asia?
53144.e: The Mekong is several thousand kilometres long, which makes it the longest river in South-East Asia.
53144.m: The Mekong is the longest river in South-East Asia.

53145.q: What do the Vietnamese call the Mekong because of its many mouth branches?
53145.e: In Vietnam the Mekong is called Cửu Long, which means “nine dragons”. The name refers to the many branches into which the river splits in the delta.
53145.m: The Vietnamese call the Mekong nine dragons.

53146.q: What happens to the Tonle Sap River in Cambodia during the rainy season?
53146.e: In the rainy season the Mekong carries so much water that it pushes the Tonle Sap River backwards into the Tonle Sap lake. The lake then becomes many times bigger.
53146.m: In the rainy season the Tonle Sap flows backwards.

53147.q: Which capital city lies right on the Mekong on the border with Thailand?
53147.e: Vientiane is the capital of Laos. It lies on the Mekong, which forms the border between Laos and Thailand there.

53148.q: What are the Petronas Towers in Kuala Lumpur?
53148.e: The two twin towers are 452 metres tall. From 1998 to 2004 they were the tallest buildings in the world.
53148.m: The Petronas Towers are famous twin towers.

53149.q: Kuala Lumpur is the capital of which country?
53149.e: Kuala Lumpur is the capital and largest city of Malaysia. Merdeka 118, the second tallest building in the world, also stands there.
53149.m: Kuala Lumpur is the capital of Malaysia.

53150.q: What does the name Kuala Lumpur mean in English?
53150.e: Kuala means river mouth and lumpur means mud. The city grew up where two muddy rivers flow together.
53150.m: Kuala Lumpur means muddy river mouth.

53151.q: What climate is there in Kuala Lumpur?
53151.e: Kuala Lumpur lies close to the Equator. It is hot all year, and there are heavy downpours almost every day.
53151.m: In Kuala Lumpur it is hot and humid all year.

53152.q: Which two parts does Malaysia consist of?
a: The Malay Peninsula and the north of Borneo
53152.e: West Malaysia lies on the Malay Peninsula, East Malaysia in the north of Borneo. The South China Sea lies in between.
53152.m: Malaysia lies on the peninsula and on Borneo.

53153.q: What is the currency of Malaysia called?
53153.e: In Malaysia people pay with the Malaysian ringgit. The kyat is the currency of Myanmar.
53153.m: In Malaysia people pay with the ringgit.

53154.q: How is the King of Malaysia chosen?
a: The rulers of the states elect him
The people elect him every four years
The eldest son inherits the role
53154.e: Malaysia is an elective monarchy. The rulers of nine states, mostly sultans, elect one of themselves as king every five years.
53154.m: The King of Malaysia is elected every five years.

53155.q: Malaysia is the world’s second biggest producer of which vegetable oil, after Indonesia?
53155.e: After Indonesia, Malaysia produces the most palm oil. Large areas of rainforest were turned into plantations for it.
53155.m: Malaysia produces a lot of palm oil.

53156.q: Which mountain in the Malaysian part of Borneo is the highest in Malaysia?
53156.e: Mount Kinabalu in the state of Sabah is about 4,100 metres high. The national park around it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
53156.m: Kinabalu is the highest mountain in Malaysia.

53157.q: What can you find in the Batu Caves near Kuala Lumpur?
a: A Hindu temple in limestone caves
53157.e: The Batu Caves are limestone caves with a Hindu shrine. In front of the entrance stands a huge golden statue, and a long staircase leads up.
53157.m: There is a Hindu temple in the Batu Caves near Kuala Lumpur.

53158.q: What kind of state is Singapore?
53158.e: Singapore was briefly part of Malaysia but became a country of its own in 1965. There the city and the state are almost the same thing.

53159.q: What does the name Singapore mean?
53159.e: The name comes from Sanskrit: singa means lion and pura means city.

53160.q: Which figure with a lion’s head and a fish’s body is the symbol of Singapore?
53160.e: The Merlion is a mythical creature that is part lion and part fish. The fish body recalls the city’s past as a fishing village.
53160.m: The Merlion is the symbol of Singapore.

53161.q: Which European country set up a trading post in Singapore in 1819?
53161.e: The Briton Stamford Raffles founded the post for the British East India Company. Singapore stayed British until 1963.
53161.m: Singapore was a British colony for a long time.

53162.q: How many official languages does Singapore have?
53162.e: The official languages are English, Malay, Mandarin Chinese and Tamil. They reflect the different groups in the population.

53163.q: How big is the city-state of Singapore compared with the canton of Zurich?
a: It is ten times as big
It is the same size as Switzerland
53163.e: Singapore has an area of about 730 square kilometres, the canton of Zurich about 1,700. Even so, about six million people live in Singapore (as of 2024).
53163.m: Singapore is smaller than the canton of Zurich.

53164.q: What are the huge artificial trees in the Gardens by the Bay park in Singapore called?
53164.e: The Supertrees are steel structures up to 50 metres tall, covered with plants. At night they light up during a light and music show.

53165.q: What is the port of Singapore known for around the world?
a: It is one of the largest container ports
It is purely a fishing harbour
It lies on an inland lake
It is only open in summer
53165.e: Singapore lies on one of the most important sea routes in the world. Its port is one of the busiest container ports on Earth.
53165.m: Singapore has one of the largest ports in the world.

53166.q: What is the capital of Cambodia?
53166.e: Phnom Penh lies where the Tonle Sap River flows into the Mekong. It is the largest city in the country.
53166.m: The capital of Cambodia is Phnom Penh.

53167.q: What happened in Cambodia under the rule of the Khmer Rouge from 1975 to 1979?
53167.e: Under the Khmer Rouge an estimated 1.5 to 2 million people died through violence, hunger and forced labour.
53167.m: A great many people died in Cambodia under the Khmer Rouge.

53168.q: Which foreign currency is often used in everyday life in Cambodia?
53168.e: The official currency is the Cambodian riel. But in everyday life people often pay in US dollars.
53168.m: In Cambodia people often pay in US dollars too.

53169.q: In which century was Angkor Wat built?
53169.e: The temple was built under King Suryavarman II in the first half of the 12th century.
53169.m: Angkor Wat was built in the 12th century.

53170.q: Which town is the starting point for visits to Angkor Wat?
53170.e: Siem Reap lies only a few kilometres south of the temples. Most visitors stay overnight there.
53170.m: Siem Reap is close to Angkor Wat.

53171.q: What is the Ta Prohm temple in Angkor famous for?
a: Huge trees grow over its walls
It is the tallest tower in Asia
53171.e: At Ta Prohm the jungle has partly been left to grow. Mighty tree roots grip the old stone walls.
53171.m: At Ta Prohm trees grow over the temple walls.

53172.q: What is the Angkor Wat temple complex considered to be?
a: The largest religious building in the world
The oldest building in the world
The tallest temple in the world
The largest palace in the world
53172.e: Including its moat, Angkor Wat measures about 1.5 by 1.3 kilometres. This makes it the largest religious building in the world.
53172.m: Angkor Wat is the largest religious building in the world.

53173.q: Which is the largest city in Myanmar?
53173.e: Yangon, formerly Rangoon, is the largest city and the business centre of Myanmar. It was also the capital until 2005.
53173.m: Yangon is the largest city in Myanmar.

53174.q: What is thanaka, which many people in Myanmar put on their faces?
a: A paste made from tree bark
A cream made from rice flour
53174.e: Thanaka is made by grinding the bark of the thanaka tree on a stone with a little water. The yellowish paste cools the skin and protects it from the sun.
53174.m: Thanaka is a face paste made from tree bark.

53175.q: Which gilded shrine is the landmark of Yangon?
53175.e: The Shwedagon Pagoda is covered in gold and is the most important Buddhist shrine in Myanmar.
53175.m: The Shwedagon Pagoda stands in Yangon.

53176.q: What is the old royal city of Bagan in Myanmar known for?
53176.e: More than 2,000 temples and pagodas from the 11th to 13th centuries stand on the plain of Bagan. Bagan is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
53176.m: Thousands of temples stand in Bagan.

53177.q: What is the most important river in Myanmar called?
53177.e: The Irrawaddy flows from north to south through almost the whole country and reaches the Andaman Sea through a large delta.
53177.m: The Irrawaddy is Myanmar’s main river.

53178.q: Which colonial power ruled Myanmar until 1948?
53178.e: Myanmar was for a long time part of British India and then a separate British colony. It became independent in 1948.
53178.m: Myanmar was a British colony until 1948.

53179.q: What are the fishermen on Inle Lake in Myanmar known for?
a: They only fish at night with lamps
53179.e: The fishermen stand on one leg at the end of the boat and row with the other leg. This leaves their hands free for the net and fish trap.
53179.m: On Inle Lake the fishermen row with one leg.

53180.q: Which two oceans does the Strait of Malacca connect?
53180.e: It connects the Andaman Sea in the Indian Ocean with the South China Sea, a marginal sea of the Pacific.
53180.m: The Strait of Malacca connects the Indian Ocean with the Pacific.

53181.q: In which country is the port city of Malacca, after which the strait is named?
53181.e: Malacca lies on the west coast of Malaysia and was an important trading place for centuries. Its old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
53181.m: The city of Malacca is in Malaysia.

53182.q: Which goods made trade in Malacca so valuable in the past?
a: Spices such as pepper and cloves
53182.e: Spices from the islands of South-East Asia passed through Malacca to India, China and Europe. That is why European powers such as Portugal wanted to control the city.
53182.m: Malacca was an important port for the spice trade.

53183.q: Which danger especially threatened ships in the Strait of Malacca in the early 2000s?
53183.e: Because of the many ships and the narrow waters, pirate attacks were frequent. Joint patrols by the neighbouring countries have reduced the number of attacks.
53183.m: There were many pirate attacks in the Strait of Malacca.

53184.q: Roughly how long is the Strait of Malacca?
53184.e: From Singapore to the northern tip of Sumatra the strait is about 900 kilometres long. At its narrowest point it is only a few kilometres wide.
53184.m: The Strait of Malacca is about 900 kilometres long.

53185.q: Why do farmers build rice terraces on steep slopes?
a: To create level fields that hold water
53185.e: Paddy rice grows in flooded fields. On the level steps the water stays put, and the soil is not washed away so easily.
53185.m: Rice terraces hold water on the slope.

53186.q: In which country are the famous rice terraces of Banaue?
53186.e: The Banaue rice terraces lie in the mountains of the island of Luzon in the Philippines. They were built long ago by the Ifugao people.
53186.m: The Banaue rice terraces are in the Philippines.

53187.q: What do the rice farmers on Bali share in their old subak system?
53187.e: In the subak system the farmers share the water, organised through water temples. This cultural landscape has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2012.
53187.m: On Bali the rice farmers share the water.

53188.q: In which region of Vietnam are the well-known rice terraces around the town of Sa Pa?
a: In the mountains in the north
On an island in the south
53188.e: Sa Pa lies in the mountains of northern Vietnam near the border with China. There mountain peoples grow rice on steep terraces.
53188.m: There are rice terraces around Sa Pa in northern Vietnam.

53189.q: How many rice harvests a year are possible in good places in the warm, humid climate of South-East Asia?
53189.e: Because it is warm all year and there is enough water, in good places rice can be harvested two or even three times a year.
53189.m: In South-East Asia rice can be harvested up to three times a year.

53190.q: Which three countries share the island of Borneo?
a: Indonesia, Papua New Guinea and Australia
53190.e: Most of Borneo belongs to Indonesia. The north is shared by Malaysia and the small sultanate of Brunei.
53190.m: Borneo belongs to Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei.

53191.q: What made the small sultanate of Brunei on Borneo rich?
53191.e: Brunei produces a lot of oil and natural gas. That is why people there have high incomes and pay no income tax.

53192.q: Which two official languages does the Philippines have?
53192.e: The official languages are Filipino, which is based on Tagalog, and English. More than a hundred other languages are also spoken.
53192.m: Filipino and English are the official languages of the Philippines.

53193.q: On which river is Hanoi, the capital of Vietnam?
53193.e: Hanoi lies on the Red River in northern Vietnam. The river gets its name from the reddish colour of its mud.
53193.m: Hanoi lies on the Red River.

53194.q: Which is the largest country by area on the South-East Asian mainland?
53194.e: Myanmar covers about 677,000 square kilometres, which makes it bigger than Thailand or Vietnam.
53194.m: Myanmar is the largest country on the South-East Asian mainland.

53195.q: What does the national monument Monas in Jakarta commemorate?
53195.e: Monas is a tower about 130 metres high with a golden flame. It commemorates Indonesia’s struggle for independence.
53195.m: Monas is the national monument in Jakarta.

53196.q: Why are there many volcanoes and earthquakes in the Philippines?
a: It lies on the Pacific Ring of Fire
It lies at the North Pole
It lies in the middle of a tectonic plate
53196.e: The Philippines lies on the edge of the Pacific, where tectonic plates meet. There are especially many volcanoes and earthquakes there.
53196.m: The Philippines lies on the Pacific Ring of Fire.

53198.q: Which tropical storms hit the Philippines almost every year?
53198.e: Tropical storms form over the warm Pacific; in Asia they are called typhoons. In 2013 Typhoon Haiyan devastated large parts of the country.
53198.m: The Philippines is often hit by typhoons.

53200.q: Which religion do most of the temples in Bangkok belong to?
53200.e: Most people in Thailand are Buddhists. Bangkok has hundreds of Buddhist temples, for example Wat Arun.

53201.q: Which famous figure is worshipped in the Wat Phra Kaew temple at the Grand Palace in Bangkok?
53201.e: The Emerald Buddha is the most important Buddha figure in Thailand. It is made of green stone, and the king changes its clothing several times a year.
53201.m: The Emerald Buddha is in Wat Phra Kaew.

53202.q: Which country borders Vietnam to the north?
53202.e: Vietnam borders China to the north and Laos and Cambodia to the west. Thailand is not a direct neighbour.
53202.m: To the north, Vietnam borders China.

53203.q: Which European country ruled Vietnam as a colony as part of Indochina?
53203.e: From the 19th century Vietnam was part of French Indochina. That is why you can still find French buildings and baguettes there today.

53204.q: What is the largest city in Vietnam, formerly called Saigon, called today?
53204.e: Vietnam’s largest city lies in the south. In 1976 it was renamed after the politician Ho Chi Minh, but many people still call it Saigon.
53204.m: Saigon is now called Ho Chi Minh City.

53205.q: Roughly how many countries does the Mekong flow through?
53205.e: The Mekong flows through China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam. In places it forms the border between these countries.
53205.m: The Mekong flows through six countries.

53206.q: What is the area on the Mekong where Thailand, Laos and Myanmar meet called?
53206.e: Three countries meet where the Mekong and the Ruak flow together. This border area is called the Golden Triangle.
53206.m: Three countries meet at the Golden Triangle.

53207.q: Which structures on the Mekong worry fishermen downstream?
53207.e: Large dams have been built, above all in China and Laos. They change the water level and block fish on their migrations.

53208.q: Which country is a neighbour of Cambodia?
53208.e: Cambodia borders Thailand, Laos and Vietnam. To the south-west lies the Gulf of Thailand.
53208.m: Cambodia borders Thailand, Laos and Vietnam.

53209.q: Which mythical creature forms the railings along the path to the temple at Angkor Wat?
53209.e: The many-headed snake is called a naga and is an important creature in Hindu and Buddhist mythology. At Angkor its bodies form the stone railings.
53209.m: At Angkor stone naga snakes form the railings.

53210.q: Which country does the island of Sumatra on the Strait of Malacca belong to?
53210.e: Sumatra is one of the largest islands of Indonesia. On the other side of the strait lies the Malay Peninsula with Malaysia.

53211.q: Where does most of the oil come from that tankers carry through the Strait of Malacca to East Asia?
53211.e: Huge tankers carry oil from the Persian Gulf through the strait to China, Japan and South Korea. It is the shortest sea route between these regions.
53211.m: Many oil tankers pass through the Strait of Malacca.

53212.q: What do you call rice that grows in flooded fields?
53212.e: Paddy rice grows in fields that stand under water. On terraces on a slope, the water stays on the level steps.
53212.m: Paddy rice grows in flooded fields.

53213.q: On which island is the town of Ubud with its well-known rice terraces?
53213.e: Ubud lies in the centre of the Indonesian island of Bali. To the north are the Tegallalang rice terraces, a popular place to visit.
53213.m: There are famous rice terraces near Ubud on Bali.

53214.q: Which great ape lives in the rainforests of Borneo?
53214.e: Orangutans live only on Borneo and Sumatra. Because the rainforest is being cut down, they are severely threatened.

53215.q: Which island is the third largest in the world?
53215.e: Only Greenland and New Guinea are bigger than Borneo. Madagascar comes fourth.
53215.m: Borneo is the third largest island in the world.

53216.q: What are the many native peoples of inland Borneo called together?
53216.e: Dayak is a collective name for many peoples of Borneo. In the past many of them lived in large longhouses by the rivers.
53216.m: The native peoples of Borneo are called Dayak.

53217.q: What is a lot of rainforest on Borneo cut down for?
53217.e: Palm oil, which is found in many foods, is made from the fruit of the oil palm. Large areas of rainforest on Borneo were cleared for it.
53217.m: On Borneo rainforest often gives way to oil palms.

53218.q: What is Gunung Mulu National Park in the Malaysian part of Borneo famous for?
53218.e: Mulu National Park contains the Sarawak Chamber, one of the largest underground cave chambers in the world. The park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
53218.m: Mulu National Park is famous for its caves.

53219.q: What is inside the Jewel building at Singapore’s airport?
a: A huge waterfall in the hall
A ski slope with real snow
53219.e: In the Jewel building at Changi Airport, a waterfall about 40 m high pours down from the glass dome. An indoor forest grows all around it.
53219.m: Singapore’s airport has an indoor waterfall.

53220.q: Which city was the last royal capital of Myanmar before the British conquered the country?
53220.e: Mandalay was founded in 1857 and was the seat of the Burmese kings until 1885. Today it is the country’s second largest city.
53220.m: Mandalay was the last royal capital of Myanmar.

53221.q: Which landscape covers most of the Arabian Peninsula?
53221.e: The Arabian Peninsula is very hot and dry. Large sand deserts such as the Rub’ al Khali and the Nafud cover large parts of it.
53221.m: The Arabian Peninsula is mostly desert.

53222.q: What is the largest peninsula in the world called?
53222.e: The Arabian Peninsula covers about 3 million square kilometres, more than seventy times the area of Switzerland.
53222.m: The Arabian Peninsula is the largest peninsula in the world.

53223.q: Which animal traditionally carried people and goods through the desert on the Arabian Peninsula?
53223.e: The dromedary has one hump and can go a long time without water. That is why it was the most important pack and riding animal in Arabia’s deserts.
53223.m: The dromedary is Arabia’s desert animal.

53224.q: Which country lies in the far south-west of the Arabian Peninsula?
53224.e: Yemen borders the Red Sea to the west and the Gulf of Aden to the south.
53224.m: Yemen lies in the south-west of the Arabian Peninsula.

53225.q: In which city on the Arabian Peninsula is the tallest building in the world?
53225.e: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai is more than 800 metres tall. Dubai is part of the United Arab Emirates.
53225.m: The tallest building in the world is in Dubai.

53226.q: How do many countries on the Arabian Peninsula get a large part of their drinking water?
a: From rivers that flow all year
53226.e: Because there is hardly any rain and there are no permanent rivers, seawater is desalinated in special plants.
53226.m: In the Gulf, a lot of drinking water is made from seawater.

53227.q: What is a wadi on the Arabian Peninsula?
a: A river valley that is usually dry
A green oasis with palm trees
53227.e: A wadi is a valley that carries water only briefly after rare rainfall.
53227.m: A wadi only carries water after rain.

53229.q: Roughly how many times bigger than Switzerland is Saudi Arabia?
53229.e: Saudi Arabia has about 2.15 million km², Switzerland about 41,000 km². 2,150,000 divided by 41,000 is about 52.
53229.m: Saudi Arabia is about fifty times as big as Switzerland.

53230.q: In which city in Saudi Arabia is the tomb of the Prophet Muhammad?
53230.e: Muhammad is buried in the Prophet’s Mosque in Medina, the second holiest city of Islam.
53230.m: Medina is the city of the Prophet’s Mosque.

53231.q: Which big port city of Saudi Arabia lies on the Red Sea?
53231.e: Jeddah is one of the largest cities in the country and, for many pilgrims, the gateway to Mecca.
53231.m: Jeddah is the big port city on the Red Sea.

53232.q: What is the main colour of the flag of Saudi Arabia?
53232.e: The green flag shows the Islamic declaration of faith in white writing with a sword underneath.
53232.m: The flag of Saudi Arabia is green.

53233.e: Saudi Arabia is a kingdom. King Abdulaziz ibn Saud founded it in 1932, and his family has ruled ever since.

53234.q: In which emirate is the tallest building in the world, the Burj Khalifa?
53234.e: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai is more than 800 metres tall. Dubai is the best-known city of the United Arab Emirates.
53234.m: The Burj Khalifa is in Dubai.

53235.q: Which famous Paris museum has had a branch in Abu Dhabi since 2017?
53235.e: The Louvre Abu Dhabi opened in 2017 and bears the name of the museum in Paris.
53235.m: Abu Dhabi has had its own Louvre since 2017.

53236.q: What made the United Arab Emirates rich?
53236.e: From the 1960s a lot of oil was produced in the Emirates. The money was used to build modern cities such as Dubai and Abu Dhabi.

53237.q: Which is the largest of the emirates by area?
53237.e: Abu Dhabi covers about 87 per cent of the land area of the UAE.
53237.m: Abu Dhabi is by far the largest emirate.

53238.q: Which landscape covers most of the United Arab Emirates?
53238.e: The Emirates lie on the Arabian Peninsula. Most of the country is hot sandy and stony desert.

53239.q: Which building in Dubai was the tallest in the world in 2025?
53239.e: The Burj Khalifa opened in 2010 and is the tallest structure in the world (as of 2025).
53239.m: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai is the tallest building in the world.

53240.q: Which natural resource made Dubai rich from the 1960s?
53240.e: In 1966 oil was found off Dubai. The money was used to expand the city. Today Dubai earns mainly from trade and tourism.

53241.q: Which luxury hotel in Dubai is shaped like a sail?
53241.e: The Burj Al Arab hotel stands on an artificial island off the beach and opened in 1999.
53241.m: The Burj Al Arab looks like a sail.

53242.q: Which city is the largest city in the United Arab Emirates?
53242.e: Dubai has more inhabitants than any other city in the UAE and is a centre for trade and tourism.
53242.m: Dubai is the largest city in the Emirates.

53243.q: What is the strait that connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman called?
53243.e: At its narrowest point the Strait of Hormuz is only about 40 km wide, and it is one of the most important shipping routes.
53243.m: The Strait of Hormuz is the gateway to the Persian Gulf.

53244.q: Which country lies along the whole northern shore of the Persian Gulf?
53244.e: Iran owns the entire northern coast, while the Arab states lie on the southern shore.
53244.m: The northern shore of the Persian Gulf belongs to Iran.

53245.q: Which island country lies in the Persian Gulf?
53245.e: Bahrain consists of many islands off the coast of Saudi Arabia, and its capital is Manama.
53245.m: Bahrain is an island country in the Persian Gulf.

53246.q: Which country juts into the Persian Gulf as a peninsula and has Doha as its capital?
53246.e: Qatar is a small peninsula on the east coast of Arabia, and its capital is Doha.
53246.m: Qatar is a peninsula in the Persian Gulf.

53247.q: What did many people on the Persian Gulf live from before oil was found?
53247.e: Divers brought up oysters with pearls from the Gulf until cultured pearls and oil replaced this trade.
53247.m: Before oil, people on the Gulf lived from pearls.

53248.q: The Persian Gulf is a marginal sea of which ocean?
53248.e: The Persian Gulf is connected to the Indian Ocean through the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea.
53248.m: The Persian Gulf is a marginal sea of the Indian Ocean.

53249.q: Which landscape shapes large parts of Iran?
53249.e: Most of Iran lies on a plateau. It is surrounded by high mountains such as the Zagros, and there are large deserts inland.
53249.m: Iran is a country of mountains and deserts.

53250.q: What is the Iranian New Year festival at the start of spring called?
53250.e: Nowruz means “new day” and is celebrated around 21 March, when day and night are the same length.
53250.m: Nowruz is the Persian New Year festival in spring.

53251.q: What kind of mountain is Damavand, the highest mountain in Iran?
a: A glaciated mountain by the sea
53251.e: Damavand is a volcano in the Alborz mountains and more than 5600 metres high.
53251.m: Damavand is a volcano and the highest mountain in Iran.

53252.q: Which large inland body of water does Iran border to the north?
53252.e: Iran’s northern coast lies on the Caspian Sea, the largest lake on Earth.
53252.m: To the north, Iran borders the Caspian Sea.

53253.q: What is the capital of Iran?
53253.e: Tehran lies in the north of the country at the foot of the Alborz mountains and is Iran’s largest city.
53253.m: Tehran is the capital of Iran.

53254.q: What can you find in the interior of the Iranian Plateau?
53254.e: In the interior of Iran lie large deserts such as the Dasht-e Kavir, with salt crusts and marshes.
53254.m: There are large salt deserts in the interior of Iran.

53255.q: Tehran is the capital of which country?
53255.e: Tehran is the capital and largest city of Iran. Many millions of people live in the metropolitan area.
53255.m: Tehran is the capital of Iran.

53256.q: What rises directly north of Tehran?
53256.e: Tehran lies on the southern slope of the Alborz mountains. The mountains are often covered in snow in winter and mark the city’s northern edge.
53256.m: Tehran lies at the foot of a high mountain range.

53257.q: Which structure from 1971 is a well-known landmark of Tehran?
53257.e: The Azadi Tower, Freedom Tower in English, stands on a large square in the west of Tehran.
53257.m: The Azadi Tower is a landmark of Tehran.

53258.q: What is the capital of Iraq?
53258.e: Baghdad is the largest city in Iraq and lies in the centre of the country.
53258.m: Baghdad is the capital of Iraq.

53259.q: What special shape did the city of Baghdad have when it was founded?
53259.e: The caliph al-Mansur had Baghdad laid out as a round city in 762. It became a centre of learning.
53259.m: Baghdad was founded as a round city.

53260.q: Which city is Iraq’s most important port?
53260.e: Basra lies in the far south near the coast and is Iraq’s access to the sea.
53260.m: Basra is the port city in the south of Iraq.

53261.q: Which two languages are official languages in Iraq?
53261.e: Iraq’s constitution names Arabic and Kurdish as official languages.
53261.m: Arabic and Kurdish are the official languages of Iraq.

53262.q: Which two big rivers flow through Iraq?
53262.e: The Euphrates and Tigris flow through Iraq and reach the Persian Gulf together. The land between them is called Mesopotamia.
53262.m: The Euphrates and Tigris flow through Iraq.

53263.q: Which sea does Iraq have a short stretch of access to?
53263.e: Iraq has only a few dozen kilometres of coast in the far south.
53263.m: Iraq has only a short stretch of access to the Persian Gulf.

53264.q: Through which countries does the Euphrates flow?
53264.e: The Euphrates rises in Turkey, flows through Syria and Iraq and joins the Tigris there.
53264.m: The Euphrates flows through Turkey, Syria and Iraq.

53265.q: What is the water of the Euphrates especially important for to the people along the river?
53265.e: In this dry region, grain and vegetables only grow if fields are watered with river water.
53265.m: The Euphrates waters fields in a dry land.

53266.q: Which river is longer, the Euphrates or the Tigris?
53266.e: The Euphrates is about 2700 to 2800 km long, the Tigris about 1900 km. The Euphrates is the longest river in Western Asia.
53266.m: The Euphrates is longer than the Tigris.

53267.q: Which big dam in Turkey holds back the Euphrates?
53267.e: The Atatürk Dam in south-eastern Anatolia supplies electricity and water for irrigation.
53267.m: The Atatürk Dam holds back the Euphrates.

53268.q: Apart from the Tigris, which other big river flows through Mesopotamia?
53268.e: Mesopotamia means “land between the rivers”. This refers to the Euphrates and Tigris, where cities such as Assur and Babylon grew up early on.
53268.m: The Euphrates and Tigris flow through Mesopotamia.

53269.q: Which capital city lies on the Tigris?
53269.e: Baghdad, the capital of Iraq, lies on the Tigris. Mosul in northern Iraq is also on this river.

53270.q: In which country does the Tigris rise?
53270.e: The Tigris rises in the mountains of south-eastern Turkey. It then flows through Iraq to the Persian Gulf.

53271.q: Which landscape lies in the south of Iraq on the lower Euphrates and Tigris?
53271.e: The Mesopotamian Marshes are wetlands where the Marsh Arabs have lived for thousands of years.
53271.m: There are large marshes on the lower Euphrates and Tigris.

53272.q: Which city in Mesopotamia is seen as one of the first big cities in the world?
53272.e: By around 3000 BC Uruk already had tens of thousands of inhabitants and was a centre of the Sumerians.
53272.m: Uruk was one of the first big cities in the world.

53273.q: How did farmers in Mesopotamia make the dry land fertile?
53273.e: They led the water of the rivers onto the fields through a network of canals.
53273.m: In Mesopotamia fields were watered with canals.

53274.q: Which Babylonian king had a famous collection of laws written on a stone pillar?
53274.e: The Code of Hammurabi dates from around 1750 BC and is now in the Louvre in Paris.
53274.m: King Hammurabi had laws written on a stone pillar.

53275.q: Between which two rivers does Mesopotamia lie?
53275.e: Mesopotamia means land between the rivers. This refers to the Euphrates and Tigris in present-day Iraq.
53275.m: Mesopotamia lies between the Euphrates and Tigris.

53276.q: Which ancient city in Mesopotamia does the blue Ishtar Gate come from?
53276.e: The Ishtar Gate was a city gate of Babylon and is decorated with blue glazed bricks. Today it stands reconstructed in a museum in Berlin.
53276.m: The Ishtar Gate comes from Babylon.

53277.q: Why does an hour have 60 minutes?
a: Because of Mesopotamia’s base-60 number system
Because of the phases of the moon
Because of the invention of the clock
53277.e: The Sumerians and Babylonians counted using the base number 60, and our way of dividing time comes from that.

53278.q: Which curved, fertile region does Mesopotamia belong to?
53278.e: The Fertile Crescent stretches from the Persian Gulf through Mesopotamia to the Mediterranean coast.
53278.m: Mesopotamia is part of the Fertile Crescent.

53279.q: What is special about swimming in the Dead Sea?
a: You float on the surface almost by yourself
You sink straight to the bottom
There are huge waves for surfing
53279.e: The water is very salty and therefore heavier than normal water. The body is pushed up strongly, and you can even lie back and read a newspaper.
53279.m: You don’t sink in the salty Dead Sea.

53280.q: Which raw material for fertiliser is extracted from the water of the Dead Sea?
53280.e: Potash, which is used as fertiliser in farming, is produced in large evaporation ponds.
53280.m: Potash for fertiliser is extracted from the Dead Sea.

53281.q: Why does the Dead Sea have its name?
a: Almost no living things live in it
53281.e: Because of all the salt, no fish or plants can live in it, apart from a few microorganisms.
53281.m: Hardly any living things live in the Dead Sea.

53282.q: Which river flows into the Dead Sea?
53282.e: The Jordan flows south from the Sea of Galilee into the Dead Sea, which has no outflow.
53282.m: The Jordan flows into the Dead Sea.

53283.q: How does the Dead Sea lose its water, even though it has no outflow?
53283.e: In the great heat the water evaporates and the salt is left behind. That is why the lake is so salty.
53283.m: The Dead Sea loses its water through evaporation.

53284.q: What is special about the location of the Dead Sea?
a: Its shore is the lowest point on land on Earth
It lies on a high mountain
It lies at the North Pole
53284.e: The shore of the Dead Sea lies more than 400 metres below sea level. No other place on land is so low.
53284.m: The Dead Sea lies lower than any other place on land.

53285.q: Which famous ancient texts were found from 1947 in caves at Qumran by the Dead Sea?
53285.e: In 1947 a shepherd discovered the first scrolls, including very old copies of biblical texts.
53285.m: The Dead Sea Scrolls were found at Qumran.

53286.q: Which famous rock city is in Jordan?
53286.e: Petra was carved straight into red sandstone cliffs by the Nabataeans more than 2000 years ago. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
53286.m: The rock city of Petra is in Jordan.

53287.q: What form of state does Jordan have?
53287.e: Jordan is a Hashemite kingdom with a king at its head.

53288.q: Through which city does Jordan have its only access to the sea?
53288.e: Aqaba lies in the far south and is the country’s only port.
53288.m: Jordan’s port city on the sea is Aqaba.

53289.q: Which very salty body of water lies on Jordan’s western border?
53289.e: The Dead Sea is so salty that you can swim in it without effort. Its shore is the lowest place on land on Earth.

53290.q: Which river does Jordan border to the west?
53290.e: The Jordan forms part of the border in the west and gave the country its name.
53290.m: Jordan is named after the River Jordan.

53292.q: How were the famous buildings of Petra made?
a: They were carved straight out of the rock
They were built of mud bricks
53292.e: The Nabataeans carved temples, tombs and houses straight out of the sandstone cliffs. That is why Petra is called a rock city.
53292.m: The buildings of Petra are carved out of the rock.

53293.q: What did the people of Petra trade especially successfully?
53293.e: Caravans carrying frankincense from southern Arabia and spices to the Mediterranean passed through Petra.
53293.m: Petra became rich from the frankincense trade.

53294.q: How did the people of Petra get their water?
53294.e: The Nabataeans collected rainwater in gutters, pipes and cisterns and stored it for the dry season.
53294.m: Petra collected its water in cisterns.

53295.q: Which empire took over the kingdom of Petra in AD 106?
53295.e: Under Emperor Trajan the area became the Roman province of Arabia in AD 106.
53295.m: From AD 106 Petra belonged to the Roman Empire.

53296.q: Which big city in Israel lies on the Mediterranean and is the most important business centre?
53296.e: Tel Aviv was founded in 1909 and is today a centre for trade, banking and technology.
53296.m: Tel Aviv is Israel’s business centre on the Mediterranean.

53297.q: On which sea is the Israeli port city of Haifa?
53297.e: Haifa lies in the north of Israel on the Mediterranean and on Mount Carmel. It is an important port city.
53297.m: Haifa is a port city on the Mediterranean.

53298.q: Which city lies in the far south of Israel on the Red Sea?
53298.e: Eilat lies on the Gulf of Aqaba and is a popular place for diving.
53298.m: Eilat is Israel’s city on the Red Sea.

53299.q: What is the Knesset in Israel?
53299.e: The Knesset is the parliament of Israel. It has 120 members and meets in Jerusalem.
53299.m: Israel’s parliament is called the Knesset.

53300.q: For which three religions is Jerusalem a holy city?
53300.e: Jerusalem is home to the Western Wall, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre and the Dome of the Rock.
53300.m: Jerusalem is holy to three world religions.

53301.q: What is the capital of Lebanon?
53301.e: Beirut lies on the Mediterranean coast and is the largest city in the country.
53301.m: Beirut is the capital of Lebanon.

53302.q: Which tree is shown on the flag of Lebanon?
53302.e: The cedar of Lebanon grows in the mountains and has been a symbol of the country since ancient times.
53302.m: The cedar is the symbol of Lebanon.

53303.q: Roughly how big is Lebanon compared with Switzerland?
53303.e: Lebanon has about 10,450 km², Switzerland about 41,300 km². 10,450 divided by 41,300 is about 0.25.
53303.m: Lebanon is about a quarter the size of Switzerland.

53304.q: Which ancient seafaring people lived on the coast of present-day Lebanon?
53304.e: The Phoenicians founded cities such as Tyre, Sidon and Byblos and traded all over the Mediterranean.
53304.m: The Phoenicians were the seafaring people of Lebanon.

53305.q: What is the fertile Beqaa Valley in Lebanon mainly used for?
53305.e: In the Beqaa Valley between two mountain ranges, grain, vegetables and grapes for wine are grown.
53305.m: The Beqaa Valley is Lebanon’s breadbasket.

53306.q: What nickname did Lebanon once have because of its mountains and banks?
53306.e: Lebanon was called this because of its snowy mountains and Beirut’s strong banking sector.
53306.m: Lebanon was once called the “Switzerland of the Middle East”.

53307.q: Which well-known beach resort in Egypt lies on the Red Sea?
53307.e: Hurghada lies on Egypt’s Red Sea coast and is popular with divers and holidaymakers.
53307.m: Hurghada is a beach resort on the Red Sea.

53308.q: Between which two continents does the Red Sea lie?
53308.e: To the west of the Red Sea lies Africa, to the east the Arabian Peninsula in Asia. In the south, the Bab-el-Mandeb strait leads into the Gulf of Aden.
53308.m: The Red Sea separates Africa from Asia.

53309.q: Which large country on the Arabian Peninsula has a long coast on the Red Sea?
53309.e: Saudi Arabia lies on the eastern side of the Red Sea. In the north it also borders the Gulf of Aqaba.
53309.m: Saudi Arabia lies on the Red Sea.

53310.q: Which African country with the capital Asmara lies on the Red Sea?
53310.e: Eritrea has a long coast on the Red Sea, opposite the Arabian Peninsula.
53310.m: Eritrea lies on the Red Sea.

53311.q: Which small country lies on the African side of the Bab-el-Mandeb strait?
53311.e: Djibouti lies on the Gulf of Aden at the southern entrance to the Red Sea, so its port is very important.
53311.m: Djibouti guards the entrance to the Red Sea.

53312.q: How was the trench of the Red Sea formed?
a: Two tectonic plates are moving apart
53312.e: The African and Arabian plates are drifting apart, which is why the Red Sea is slowly getting wider.
53312.m: The Red Sea is getting wider because of plate movement.

53313.q: Why does Dubai rely heavily on tourism and trade instead of just oil?
a: It is not by the sea
53313.e: Dubai had much less oil than Abu Dhabi, so it expanded its port, airport and tourism early on.
53313.m: Today Dubai lives mainly from trade and tourism.

53314.q: What made Saudi Arabia rich in the 20th century?
53314.e: From 1938 huge oil deposits were found in Saudi Arabia. Selling oil made the country very rich.

53315.q: What is oil often called because of its colour and value?
53315.e: Oil is dark and so valuable that it has made the Gulf states rich.
53315.m: Oil is also called black gold.

53316.q: Apart from oil, which raw material is extracted in huge amounts in the Persian Gulf?
53316.e: The largest natural gas field in the world lies under the Persian Gulf. Qatar and Iran extract a great deal of natural gas there.
53316.m: The Persian Gulf has a lot of oil and natural gas.

53317.q: In which country is the largest conventional oil field in the world?
53317.e: The Ghawar field in eastern Saudi Arabia is about 280 km long. It is the largest conventional oil field in the world.
53317.m: The largest oil field in the world is in Saudi Arabia.

53318.q: What did Switzerland have because of the oil crisis of 1973?
53318.e: Because Arab oil states supplied less oil, the Federal Council banned driving on three Sundays in November and December 1973.

53319.q: Which sea is surrounded by big oil countries such as Saudi Arabia, Iran and Kuwait?
53319.e: Some of the largest oil deposits in the world lie around the Persian Gulf. Oil was first found there in Iran in 1908.
53319.m: There is a lot of oil around the Persian Gulf.

53320.q: What is the strait between Russia and Alaska called?
53320.e: At its narrowest point the Bering Strait is only about 82 kilometres wide. It separates Asia from North America.
53320.m: The Bering Strait separates Russia from Alaska.

53321.q: Which ocean does Russia border to the east?
53321.e: In the east, Russia reaches the Pacific. Sakhalin, Russia’s largest island, lies there too, north of Japan.
53321.m: In the east, Russia reaches the Pacific.

53322.q: Which long river in the European part of Russia flows into the Caspian Sea?
53322.e: At about 3500 km, the Volga is the longest river in Europe. It flows into the Caspian Sea.
53322.m: The Volga is the longest river in Europe.

53323.q: What is the highest mountain in Russia, in the Caucasus, called?
53323.e: Elbrus is 5642 metres high and lies in the Caucasus. It is often also seen as the highest mountain in Europe.
53323.m: Elbrus in the Caucasus is Russia’s highest mountain.

53324.q: Roughly how many times does the area of Switzerland fit into the area of Russia?
53324.e: Russia has about 17.1 million km², Switzerland about 41,300 km². 17,100,000 divided by 41,300 is about 414.
53324.m: Russia is about four hundred times as big as Switzerland.

53325.q: What is the Russian exclave on the Baltic Sea between Poland and Lithuania called?
53325.e: The Kaliningrad region has no land connection to the rest of Russia. It lies on the Baltic Sea between Poland and Lithuania.
53325.m: Kaliningrad is a Russian region with no land link to the rest of the country.

53326.q: What is the currency of Russia called?
53326.e: In Russia people pay with the rouble. One rouble is divided into 100 kopecks.
53326.m: The Russian currency is called the rouble.

53327.q: Roughly how many people live in Moscow?
53327.e: About 13 million people live in Moscow. This makes the Russian capital one of the largest cities in Europe, with more inhabitants than the whole of Switzerland.
53327.m: With about 13 million people, Moscow is one of the largest cities in Europe.

53328.q: What is the fortified complex in the centre of Moscow where the Russian president has his official residence called?
53328.e: The Moscow Kremlin is a medieval fortress with palaces and churches. It is the official residence of the Russian president.
53328.m: The Kremlin is Moscow’s political centre.

53329.q: Which famous square lies right next to the Moscow Kremlin?
53329.e: Red Square borders the eastern wall of the Kremlin. The old Russian word for “red” also meant “beautiful”.
53329.m: Red Square lies right next to the Kremlin.

53330.q: Which church with colourful onion domes stands on Red Square in Moscow?
53330.e: St Basil’s Cathedral was built in the 16th century under Ivan the Terrible. Its colourful onion domes are a symbol of Russia.
53330.m: St Basil’s Cathedral with its colourful domes is a landmark of Moscow.

53331.e: The city is named after the Moskva River, which flows through it. The Moskva later flows into the Oka, a tributary of the Volga.
53331.m: Moscow bears the name of its river, the Moskva.

53332.q: What is the Moscow Metro especially known for?
53332.e: Many stations of the Moscow Metro, which opened in 1935, are decorated with marble, mosaics and chandeliers. That is why they are often called “underground palaces”.
53332.m: The Moscow Metro has stations that look like palaces.

53333.q: What is the second largest city in Russia, which used to be the capital, called?
53333.e: Saint Petersburg was the capital of the Russian Empire from 1712 to 1918. In 1918 the capital was moved back to Moscow.
53333.m: Before Moscow, Saint Petersburg was Russia’s capital for a long time.

53334.q: Which huge region in Russia stretches from the Urals to the Pacific?
53334.e: Siberia covers the whole northern part of Asia from the Urals to the Pacific. It makes up about three quarters of Russia’s area.
53334.m: Siberia stretches from the Urals to the Pacific Ocean.

53335.q: What is the permanently frozen ground that covers large parts of Siberia called?
53335.e: With permafrost, the ground stays frozen without a break for at least two years. In summer only a thin layer at the surface thaws.
53335.m: Permafrost ground only thaws at the surface, even in summer.

53336.q: Which village in Siberia is seen as one of the coldest inhabited places on Earth?
53336.e: In 1933 about -67.7 degrees Celsius was measured in Oymyakon. That is why the village is seen as the “Pole of Cold” of the Northern Hemisphere.
53336.m: Oymyakon is one of the coldest inhabited places in the world.

53337.q: Which city is the largest city in Siberia?
53337.e: Novosibirsk has about 1.6 million inhabitants. The city grew up at the end of the 19th century when the Trans-Siberian Railway was built.
53337.m: Novosibirsk is the largest city in Siberia.

53338.q: What is the main type of climate in Siberia?
a: Continental climate with very cold winters
53338.e: Siberia lies far away from warming seas. That is why the winters are extremely cold and the summers are short but often warm.
53338.m: Siberia has a continental climate with icy winters.

53339.q: What probably exploded over Siberia in 1908 and flattened millions of trees?
a: A gas store in a factory
53339.e: In the Tunguska event, an object from space probably exploded in the air. Trees were flattened over more than 2000 km².
53339.m: In 1908 an asteroid or comet probably exploded over Siberia.

53340.q: Which Ice Age animal is found again and again in the frozen ground of Siberia?
53340.e: In Siberia’s permafrost, dead animals are preserved as if in a freezer. That is why well-preserved mammoths are found there.
53340.m: Whole mammoths have been found in Siberia’s permafrost.

53341.q: Which two cities does the Trans-Siberian Railway connect?
53341.e: The main line of the Trans-Siberian runs from Moscow to Vladivostok on the Pacific.
53341.m: The Trans-Siberian runs from Moscow to Vladivostok on the Pacific.

53342.q: On which ocean is Vladivostok, the end of the Trans-Siberian line?
53342.e: Vladivostok lies in Russia’s Far East on the Sea of Japan, part of the Pacific. It is an important port.
53342.m: The Trans-Siberian ends in Vladivostok on the Pacific.

53343.q: Through which huge region does the Trans-Siberian Railway run?
53343.e: The name says it all: the railway runs right across Siberia. It was built from 1891, in the time of the tsars.
53343.m: The Trans-Siberian runs right across Siberia.

53344.q: Roughly how many days does a non-stop journey on the Trans-Siberian Railway from Moscow to Vladivostok take?
53344.e: Depending on the service, the train takes about six to seven days for the more than 9000 kilometres. Passengers sleep in sleeping cars.
53344.m: A trip on the Trans-Siberian takes about a week.

53345.q: Roughly how long is the Trans-Siberian line from Moscow to Vladivostok?
53345.e: At more than 9000 kilometres, the Trans-Siberian is the longest railway line in the world. It crosses seven time zones.
53345.m: The Trans-Siberian is the longest railway line in the world.

53346.q: What track gauge does the Trans-Siberian Railway have?
53346.e: In Russia trains run on broad gauge track of 1520 millimetres. This is wider than the standard gauge of 1435 millimetres used by Swiss Federal Railways (SBB).
53346.m: Russian trains run on wider tracks than the SBB.

53347.q: Which famous lake does the Trans-Siberian pass?
53347.e: The line runs along the southern shore of Lake Baikal. It is the deepest lake in the world, and many travellers stop in Irkutsk to visit it.

53348.q: Roughly how long is Lake Baikal?
53348.e: Lake Baikal is about 673 kilometres long but at most 82 kilometres wide. It has the shape of a long crescent.
53348.m: Lake Baikal is a very long, narrow lake.

53349.q: Roughly what share of the Earth’s liquid fresh water is in Lake Baikal?
53349.e: Because it is so deep, Lake Baikal holds about 20 per cent of the Earth’s liquid fresh water. That is more than all five Great Lakes of North America together.
53349.m: About a fifth of the world’s liquid fresh water is in Lake Baikal.

53350.q: Which species of seal lives only in Lake Baikal?
53350.e: The Baikal seal, also called the nerpa, is one of the few seals that live in fresh water. It is found only in Lake Baikal.
53350.m: The Baikal seal is a freshwater seal that lives only in Lake Baikal.

53351.q: How many rivers flow out of Lake Baikal?
53351.e: More than 300 rivers flow into Lake Baikal, but only the Angara flows out of it.
53351.m: Many rivers flow into Lake Baikal, but only one flows out.

53352.q: Why do many animal species live in Lake Baikal that are found nowhere else?
a: Because the lake is very old and remote
Because the lake was made by people
Because animals from zoos were released there
Because the lake dries up every year
53352.e: Lake Baikal is about 25 million years old. Over this long time its own species have developed there, such as the Baikal seal and the omul fish.
53352.m: Ancient Lake Baikal has many animals found only there.

53354.q: Which list is Lake Baikal on because of its unique nature?
a: List of the most polluted waters
53354.e: Lake Baikal was added to UNESCO’s World Natural Heritage list in 1996. Many of its animal and plant species are found only there.
53354.m: Lake Baikal is UNESCO World Natural Heritage.

53355.q: In which direction does the Lena mainly flow?
53355.e: The Lena rises in mountains near Lake Baikal and then flows north. It flows into the Arctic Ocean.
53355.m: The Lena flows from south to north to the Arctic Ocean.

53356.q: Into which sea does the Lena in Siberia flow?
53356.e: The Lena flows into the Laptev Sea through a large delta. This is part of the Arctic Ocean.
53356.m: The Lena flows into the Arctic Ocean.

53357.q: Why do many houses in the city of Yakutsk on the Lena stand on stilts?
a: Because of termites in the ground
53357.e: Yakutsk is built on permafrost. If the warm houses stood directly on the ground, it would thaw and the houses would sink.
53357.m: Yakutsk on the Lena stands on frozen ground.

53358.q: What are the Lena Pillars, which are a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
a: Tall rock towers on the riverbank
53358.e: The Lena Pillars are limestone rocks up to 100 metres high that rise along the bank for many kilometres. They have been World Natural Heritage since 2012.
53358.m: The Lena Pillars are spectacular rocks on the bank of the Lena.

53359.q: What does the Lena form at its mouth?
53359.e: The Lena Delta consists of many river branches and islands. It is one of the largest river deltas on Earth and a protected area for birds.
53359.m: At its mouth, the Lena branches into a huge delta.

53360.q: Why can ships hardly use the Lena for many months of the year?
53360.e: In the long Siberian winter the Lena freezes over. Then the ice is sometimes even used as a road for lorries.
53360.m: In winter the frozen Lena becomes an ice road.

53361.q: Which river is seen as the river carrying the most water in Russia?
53361.e: At its mouth the Yenisei carries on average about 19,000 cubic metres of water per second. That is more than any other river in Russia.
53361.m: The Yenisei carries more water than any other river in Russia.

53362.q: Into which sea does the Yenisei flow?
53362.e: The Yenisei flows from south to north through Siberia. It flows into the Kara Sea, a marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean.
53362.m: The Yenisei flows into the Arctic Ocean.

53363.q: Through which large region does the Yenisei flow?
53363.e: The Yenisei flows through Siberia in the Asian part of Russia. The city of Krasnoyarsk, with over a million people, lies on its banks.
53363.m: The Yenisei is a large river in Siberia.

53364.q: Which two parts of Siberia does the Yenisei roughly divide?
53364.e: West of the Yenisei lies the flat West Siberian Plain. To the east begins the higher Central Siberian Plateau.
53364.m: The Yenisei forms the border between Western and Eastern Siberia.

53365.q: In which direction does the Yenisei flow?
a: In a circle around a lake
53365.e: The Yenisei rises in southern Siberia and flows north into the Arctic Ocean.
53365.m: The Yenisei flows from south to north.

53366.q: What is the power of the Yenisei mainly used for?
a: to generate electricity with hydroelectric power stations
53366.e: Some of Russia's largest hydroelectric power stations stand on the Yenisei, for example near Sayanogorsk and Krasnoyarsk. They supply electricity for industry and cities.
53366.m: Large dams on the Yenisei generate a lot of electricity.

53367.q: Through which country does the Ob flow?
53367.e: The Ob flows through Siberia in Russia. Together with its tributary, the Irtysh, it forms one of the longest river systems in Asia.
53367.m: The Ob is a large river in Siberia.

53368.q: Into which sea does the Ob flow?
53368.e: The Ob flows from south to north through Siberia and enters the Arctic Ocean through a long bay.
53368.m: The Ob flows north into the Arctic Ocean.

53369.q: Which large Siberian city lies on the Ob?
53369.e: Novosibirsk was founded in 1893 where the Trans-Siberian Railway crosses the Ob. Today it is the third-largest city in Russia.
53369.m: Novosibirsk grew up at the railway bridge over the Ob.

53370.q: Why are there often big floods on the Ob in spring?
a: The ice thaws in the south while the river is still frozen in the north
Because spring has the most rain
Because the sea pushes into the river
Because the glaciers in the Urals melt
53370.e: The Ob flows north. On the upper river in the south it thaws earlier, but further north ice still blocks the way. The water builds up and overflows the banks.
53370.m: On the Ob, meltwater builds up in spring.

53371.q: Through which lowland does the Ob flow?
53371.e: The West Siberian Plain is one of the largest flat areas on Earth. Because it is so flat, there are huge swamps there.
53371.m: The Ob crosses the flat and swampy West Siberian Plain.

53372.q: Which valuable raw materials are extracted in large quantities in the area of the lower Ob?
53372.e: Some of the largest oil and gas fields in the world lie in the West Siberian Plain along the Ob. A large part of Russia's natural gas comes from there.
53372.m: A lot of oil and gas is extracted along the lower Ob.

53373.q: What is the huge belt of coniferous forest in northern Russia called?
53373.e: The taiga is the boreal coniferous forest that stretches right across Russia. It is the largest continuous forest area on Earth.
53373.m: The taiga is the great coniferous forest of the north.

53374.q: Which landscape lies to the north of the taiga?
53374.e: Further north it becomes too cold for trees. In the tundra only mosses, lichens, grasses and dwarf shrubs grow.
53374.m: North of the taiga lies the treeless tundra.

53375.q: Apart from Eurasia, on which continent are there also huge areas of taiga?
53375.e: The taiga stretches right around the north of the Earth. Apart from Russia and Scandinavia, it grows mainly in Canada and Alaska.
53375.m: There is also taiga in Canada and Alaska.

53376.q: Which natural event regularly renews the forests of the taiga in a natural way?
53376.e: In the taiga, fires are often started by lightning. Afterwards young trees grow back, and some pines even need fire for their seeds to sprout.
53376.m: Forest fires are part of the natural cycle of the taiga.

53377.q: Which small predator of the taiga was once much sought after for its valuable fur?
53377.e: The sable is a marten with especially soft fur. The hunt for sable furs was a strong driving force behind Russia's conquest of Siberia.
53377.m: The sable is a taiga marten with valuable fur.

53378.q: Which advantage helps evergreen conifers in the taiga?
a: They do not have to grow new leaves in spring.
They store water in their trunk like cacti.
53378.e: Because spruces and pines keep their needles, they can start photosynthesis straight away in the short summer. Deciduous trees would first have to grow new leaves.
53378.m: Conifers make use of the short summer because they keep their needles.

53379.q: What is the Kamchatka Peninsula especially famous for?
53379.e: Kamchatka lies on the Pacific Ring of Fire. The peninsula has over 160 volcanoes, about 29 of them active.
53379.m: Kamchatka is a land of volcanoes.

53380.q: Roughly how many active volcanoes are there on Kamchatka?
53380.e: Kamchatka has over 160 volcanoes, about 29 of them active. The highest is Klyuchevskaya Sopka at around 4750 metres.

53381.q: Which ocean lies to the east of the Kamchatka Peninsula?
53381.e: Kamchatka lies in the far east of Russia. To the east the peninsula borders the Pacific, to the west the Sea of Okhotsk.

53382.q: What is the famous valley on Kamchatka with around 90 hot spouting springs called?
53382.e: In the Valley of Geysers, fountains of hot water keep shooting out of the ground. It is one of the largest geyser fields in the world.
53382.m: In the Valley of Geysers hot water sprays out of the ground.

53383.q: What is special about the city of Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky?
a: It is not linked to the rest of Russia by road or rail
It is the capital of Russia
It lies in the middle of a desert
53383.e: Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky lies on a bay of the Pacific. You can only reach the city by plane or ship.
53383.m: You can only reach Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky by plane or ship.

53384.q: Which large predators catch salmon in Kamchatka's rivers in summer?
53384.e: A great many brown bears live on Kamchatka. In summer, salmon swim up the rivers and the bears fish them out of the water.
53384.m: Kamchatka's brown bears eat a lot of salmon in summer.

53385.q: Which country is the largest landlocked country in the world?
53385.e: Kazakhstan covers about 2.7 million km² and has no access to an ocean. This makes it the largest landlocked country on Earth.
53385.m: Kazakhstan is the largest country without a sea coast.

53386.q: With which neighbouring country does Kazakhstan share its longest border?
53386.e: The border between Kazakhstan and Russia is about 7500 kilometres long. It is one of the longest land borders in the world.
53386.m: Kazakhstan's longest border is with Russia.

53387.q: What is the name of the spaceport in Kazakhstan from which Yuri Gagarin launched into space in 1961?
53387.e: Baikonur is the oldest and largest rocket launch site in the world. Russia rents it from Kazakhstan.
53387.m: The first person in space launched from Baikonur in Kazakhstan.

53388.q: Which landscape covers large parts of Kazakhstan?
53388.e: A large part of Kazakhstan is wide, flat grassland. In the past this steppe was used mainly by nomads with their herds.
53388.m: Kazakhstan is a land of wide steppes.

53389.q: Which currency did people pay with in Kazakhstan when it was still part of the Soviet Union?
53389.e: Kazakhstan introduced the tenge as its own currency in 1993. Before that, people there paid with roubles, as in the whole Soviet Union.
53389.m: Today people in Kazakhstan pay with the tenge.

53390.q: Since which year has Kazakhstan been an independent country?
53390.e: Kazakhstan was a republic of the Soviet Union. When the Soviet Union broke up, it declared independence in December 1991.
53390.m: Kazakhstan has been independent since the break-up of the Soviet Union in 1991.

53391.q: Where in Kazakhstan are the high mountains?
a: In the north-west by the Caspian Sea
In the middle of the steppe
53391.e: The Tian Shan rises in the south-east of Kazakhstan. At its foot lies Almaty, the largest city in the country.
53391.m: There are high mountains in the south-east of Kazakhstan.

53392.q: What has happened to the Aral Sea since the 1960s?
a: It has been connected to the ocean.
53392.e: Since 1960 the Aral Sea has lost most of its area. It is considered one of the greatest environmental disasters caused by humans.
53392.m: Human activity has made most of the Aral Sea disappear.

53393.q: Where did the Aral Sea once get most of its water from?
a: From glaciers right on the shore
53393.e: The Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers brought water from the mountains of Central Asia. Today only a little of it reaches the lake.
53393.m: The Aral Sea depends on the water of two rivers.

53394.q: What was the water of the rivers feeding the Aral Sea mainly diverted for?
a: to supply Moscow with drinking water
53394.e: In Soviet times huge cotton fields were created and watered with river water. As a result, hardly any water flowed into the lake.
53394.m: The Aral Sea's water was taken away for cotton fields.

53395.q: Which two countries share the Aral Sea?
53395.e: The northern part of the Aral Sea belongs to Kazakhstan, the southern part to Uzbekistan.
53395.m: The Aral Sea lies between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.

53396.q: What did Kazakhstan build in 2005 to save the North Aral Sea?
53396.e: The Kok-Aral Dam holds back the water of the Syr Darya in the northern part. Since then the water level there has risen again and there are fish again.
53396.m: A dam has partly saved the North Aral Sea.

53397.q: What can you see today in the former port town of Moynaq on the Aral Sea?
a: rusty ships in the desert sand
an ice rink on the shore
53397.e: Moynaq used to lie on the shore; today the water is over 100 kilometres away. Old fishing boats lie in the sand in the “ship graveyard”.
53397.m: In Moynaq ships lie in the middle of the desert.

53398.q: What has formed on the dried-up bed of the Aral Sea?
53398.e: A new desert, the Aralkum, has formed on the former lake bed. The wind carries salty dust from there far across the land.
53398.m: Where the Aral Sea used to be, there is now desert.

53399.q: Which raw material is extracted in large quantities around and under the Caspian Sea?
53399.e: Around the Caspian Sea and beneath its bed lie large deposits of oil and natural gas. As early as the 19th century, a lot of oil was extracted near Baku.
53399.m: A lot of oil is extracted at the Caspian Sea.

53400.q: Which river supplies most of the water flowing into the Caspian Sea?
53400.e: The Volga is the longest river in Europe and flows into the Caspian Sea through a large delta. It brings about 80 per cent of the incoming water.
53400.m: The Volga is the most important river feeding the Caspian Sea.

53401.q: How many countries border the Caspian Sea?
53401.e: The countries on its shores are Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan.
53401.m: Five countries share the shores of the Caspian Sea.

53402.q: Where is the water level of the Caspian Sea compared with sea level?
53402.e: The Caspian Sea lies in a deep basin. Its water level is about 28 metres below sea level.
53402.m: The surface of the Caspian Sea is below sea level.

53403.q: Which capital city lies on the shore of the Caspian Sea?
53403.e: Baku is the capital of Azerbaijan and lies on a peninsula on the Caspian Sea. Its old town with the Palace of the Shirvanshahs is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
53403.m: Baku is the capital on the Caspian Sea.

53404.q: Which fish from the Caspian Sea are famous for their caviar?
53404.e: Caviar is the salted eggs of sturgeon. Because too many were caught, many kinds of sturgeon are now seriously endangered.

53405.q: Why is the water of the Caspian Sea slightly salty?
a: because it has no outflow and water evaporates
because it is connected to the Pacific underground
because factories pour salt into it
53405.e: A lake with no outflow only loses water through evaporation. The dissolved salts stay behind, so it has about a third of the saltiness of sea water.
53405.m: The Caspian Sea is salty because it has no outflow.

53406.q: Which regions did the Silk Road connect in ancient times and the Middle Ages?
53406.e: The Silk Road was a network of trade routes right across Asia. It connected China with the Mediterranean region.
53406.m: The Silk Road connected China with the Mediterranean.

53407.q: Why was Chinese silk so valuable in the West for a long time?
a: Only China knew the secret of how to make it
Silk grew only on high mountains
Silk could only be sold in winter
53407.e: Silk is made from the cocoons of the silkworm. China kept the method secret for a long time, so silk was rare and expensive in the West.
53407.m: China guarded the secret of silk for a long time.

53408.q: Which merchant from Venice travelled along the Silk Road all the way to China in the 13th century?
53408.e: Marco Polo travelled to China with his father and uncle and stayed there for many years. His travel account made Asia known in Europe.
53408.m: Marco Polo travelled to China along the Silk Road.

53409.q: In which old Chinese capital did the Silk Road traditionally begin?
53409.e: The city used to be called Chang'an and was the capital of several Chinese dynasties. From there the caravans set off westwards.
53409.m: The Silk Road began in the old imperial city of Xi'an.

53410.q: Which animals carried goods through deserts on the Silk Road?
53410.e: Bactrian camels with two humps can go a long time without water. In caravans they carried goods through deserts and steppes.
53410.m: Camel caravans carried goods along the Silk Road.

53411.q: Apart from goods, what else spread along the Silk Road?
53411.e: Ideas also travelled along the Silk Road. This is how Buddhism and papermaking spread from China and India to other countries.
53411.m: Religions and knowledge also spread along the Silk Road.

53412.q: What are the inns on the Silk Road where caravans stayed overnight called?
53412.e: Caravanserais were walled inns with a courtyard for the animals. They were about a day's journey apart.
53412.m: Silk Road merchants rested in caravanserais.

53413.q: In which country is the city of Samarkand?
53413.e: Samarkand lies in the south-east of Uzbekistan and is the country's second-largest city. The capital is Tashkent.
53413.m: Samarkand is a city in Uzbekistan.

53414.q: On which famous trade route between China and Europe did Samarkand lie?
53414.e: On the Silk Road, merchants brought silk, spices and other goods from China to the Mediterranean. Samarkand was an important stop.
53414.m: Samarkand lay on the Silk Road.

53415.q: Which religion shapes Samarkand's magnificent buildings with their mosques and madrasas?
53415.e: There are many mosques, madrasas and mausoleums in Samarkand. Many were built on the orders of the ruler Timur in the 14th century.
53415.m: Samarkand is an old Islamic city.

53416.q: What is a madrasa, like those in Samarkand?
53416.e: In a madrasa, students learnt religion, but often also mathematics and astronomy. They lived in cells around a courtyard.
53416.m: A madrasa is an Islamic place of learning.

53417.q: What did a ruler in Samarkand have built in the 15th century to study the stars?
53417.e: Ulugh Beg was a ruler and astronomer. His observatory was one of the most important of its time.
53417.m: There was a famous observatory in Samarkand.

53418.q: Which colour especially marks the domes and tiles of Samarkand's buildings?
53418.e: Many mosques, madrasas and mausoleums in Samarkand have turquoise and deep blue domes and mosaics. The colour is seen as typical of Timurid architecture.
53418.m: Blue domes are typical of Samarkand.

53419.q: Why did Samarkand become rich in the Middle Ages?
a: because it lay on the Silk Road
because it lay by the sea
because it had large gold mines
because it had a lot of oil
53419.e: Samarkand lay at a crossroads of important trade routes between China, Persia and India. Merchants brought goods and wealth to the city.
53419.m: Samarkand became rich through trade on the Silk Road.

53420.q: Which is the smallest US state by area?
53420.e: Rhode Island on the East Coast is the smallest state, with around 4000 square kilometres.
53420.m: Rhode Island is the smallest state in the USA.

53421.q: Which US state has the most inhabitants (as of 2024)?
53421.e: California has around 39 million inhabitants, making it the most populous state. Texas comes second.
53421.m: California is the state with the most people.

53422.q: Which city is the capital of Texas?
53422.e: The capital of Texas is Austin, even though Houston is the largest city in the state. In the USA, a state's capital is often not its largest city.
53422.m: Austin is the capital of Texas.

53423.q: Which city is the capital of California?
53423.e: Sacramento, inland, is the capital of California. The better-known cities of Los Angeles and San Francisco are big cities but not the seat of government.
53423.m: California's government is based in Sacramento.

53424.q: Which city is the capital of the state of New York?
53424.e: The capital of New York State is Albany on the Hudson River. New York City is the largest city, but not the seat of government.
53424.m: Albany is the capital of New York State.

53425.q: Which state has the nickname “Lone Star State”?
53425.e: Texas is called the “Lone Star State” because its flag shows a single star. It recalls the time when Texas was an independent republic from 1836 to 1845.
53425.m: Texas is the state with the lone star.

53426.q: What do the letters “D.C.” in Washington, D.C. stand for?
53426.e: “D.C.” means District of Columbia. The name recalls Christopher Columbus.
53426.m: Washington lies in the District of Columbia.

53427.q: Who is the capital Washington named after?
53427.e: The capital bears the name of George Washington, the first President of the USA. He also chose the site for the new capital.
53427.m: Washington, D.C. is named after the first president.

53428.q: Who lives and works in the White House in Washington, D.C.?
53428.e: The White House is the home and office of the American president. It has stood in the capital for over 200 years.
53428.m: The President of the USA lives in the White House.

53429.q: What status does Washington, D.C. have within the USA?
53429.e: Washington, D.C. is a federal district and does not belong to any state. This was so that the capital would not give any single state an advantage.
53429.m: Washington, D.C. is a federal district, not a state.

53430.q: Which structure in Washington is an obelisk about 170 metres tall?
53430.e: The Washington Monument is an obelisk about 169 metres tall in honour of George Washington. It was completed in 1884.
53430.m: The big obelisk in Washington is the Washington Monument.

53431.q: How many boroughs does New York City consist of?
53431.e: New York City consists of five boroughs: Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and Staten Island.
53431.m: New York City has five boroughs.

53432.q: Which river flows past the west side of Manhattan?
53432.e: The Hudson River flows past the west side of Manhattan and separates New York from New Jersey. On the east side is the East River, an arm of the sea.
53432.m: The Hudson flows west of Manhattan.

53433.q: What was New York called when it was a Dutch settlement?
53433.e: The Dutch founded the settlement of Nieuw Amsterdam in the 17th century. In 1664 the English took over the town and named it New York.
53433.m: New York used to be called Nieuw Amsterdam.

53434.q: In which state is Los Angeles?
53434.e: Los Angeles lies in southern California on the Pacific coast. It is the largest city in that state.
53434.m: Los Angeles is in southern California.

53435.q: What does the Spanish name “Los Angeles” mean in English?
53435.e: “Los Angeles” is Spanish and means “the angels”. The city was founded by Spaniards in 1781.

53436.q: With the 2028 Games, how many times will Los Angeles have hosted the Summer Olympics?
53436.e: Los Angeles was host in 1932 and 1984 and will be again in 2028. That makes three times.
53436.m: In 2028 Los Angeles will be an Olympic city for the third time.

53437.q: Which natural hazard especially threatens Los Angeles because of the San Andreas Fault?
53437.e: At the San Andreas Fault two tectonic plates grind past each other. This causes earthquakes again and again.
53437.m: The ground often shakes along the San Andreas Fault.

53438.q: By population, where does Los Angeles rank among US cities?
53438.e: Los Angeles has almost 3.9 million inhabitants and is the second-largest city in the USA after New York City. Chicago comes third.
53438.m: Los Angeles is the second-largest city in the USA.

53439.q: In which direction do the Rocky Mountains run?
a: In a circle around a basin
53439.e: The Rocky Mountains stretch from Canada in the north to New Mexico in the south. They are the most important mountain range in western North America.
53439.m: The Rocky Mountains run from north to south.

53440.q: Roughly how high are the highest peaks of the Rocky Mountains?
53440.e: The highest peak is Mount Elbert in Colorado at 4401 metres. It is a little lower than the Dom in Valais at 4545 metres.
53440.m: The highest Rockies are about as high as high peaks in Valais.

53441.q: The Continental Divide runs along the Rocky Mountains. What does it separate?
a: Rivers flowing to the Pacific from rivers flowing to the Atlantic
The north of the USA from the south
53441.e: West of the divide, water flows into the Pacific; east of it, into the Atlantic or the Gulf of Mexico. Switzerland also has such divides, for example at the Gotthard.
53441.m: The Continental Divide separates rivers flowing to two oceans.

53442.q: Roughly how long are the Rocky Mountains?
53442.e: The Rocky Mountains stretch for about 4800 kilometres. That is about four times as long as the arc of the Alps, which is about 1200 kilometres long.
53442.m: The Rocky Mountains are about 4800 kilometres long.

53443.q: In which country is the northern part of the Rocky Mountains?
53443.e: The Rocky Mountains reach far into Canada, for example into the provinces of Alberta and British Columbia. Well-known national parks such as Banff and Jasper are there.
53443.m: The Rocky Mountains are in the USA and Canada.

53444.q: Which big city at the foot of the Rocky Mountains is called the “Mile High City” because it lies about 1600 metres up?
53444.e: Denver in Colorado lies about one mile, or roughly 1609 metres, above sea level. Hence the nickname “Mile High City”.
53444.m: Denver lies one mile above sea level.

53445.q: About how long ago did the Rocky Mountains begin to fold up?
53445.e: The Rocky Mountains were folded up about 80 to 55 million years ago. This mountain building is called the Laramide orogeny.
53445.m: The Rocky Mountains formed about 80 million years ago.

53446.q: In which part of the USA does the Mississippi rise?
a: In the south on the Gulf of Mexico
53446.e: The Mississippi begins as a small stream at Lake Itasca in the state of Minnesota in the north of the USA. From there it flows south to the Gulf of Mexico.
53446.m: The Mississippi flows from north to south through the USA.

53447.q: Roughly how long is the Mississippi?
53447.e: The Mississippi is about 3780 kilometres long. The Rhine, at about 1230 kilometres, is only about a third as long.
53447.m: The Mississippi is almost 3800 kilometres long.

53448.q: Roughly how long is the Grand Canyon?
53448.e: The gorge is about 450 kilometres long. If you want to drive from the South Rim to the North Rim, you have to drive about 350 kilometres around the gorge.
53448.m: The Grand Canyon is about 450 kilometres long.

53449.q: Why is the Grand Canyon so valuable for geology?
a: Its rock layers show almost 2 billion years of Earth's history
It is the only place with volcanic rock
The first oil was found there
It contains the oldest glaciers in the world
53449.e: In the walls of the canyon, many rock layers lie on top of each other. The lowest are almost two billion years old.
53449.m: The rock walls of the Grand Canyon are like a book of Earth's history.

53450.q: Which famous list was the Grand Canyon added to in 1979?
