53450.e: The Grand Canyon was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1979. From Switzerland, for example, the Old City of Bern has been on it since 1983.
53450.m: The Grand Canyon has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979.

53451.q: Roughly how much of the fresh water on the Earth's surface do the Great Lakes contain?
53451.e: The Great Lakes contain about 20 per cent of the fresh water in the Earth's lakes and rivers. Only Lake Baikal holds a similar amount of water.
53451.m: The Great Lakes hold about a fifth of the Earth's surface fresh water.

53452.q: In which US state are Niagara Falls?
53452.e: The American side of Niagara Falls belongs to the state of New York. The nearby city is also called Niagara Falls.
53452.m: Niagara Falls are in the state of New York.

53453.q: What is a large part of the Niagara's water diverted for before the falls?
a: For New York City's drinking water
53453.e: A large part of the water flows through tunnels to hydroelectric power stations in the USA and Canada. At night and in winter more water is diverted.
53453.m: The water of the Niagara River supplies a lot of electricity.

53454.q: Why are Niagara Falls slowly moving upstream?
a: The water wears away soft rock under the hard edge
Tectonic plates push the falls south
The lakes get bigger every year
People move the edge of the falls
53454.e: Under a hard layer of dolomite rock lies softer rock that is washed away. Then the edge breaks off and the falls move upstream.
53454.m: Erosion makes Niagara Falls move upstream.

53455.q: Why does the hot spring “Grand Prismatic Spring” glow in such bright colours?
a: Because of microorganisms in the warm water
Because of lamps on the bottom
53455.e: Around the edge of the spring live bacteria and other microorganisms that are yellow, orange or red depending on the water temperature. In the hot centre the water is deep blue.
53455.m: Microorganisms colour the springs in Yellowstone.

53456.q: In which year did Alaska become a US state?
53456.e: Alaska became the 49th state in January 1959. Before that it was a US territory.

53457.q: Which number US state did Hawaii become in 1959?
53457.e: Hawaii was admitted in August 1959 as the 50th and so far last state. Since then the US flag has had 50 stars.
53457.m: Hawaii is the newest state in the USA.

53458.q: Which city is the capital of Hawaii?
53458.e: Honolulu lies on the island of Oʻahu and is Hawaii's largest city. The famous Waikīkī beach is also there.
53458.m: Honolulu is the capital of Hawaii.

53459.q: Which sport has its roots in Hawaii?
53459.e: People in Hawaii were riding the waves on boards centuries ago. From there surfing spread all over the world.

53460.q: What is special about Badwater Basin in Death Valley?
a: It is the lowest point in North America
It is the highest mountain in North America
It is the largest lake in North America
53460.e: Badwater Basin lies 86 metres below sea level. It is the lowest point in North America.
53460.m: Badwater Basin is the lowest point in North America.

53461.q: Which record does Death Valley hold?
a: Highest air temperature ever recorded on Earth
Lowest temperature ever recorded on Earth
53461.e: In 1913 a temperature of 56.7 °C was measured in Death Valley. It is officially considered the highest air temperature ever recorded on Earth.
53461.m: The highest air temperature on Earth was recorded in Death Valley.

53462.q: In which state does most of Death Valley lie?
53462.e: Death Valley lies in eastern California; a small part of the national park reaches into Nevada. It is the largest national park outside Alaska.

53463.q: Why is it so hot and dry in Death Valley?
a: It lies low and in the rain shadow of high mountains
It lies right on the equator
The wind blows warm sea air into it
53463.e: High mountains to the west keep the rain clouds away; this is called a rain shadow. In addition, hot air gets trapped in the deep, narrow valley.
53463.m: The rain shadow makes Death Valley very dry.

53464.q: How do the “sailing stones” on the Racetrack Playa in Death Valley move?
a: Thin sheets of ice are pushed by the wind and take the stones with them
Animals roll the stones around at night
53464.e: In 2014 researchers observed that thin sheets of ice form after cold nights. A light wind pushes the ice, and with it the stones, across the wet ground.
53464.m: Ice and wind make the stones in Death Valley move.

53465.q: Which desert does Death Valley belong to?
53465.e: Death Valley lies in the north of the Mojave Desert. This desert stretches across parts of California, Nevada, Utah and Arizona.
53465.m: Death Valley lies in the Mojave Desert.

53466.q: From which place in Florida do many NASA rockets launch?
53466.e: The launch sites, such as the Kennedy Space Center, are at Cape Canaveral and on neighbouring Merritt Island. The Apollo missions to the Moon, among others, launched from there.
53466.m: Many rockets launch from Cape Canaveral in Florida.

53467.q: Near which city in Florida is the famous Walt Disney World theme park?
53467.e: Walt Disney World lies near Orlando in central Florida. The capital of Florida, however, is Tallahassee.
53467.m: Walt Disney World is near Orlando in Florida.

53468.q: Between which bodies of water does the Florida peninsula lie?
a: The Atlantic and the Gulf of Mexico
The Pacific and the Gulf of California
53468.e: Florida juts south into the sea as a peninsula. To the east is the Atlantic, to the west the Gulf of Mexico.
53468.m: Florida lies between the Atlantic and the Gulf of Mexico.

53469.q: What is the chain of islands in southern Florida that reaches as far as Key West called?
53469.e: The Florida Keys are a long chain of small islands. A road with many bridges links them all the way to Key West, the southernmost city of the 48 connected states.
53469.m: The Florida Keys reach as far as Key West.

53470.q: What are the Everglades in Florida?
a: A coral reef off the coast
53470.e: The Everglades are a huge wetland in southern Florida. They are home to many rare animals and plants.
53470.m: The Everglades are a huge wetland in Florida.

53471.q: Which two crocodilians live together in the Everglades, which hardly happens anywhere else?
53471.e: In the Everglades the American alligator from fresh water meets the American crocodile from salt water. South Florida is considered the only place in the world where both live together.
53471.m: Alligators and crocodiles live together in the Everglades.

53472.q: Which introduced animal is a big problem in the Everglades today?
53472.e: Burmese pythons from South-East Asia were released by pet owners and are multiplying rapidly in the Everglades. They eat many native mammals and birds.
53472.m: The introduced Burmese python threatens the animals of the Everglades.

53473.q: How is part of the Everglades protected today?
a: It is fenced off and forbidden
53473.e: Everglades National Park was founded in 1947. It protects the southern part of the wetland.
53473.m: Part of the Everglades is a national park.

53474.q: How many US states border Mexico?
53474.e: California, Arizona, New Mexico and Texas border Mexico. The border is about 3100 kilometres long.

53475.q: Which US state borders Canada but is separated from the rest of the country?
53475.e: Alaska lies in the north-west of America. Canada lies between Alaska and the other states.
53475.m: Alaska is separated from the rest of the USA by Canada.

53476.q: What is special about the “Four Corners” point in the USA?
a: Four states meet at one point there
A tower with four corners stands there
53476.e: At the Four Corners, Utah, Colorado, Arizona and New Mexico meet at right angles. You can stand in four states at the same time there.
53476.m: At the Four Corners you can stand in four states at once.

53477.q: Which state consists of two large peninsulas between the Great Lakes?
53477.e: Michigan consists of the Lower and Upper Peninsulas. The Mackinac Bridge connects the two parts.

53478.q: What is the long green space in Washington between the Capitol and the Lincoln Memorial called?
53478.e: The National Mall is a long park with many monuments and museums. Big rallies and celebrations often take place there.
53478.m: The National Mall is the big green space in the centre of Washington.

53479.q: In which building in Washington, D.C. does the US parliament meet?
53479.e: Congress, the parliament of the USA, works in the Capitol with its large dome. The White House, on the other hand, is the seat of the president.
53479.m: The US parliament meets in the Capitol.

53480.q: Which organisation runs many museums in Washington that you can visit for free?
53480.e: The Smithsonian Institution runs numerous museums in Washington, such as the Air and Space Museum. Entry is free.
53480.m: The Smithsonian Institution's museums are free to enter.

53481.q: Which street in Manhattan is a symbol of the financial world all over the globe?
53481.e: The New York Stock Exchange is on Wall Street. The street's name is often used for the whole US financial industry.
53481.m: Wall Street stands for the financial world.

53482.q: What is New York City's nickname?
53482.e: New York is often called “The Big Apple”. “Windy City”, on the other hand, is Chicago and “Big Easy” is New Orleans.
53482.m: New York City is also called the Big Apple.

53483.q: Which street in New York is famous for its theatres and musicals?
53483.e: Many big theatres are on Broadway in Manhattan. That is why “Broadway musical” is a world-famous term.
53483.m: Broadway is New York's theatre district.

53484.q: Roughly how many inhabitants did New York City have in the 2020 census?
53484.e: In the 2020 census New York City had about 8.8 million inhabitants. That is about as many as the whole of Switzerland.
53484.m: New York City has about as many inhabitants as Switzerland.

53485.q: What is the name of New York City's largest airport, in the borough of Queens?
53485.e: John F. Kennedy International Airport, JFK for short, is the city's most important international airport. Flights from Zurich land there too.
53485.m: New York's largest airport is called JFK.

53486.q: What climate does Los Angeles have?
53486.e: Los Angeles has a Mediterranean climate. The summers are warm and dry, and most of the rain falls in winter.
53486.m: Los Angeles has a mild Mediterranean climate.

53487.q: Which environmental problem is made worse by Los Angeles lying in a basin between mountains?
53487.e: The mountains around the basin trap the exhaust fumes from all the traffic. In sunshine, this turns into smog.
53487.m: Lying in a basin encourages smog in Los Angeles.

53488.q: Into which sea does the Mississippi flow?
53488.e: The Mississippi flows into the Gulf of Mexico south of New Orleans. The Gulf is part of the Atlantic.
53488.m: The Mississippi flows into the Gulf of Mexico.

53489.q: Near which city does the Missouri flow into the Mississippi?
53489.e: The Missouri joins the Mississippi just above St. Louis. The city is famous for the huge Gateway Arch.
53489.m: The Missouri and Mississippi meet near St. Louis.

53490.q: What is the shape of the Mississippi's mouth, with its many channels, called?
53490.e: The Mississippi drops a lot of mud at its mouth and forms many channels. From above, the delta looks like a bird's foot.
53490.m: The Mississippi has a bird's-foot delta.

53491.q: Roughly what share of the area of the USA do the Mississippi and its tributaries drain?
53491.e: The Mississippi's catchment area covers about 40 per cent of the area of the USA (not counting Alaska and Hawaii). It stretches from the Rocky Mountains to the Appalachians.
53491.m: The Mississippi drains about two fifths of the USA.

53492.q: Roughly how wide is the Grand Canyon at its widest point?
53492.e: At its widest point the Grand Canyon is about 29 kilometres wide. That is roughly the length of Lake Zurich from Zurich to Rapperswil.
53492.m: The Grand Canyon is up to 29 kilometres wide.

53493.q: Which rim of the Grand Canyon is usually closed to visitors in winter because of snow?
53493.e: The North Rim lies about 2500 metres high, higher than the South Rim. In winter the access road is closed because of snow.
53493.m: The North Rim of the Grand Canyon is closed in winter.

53494.q: Which river carved out the Grand Canyon?
53494.e: Over millions of years the Colorado River has cut deep into the rock. Above the canyon it is dammed to form the reservoir Lake Powell.
53494.m: The Colorado River shaped the Grand Canyon.

53495.q: How do you reach the village of Supai, deep in a side canyon of the Grand Canyon?
a: Only on foot, with mules or by helicopter
53495.e: The Havasupai people have lived in the village of Supai for centuries. No road leads down there, so mules even deliver the post.
53495.m: You can only reach Supai in the Grand Canyon on foot, with mules or by helicopter.

53496.q: Which of the Great Lakes has the smallest area?
53496.e: Lake Ontario has the smallest area of the five lakes. Because it is deep, however, it holds more water than Lake Erie.
53496.m: Lake Ontario is the smallest of the Great Lakes.

53497.q: Which of the Great Lakes is the shallowest?
53497.e: Lake Erie is on average only about 19 metres deep. That is why it warms up quickly in summer and often freezes over in winter.
53497.m: Lake Erie is the shallowest of the Great Lakes.

53498.q: Which English memory word helps you remember the names of the five Great Lakes?
53498.e: The letters of HOMES stand for Huron, Ontario, Michigan, Erie and Superior.
53498.m: The word HOMES helps you remember the Great Lakes.

53499.q: How were the basins of the Great Lakes formed?
a: Ice Age glaciers scoured them out
53499.e: In the last Ice Age, huge glaciers scoured the basins deep. When the ice melted, they filled with water.
53499.m: Ice Age glaciers shaped the Great Lakes.

53500.q: Which two Great Lakes are connected by the Straits of Mackinac and lie at the same level?
53500.e: The Straits of Mackinac are so wide that Lake Michigan and Lake Huron have the same water level. For experts, they are therefore really a single lake.
53500.m: Lake Michigan and Lake Huron are really a single lake.

53501.q: In which Canadian province are Niagara Falls?
53501.e: The Canadian side of the falls belongs to the province of Ontario. There is also a city called Niagara Falls there.
53501.m: On the Canadian side, Niagara Falls are in Ontario.

53502.q: How do ships get from Lake Erie to Lake Ontario without going over Niagara Falls?
a: Through a tunnel under the falls
With a crane over the falls
On a detour via the Hudson River
53502.e: The Welland Canal in Canada connects Lake Erie with Lake Ontario. Using several locks, ships overcome the difference in height.
53502.m: Ships get round Niagara Falls through the Welland Canal.

53503.q: What did engineers do to the American Falls in 1969?
a: They dried up the falls with a dam for months
They built a glass dome over them
They blew up the edge of the falls
53503.e: In 1969 engineers dammed the water above the American Falls for a few months. This let them examine the rocks and check how stable they are.
53503.m: The American Falls were dry for a few months in 1969.

53504.q: What does the name “Yellowstone” refer to?
53504.e: The name goes back to the yellowish rocks along the Yellowstone River. French fur traders called the river “Roche Jaune”.

53505.q: What lies beneath Yellowstone National Park and heats its hot springs and geysers?
53505.e: Beneath Yellowstone lies a so-called supervolcano. Its heat warms the groundwater, which is why there are so many hot springs and geysers there.
53505.m: A volcano under Yellowstone heats the springs and geysers.

53506.q: What was Yellowstone National Park when it was founded in 1872?
53506.e: Yellowstone was founded in the USA in 1872 and is considered the world's first national park. The Swiss National Park followed in 1914.
53506.m: Yellowstone is the world's first national park.

53507.q: Roughly how big is Yellowstone National Park?
53507.e: The park covers about 9000 square kilometres. That is more than fifty times the size of the Swiss National Park, at about 170 square kilometres.
53507.m: Yellowstone National Park covers about 9000 square kilometres.

53508.q: White terraces grow at Mammoth Hot Springs in Yellowstone. What does the hot water deposit there?
53508.e: The hot spring water contains dissolved limestone. In the air it deposits it, and so step-like white terraces grow.
53508.m: At Mammoth Hot Springs, limestone forms white terraces.

53509.q: Which is the largest city in Alaska?
53509.e: About 40 per cent of Alaska's population lives in Anchorage. But it is not the capital.
53509.m: Anchorage is the largest city in Alaska.

53510.q: What does the Trans-Alaska Pipeline, about 1300 kilometres long, carry?
53510.e: The Trans-Alaska Pipeline carries oil from Prudhoe Bay in the north to the port of Valdez in the south. It started operating in 1977.

53511.q: What happens in winter in Alaska's northernmost town on the Arctic Ocean?
a: The sun does not rise for about two months
It gets as hot as in the desert
There is always a full moon
53511.e: The town of Utqiaġvik lies far north of the Arctic Circle. In winter the sun stays below the horizon there for about two months; this is called the polar night.
53511.m: In the far north there is the polar night in winter.

53512.q: Roughly how many inhabitants does Alaska have (as of 2024)?
53512.e: Alaska has only about 740,000 inhabitants, even though it is huge. This makes it one of the most thinly populated states.
53512.m: Fewer people live in Alaska than in the canton of Bern.

53513.q: What is the longest river in Alaska called?
53513.e: The Yukon rises in Canada and flows right across Alaska into the Bering Sea. It is about 3200 kilometres long.
53513.m: The Yukon is the longest river in Alaska.

53514.q: How many main islands does Hawaii consist of?
53514.e: Hawaii has eight main islands, including Hawaii, Maui, Oʻahu and Kauaʻi. There are also many small islands and atolls.

53515.q: What is the largest island of Hawaii called?
53515.e: The largest island has the same name as the whole state of Hawaii. That is why it is often called the “Big Island”.
53515.m: Hawaii's largest island is called the Big Island.

53516.q: What is the garland of flowers that people in Hawaii put around guests' necks to welcome them called?
53516.e: A lei is a garland of flowers, leaves or shells. It is a sign of friendship and welcome.
53516.m: A lei is a Hawaiian flower garland.

53517.q: What was Hawaii before it became part of the USA?
53517.e: King Kamehameha I united the islands into the Kingdom of Hawaii around 1810. The kingdom lasted until 1893; later Hawaii became part of the USA.
53517.m: Hawaii used to be a kingdom.

53518.q: Where do the Everglades mainly get their water from?
a: From rain and a large lake in the north
53518.e: In the past, water flowed slowly and widely south from Lake Okeechobee through the Everglades. There is also a lot of rain in summer.
53518.m: Rain and a large lake supply the Everglades with water.

53519.q: Which nickname does Florida have because of its weather?
53519.e: Florida is called the “Sunshine State” because the sun shines a lot there. The “Golden State” is California.

53520.q: Where does Canada rank among the largest countries in the world by area?
53520.e: With almost 10 million km², Canada is the second-largest country on Earth after Russia. That makes it about 240 times the size of Switzerland.
53520.m: Canada is the second-largest country in the world.

53521.q: Which three oceans does Canada border?
53521.e: Canada has coasts on the Atlantic in the east, the Pacific in the west and the Arctic Ocean in the north. The country's motto is “From sea to sea”.

53522.q: Which two languages do you hear especially often in the capital, Ottawa?
53522.e: Canada has two official languages: English and French. Ottawa lies on the border with French-speaking Québec.
53522.m: In Ottawa people speak English and French.

53523.q: Which French-speaking province does the city of Ottawa border directly?
53523.e: Ottawa lies in Ontario on the Ottawa River. On the other side of the river begins the province of Québec, where most people speak French.
53523.m: Ottawa lies on the border with Québec.

53524.q: Which canal in Ottawa becomes a long skating rink in winter and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
53524.e: The Rideau Canal links Ottawa with Kingston on Lake Ontario and has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2007. In winter it freezes over and becomes an ice rink kilometres long in the middle of the city.
53524.m: In winter you can skate through Ottawa on the Rideau Canal.

53525.q: How many provinces and territories does Canada consist of?
53525.e: Canada is divided into 10 provinces and 3 territories. The territories Yukon, Northwest Territories and Nunavut lie in the thinly populated north.
53525.m: Canada has ten provinces and three territories.

53526.q: Which is Canada's largest province by area?
53526.e: With about 1.5 million km², Québec is Canada's largest province. Only the territory of Nunavut is even bigger.

53527.q: In which Canadian province do the most people live?
53527.e: Almost 40 per cent of Canada's population lives in Ontario. The largest city, Toronto, and the capital, Ottawa, are there.
53527.m: Ontario is Canada's most populous province.

53528.q: Which large island in the Atlantic belongs to Canada?
53528.e: Newfoundland lies off Canada's east coast. Together with Labrador on the mainland it forms a province.

53529.q: Which Canadian territory was created in 1999 as a homeland for the Inuit?
53529.e: Nunavut was split off from the Northwest Territories in 1999. In the Inuktitut language its name means “our land”, and most of its inhabitants are Inuit.
53529.m: Nunavut is Canada's newest territory and home to many Inuit.

53530.e: Prince Edward Island in the Gulf of St Lawrence is Canada's smallest province by area. It is smaller than the canton of the Grisons.
53530.m: Prince Edward Island is Canada's smallest province.

53531.q: Which three provinces are called the Prairie Provinces in Canada?
53531.e: Alberta, Saskatchewan and Manitoba lie on the flat prairie in the middle of Canada. A lot of wheat and rapeseed is grown there.
53531.m: The Prairie Provinces of Alberta, Saskatchewan and Manitoba are Canada's breadbasket.

53532.q: In which Canadian province do most people speak French?
53532.e: Québec was settled by the French. To this day French is the most important language there.
53532.m: In Québec people mainly speak French.

53533.q: On which lake does Toronto lie?
53533.e: Toronto lies on the northern shore of Lake Ontario, one of the five Great Lakes. Off the city centre lie the car-free Toronto Islands.

53534.q: Which basketball team from Toronto became the first team from outside the USA to win the NBA championship, in 2019?
53534.e: The Toronto Raptors became NBA champions in 2019. They are the only Canadian team in the North American professional basketball league.
53534.m: The Toronto Raptors brought the NBA title to Canada in 2019.

53535.q: What is the TV tower, about 553 m tall, that is Toronto's landmark called?
53535.e: The CN Tower opened in 1976 and was the tallest free-standing structure in the world for over 30 years. From the viewing platform you can see far across Lake Ontario.
53535.m: The CN Tower is Toronto's landmark.

53536.q: Which sport's hall of fame is in Toronto?
53536.e: The Hockey Hall of Fame, the museum of ice hockey, is in Toronto. The famous Stanley Cup is also displayed there when it is not with the winning team.
53536.m: Toronto is home to the Hockey Hall of Fame.

53537.q: What is Toronto the capital of?
53537.e: Toronto is the capital of the province of Ontario, but not the capital of Canada. The provincial parliament meets here.
53537.m: Toronto is the provincial capital of Ontario.

53538.q: What is Toronto especially known for regarding its population?
a: A great many inhabitants were born abroad
The city has hardly any immigration
53538.e: Toronto is considered one of the most multicultural cities in the world. About half of its inhabitants were born outside Canada, and over 150 languages are spoken.
53538.m: In Toronto people from all over the world live together.

53539.q: Which famous waterfall is only about 130 km from Toronto?
53539.e: Niagara Falls lie on the border between Canada and the USA, between Lake Erie and Lake Ontario. From Toronto you can reach them by car in about an hour and a half.
53539.m: Niagara Falls are a popular trip from Toronto.

53540.q: In which Canadian province is Vancouver?
53540.e: Vancouver lies in the south-west of the province of British Columbia on the Pacific coast. It is the largest city in that province.
53540.m: Vancouver lies in British Columbia on the Pacific.

53541.q: Which Olympic Games took place in Vancouver in 2010?
53541.e: Vancouver hosted the Winter Olympics in 2010; the skiing events took place in Whistler. Canada won more gold medals than any other nation.
53541.m: Vancouver was a Winter Olympic city in 2010.

53542.q: Which city, not Vancouver, is the capital of British Columbia?
53542.e: The capital of British Columbia is Victoria on Vancouver Island. Vancouver is much bigger, but it is not the seat of the provincial government.
53542.m: Victoria, not Vancouver, is the capital of British Columbia.

53543.q: Which large city park with old rainforest lies on a peninsula in Vancouver?
53543.e: Stanley Park covers over 400 hectares and is bigger than Central Park in New York. A waterside path, the Seawall, runs all the way round the park.
53543.m: Stanley Park is Vancouver's green lung.

53544.q: Who is the city of Vancouver named after?
53544.e: The city bears the name of the British captain George Vancouver. He explored and mapped the Pacific coast of North America around 1792.
53544.m: Vancouver is named after a British seafarer.

53545.q: What is Vancouver's main economic importance?
a: The largest coal mine in the world
53545.e: The Port of Vancouver is the largest and busiest port in Canada. A large part of the trade with Asia passes through it.
53545.m: Vancouver is Canada's gateway to the Pacific and Asia.

53546.q: What is the climate in Vancouver like compared with the rest of Canada?
53546.e: Thanks to the Pacific, Vancouver has mild winters with little snow but a lot of rain. This makes it one of Canada's warmest big cities in winter.
53546.m: Vancouver has a mild but rainy maritime climate.

a: A very old base of rock
A coat of arms on the Canadian flag
A young fold mountain range in the west
53547.e: The Canadian Shield is a huge area of ancient Precambrian rock, some of it over 2.5 billion years old. It forms the geological core of North America.
53547.m: The Canadian Shield is Canada's ancient rock foundation.

53548.q: Roughly how much of Canada's area does the Canadian Shield cover?
53548.e: The Canadian Shield covers roughly half of Canada. It stretches from Labrador in the east to the Northwest Territories.
53548.m: About half of Canada lies on the Canadian Shield.

53549.q: Around which body of water does the Canadian Shield wrap like a horseshoe?
53549.e: The Canadian Shield surrounds Hudson Bay in a large arc. The bay lies in a hollow in the middle of the shield.
53549.m: Hudson Bay lies in the middle of the Canadian Shield.

53550.q: Why are there countless lakes on the Canadian Shield?
a: Ice Age glaciers ground out hollows
53550.e: In the last Ice Age, mighty glaciers ground down the hard rock and left behind many hollows. Later, meltwater and rainwater collected in them.
53550.m: The many lakes on the Canadian Shield date from the Ice Age.

53551.q: Why is the Canadian Shield so important for mining?
a: It contains many ores such as nickel and gold
It is made of fertile farmland
53551.e: The shield's old rock holds rich deposits of nickel, gold, copper, iron and uranium. Mining near Sudbury in Ontario, for example, is well known.
53551.m: The Canadian Shield is rich in mineral resources.

53552.q: Why is there hardly any farming on the Canadian Shield?
a: The soils are thin and stony
It is too hot and dry there
The area lies under the sea
53552.e: The Ice Age glaciers scraped away most of the soil, so there is often only a thin layer of earth over the rock. On top of that come the cold climate and many swamps.
53552.m: Forests grow better than crops on the stony Canadian Shield.

53553.q: Which vegetation covers large parts of the Canadian Shield?
53553.e: In the south of the shield grows boreal coniferous forest with spruces, pines and birches. Further north it gives way to treeless tundra.
53553.m: Boreal coniferous forest grows mainly on the Canadian Shield.

53554.q: Who is Hudson Bay named after?
a: The Hudson River in New York
53554.e: The English seafarer Henry Hudson explored the bay in 1610 while searching for a sea route to Asia. After a mutiny he was set adrift there in 1611 and was never seen again.
53554.m: Hudson Bay bears the name of Henry Hudson.

53555.q: Through which strait is Hudson Bay connected to the Atlantic?
53555.e: The Hudson Strait between Baffin Island and Québec connects Hudson Bay with the Atlantic. The first European ships came into the bay through it.
53555.m: The Hudson Strait is Hudson Bay's gateway to the Atlantic.

53556.q: Which company was founded in 1670 for the fur trade around Hudson Bay?
53556.e: In 1670 the Hudson's Bay Company received from the English king the right to trade in the whole area draining into the bay. It mainly traded beaver furs with Indigenous peoples.
53556.m: For centuries the Hudson's Bay Company was one of Canada's most important trading businesses.

53557.q: Which animals wait on Hudson Bay in autumn for the sea to freeze?
53557.e: Polar bears hunt seals on the sea ice. In autumn many of them wait on the coast, for example near the town of Churchill, until the bay freezes over.
53557.m: In autumn many polar bears wait on Hudson Bay for the ice.

53558.q: What happens to Hudson Bay in winter?
53558.e: In winter Hudson Bay is almost completely covered in ice. In summer the ice melts again, so ships can only sail for a few months a year.
53558.m: Hudson Bay is almost completely frozen in winter.

53559.q: In which country is Hudson Bay?
53559.e: Hudson Bay is a huge inland sea in northern Canada. It is about 30 times the size of Switzerland.

53560.q: What kind of body of water is Hudson Bay?
a: A large inland sea with salt water
53560.e: Hudson Bay is a huge, shallow inland sea with salt water, connected to the Atlantic and the Arctic Ocean. It is about 30 times the size of Switzerland.
53560.m: Hudson Bay is an inland sea in northern Canada.

53561.q: Roughly how long is the St Lawrence River from Lake Ontario to the gulf?
53561.e: From where it leaves Lake Ontario to its mouth, the St Lawrence River is about 1200 km long. That is about as long as the Rhine.
53561.m: The St Lawrence River is about as long as the Rhine.

53562.q: Which two large cities lie on the St Lawrence River?
53562.e: Montreal lies on an island in the St Lawrence River, and Québec City on a rock on its bank. Both cities grew up thanks to their position on this important waterway.
53562.m: Montreal and Québec are the large cities on the St Lawrence River.

53563.q: Which language do most people speak in Québec on the St Lawrence River?
53563.e: French explorers such as Jacques Cartier reached the river as early as 1535. That is why people in the province of Québec still mainly speak French today.

53564.q: What does the St Lawrence Seaway, opened in 1959, make possible?
a: Ocean-going ships can sail into the Great Lakes
Trains can travel under the river
Planes can land on the river
53564.e: With locks and canals, the seaway gets past the rapids and differences in height. This lets large ships travel from the Atlantic all the way to Chicago or Duluth.
53564.m: Thanks to the St Lawrence Seaway, ocean-going ships reach deep into North America.

53565.q: Which white whales live in the mouth of the St Lawrence River?
53565.e: The southernmost beluga population in the world lives in the mouth of the St Lawrence River. You can watch the white whales near Tadoussac, for example.
53565.m: You can see white beluga whales in the St Lawrence River.

53566.q: What is the group of islands where the St Lawrence River leaves Lake Ontario called?
53566.e: The Thousand Islands are over 1800 small islands in the St Lawrence River on the border between Canada and the USA. They are a popular holiday and boating area.
53566.m: The Thousand Islands lie in the St Lawrence River.

53567.q: Into which body of sea does the St Lawrence River flow?
a: Into the Gulf of St Lawrence
53567.e: The river becomes wider and wider towards the east and opens into the Gulf of St Lawrence. The gulf is connected to the open Atlantic.
53567.m: The St Lawrence River flows into the Gulf of St Lawrence on the Atlantic.

53568.e: With about 507,000 km², Baffin Island is Canada's largest island and the fifth-largest in the world. It belongs to the territory of Nunavut.
53568.m: Baffin Island is Canada's largest island.

53569.q: What is the climate like on the islands in Canada's far north?
53569.e: The islands of the Canadian Arctic Archipelago, such as Victoria Island, lie north of the Arctic Circle. It is cold there almost all year round.
53569.m: It is very cold in Canada's far north.

53570.q: What was the British Franklin expedition looking for in the Canadian Arctic from 1845?
a: A sea route through the Arctic
53570.e: John Franklin and 129 men searched for a sea route through the Arctic islands, but nobody came back. The wrecks of the ships were only found in 2014 and 2016.
53570.m: The Franklin expedition was lost in the Canadian Arctic.

53571.q: Which country is Canada's northernmost island closest to?
53571.e: Ellesmere Island lies in the far north of Canada, separated from Greenland only by a narrow strait.
53571.m: Canada's northernmost island lies close to Greenland.

53572.q: Which people mainly live in the Canadian territory of Nunavut?
53572.e: Most people in Nunavut are Inuit. The capital, Iqaluit, lies on Baffin Island.

53573.q: Which large hoofed animal with long, shaggy fur lives on many islands of the Canadian Arctic Archipelago?
53573.e: With long outer hair and a thick woolly undercoat, musk oxen are well protected against the Arctic cold. Particularly many live on Banks Island in the west of the archipelago.
53573.m: The musk ox is adapted to the cold of the Arctic.

53574.q: Roughly how many islands does the Canadian Arctic Archipelago have?
53574.e: The archipelago consists of over 36,000 islands with a total area of about 1.4 million km². Only very few of the islands are inhabited.
53574.m: The Canadian Arctic Archipelago is made up of tens of thousands of islands.

53575.q: Which big sporting event took place in Mexico City in 1968?
53575.e: In 1968 Mexico City became the first city in Latin America to host the Olympic Games. Because of the thin air at high altitude, there were especially good results in sprinting and jumping.
53575.m: Mexico City hosted the Summer Olympics in 1968.

53576.q: Which people built the city on whose ruins Mexico City stands?
53576.e: In the 14th century the Aztecs founded the city of Tenochtitlan on an island in Lake Texcoco. The Spanish destroyed it and built Mexico City on top.
53576.m: Mexico City stands on the old Aztec city of Tenochtitlan.

53577.q: Why does the ground in Mexico City sink a little every year?
a: The city stands on a drained lake
The city lies on a glacier
The city stands on sand dunes
The city lies below sea level
53577.e: Mexico City was built on the soft ground of former Lake Texcoco. Because a lot of groundwater is pumped out, the ground sinks in some places by up to about 25 centimetres a year.
53577.m: Mexico City is sinking because it stands on a former lake bed.

53578.q: Which ancient ruined city with a Pyramid of the Sun and a Pyramid of the Moon lies north-east of Mexico City?
53578.e: Teotihuacán lies about 50 km north-east of Mexico City and about 1500 years ago was one of the largest cities in the world. The Pyramid of the Sun is one of the largest pyramids in the Americas.
53578.m: The pyramids of Teotihuacán stand near Mexico City.

53579.q: In which stadium in Mexico City were the 1970 and 1986 World Cup finals played?
53579.e: Brazil became world champions in 1970 and Argentina in 1986 at the Estadio Azteca. It is the first stadium to have hosted matches at three World Cups, because games were also played there at the 2026 World Cup.
53579.m: Football history was made in the Aztec Stadium in Mexico City.

53580.q: Which active volcano can often be seen from Mexico City?
53580.e: Popocatépetl is about 5400 m high and lies about 70 km south-east of the city. It is one of Mexico's most active volcanoes and often puffs out ash.
53580.m: The volcano Popocatépetl watches over Mexico City.

53581.q: Which natural hazard especially threatens Mexico City, as in 1985 and 2017?
53581.e: Mexico City lies in an earthquake zone, and the soft lake bed makes the shaking stronger. Severe earthquakes destroyed many buildings in 1985 and 2017.
53581.m: Mexico City has to protect itself against earthquakes.

53582.q: Which two seas does the Yucatán Peninsula separate?
a: Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean Sea
53582.e: Yucatán juts northwards in south-eastern Mexico. To the west and north lies the Gulf of Mexico, to the east the Caribbean Sea.
53582.m: The Yucatán Peninsula lies between the Gulf of Mexico and the Caribbean.

53583.q: Which famous ruined Maya city lies on the Yucatán Peninsula?
53583.e: Chichén Itzá was a large Maya city. Its step pyramid, El Castillo, is one of the best-known buildings in Mexico.
53583.m: Chichén Itzá is a Maya city on Yucatán.

53584.q: What are the water-filled limestone holes on Yucatán called?
53584.e: Cenotes form when the roof of an underground cave in the limestone collapses. For the Maya they were important sources of water and sacred places.
53584.m: Cenotes are natural wells on Yucatán.

53585.q: Why are there hardly any rivers on the surface of the Yucatán Peninsula?
a: The water seeps into the limestone
53585.e: Yucatán is made of porous limestone, a karst landscape. Rainwater seeps away quickly and flows in underground rivers and caves.
53585.m: On Yucatán the rivers flow underground.

53586.q: What hit the coast of Yucatán about 66 million years ago and helped wipe out the dinosaurs?
53586.e: An asteroid about 10 km across struck near Chicxulub. The effects on the climate helped wipe out the dinosaurs.
53586.m: An asteroid near Yucatán helped end the dinosaurs.

53587.q: Which well-known beach resort lies on the Caribbean coast of the Yucatán Peninsula?
53587.e: Cancún in the state of Quintana Roo was built as a holiday area from 1970 onwards. Today it is one of Mexico's most important tourist centres.
53587.m: Cancún is the most famous beach resort on Yucatán.

53588.q: Apart from Mexico, which countries have a share of the Yucatán Peninsula?
53588.e: Most of the peninsula belongs to Mexico. In the south, Belize and northern Guatemala also have a share of it.
53588.m: Mexico, Belize and Guatemala share Yucatán.

53589.q: What are the two long mountain ranges that frame Mexico's highlands to the west and east called?
53589.e: The Sierra Madre Occidental runs parallel to the Pacific coast, the Sierra Madre Oriental parallel to the Gulf coast. Between them lie the Mexican highlands.
53589.m: Two Sierras Madres frame the Mexican highlands.

53590.q: What does the Spanish name “Sierra Madre” mean?
53590.e: “Sierra” means mountain range and “madre” means mother. So the Sierra Madre is Mexico's main or mother mountain range.
53590.m: The Sierra Madre is Mexico's mother mountain range.

53591.q: In which country are the Sierra Madre mountains?
53591.e: The Sierra Madre Occidental, Oriental and del Sur run through Mexico. They frame the Mexican highlands.
53591.m: The Sierra Madre is Mexico's great mountain range.

53592.q: Which plateau lies between the Sierra Madre Occidental and the Sierra Madre Oriental?
53592.e: Between the two mountain ranges lie the Mexican highlands, also called the Altiplano. They are dry and mostly over 1000 m high.
53592.m: The Mexican highlands lie sheltered between the Sierras Madres.

53593.q: Which Indigenous people lives in the Sierra Madre Occidental and is known for long-distance running?
53593.e: The Rarámuri live in the mountains and canyons of Chihuahua. Their name means roughly “the light-footed ones”, and they often run very long distances in sandals.
53593.m: The Rarámuri are the runners of the Sierra Madre.

53594.q: Which mountain range runs along the Pacific coast in southern Mexico near Acapulco?
53594.e: The Sierra Madre del Sur runs through the states of Guerrero and Oaxaca. It drops steeply to the Pacific coast, where Acapulco also lies.
53594.m: The Sierra Madre del Sur is Mexico's southern coastal range.

53595.q: Which capital city lies in the highlands between the Sierra Madre mountains?
53595.e: Mexico City lies at about 2240 m in the south of the Mexican highlands. It is one of the largest cities in the world.
53595.m: Mexico City lies in Mexico's highlands.

53596.q: Which three countries border the Gulf of Mexico?
53596.e: The Gulf of Mexico is bordered by the USA to the north, Mexico to the west and south, and Cuba to the south-east. It is a marginal sea of the Atlantic.
53596.m: The USA, Mexico and Cuba lie on the Gulf of Mexico.

53597.q: Which important Mexican port on the Gulf of Mexico is where Hernán Cortés landed in 1519?
53597.e: Veracruz was founded by Hernán Cortés in 1519 and is one of the oldest places founded by Europeans on the American mainland. Today it is one of Mexico's most important ports.
53597.m: Veracruz is Mexico's big port on the Gulf.

53598.q: What made the 1900 hurricane in the city of Galveston, Texas, so deadly?
a: A storm surge flooded the low-lying city
An earthquake made the houses collapse
A volcano erupted at the same time
53598.e: In September 1900 a storm surge flooded the low-lying island of Galveston. An estimated 6000 to 12,000 people died.
53598.m: The Galveston hurricane of 1900 was the deadliest natural disaster in the USA.

53599.q: Which oil disaster happened in the Gulf of Mexico in 2010?
a: The explosion of the Deepwater Horizon oil rig
53599.e: In April 2010 the Deepwater Horizon oil rig exploded. Afterwards oil poured into the sea for months, causing one of the biggest oil spills in history.
53599.m: The Deepwater Horizon disaster polluted the Gulf of Mexico in 2010.

53600.q: Why do strong hurricanes often form over the Gulf of Mexico?
a: The sea water is very warm in summer
The water there is especially low in salt
The sea there is very deep and cold
53600.e: Hurricanes get their energy from warm sea water. The warm Gulf often makes them stronger; Hurricane Katrina, for example, hit New Orleans in 2005.
53600.m: Warm water in the Gulf of Mexico makes hurricanes stronger.

53601.q: Which raw material is extracted in large quantities from the seabed in the Gulf of Mexico?
53601.e: There are a great many oil rigs in the Gulf that extract oil and natural gas from the seabed. The region is one of the most important oil-producing areas in the world.
53601.m: There are large oil deposits under the Gulf of Mexico.

53602.q: Through which strait is the Gulf of Mexico connected to the open Atlantic?
53602.e: The Straits of Florida lie between Florida and Cuba. Warm water flows through them from the Gulf into the Atlantic and feeds the Gulf Stream.
53602.m: Water flows from the Gulf of Mexico into the Atlantic through the Straits of Florida.

53603.q: Between which two countries does the Rio Grande form part of the border?
53603.e: For about 2000 km the Rio Grande forms the border between the US state of Texas and Mexico. This makes it one of the best-known border rivers in the world.
53603.m: The Rio Grande separates Texas from Mexico.

53604.q: Which US state lies on the Rio Grande on the border with Mexico?
53604.e: For about 2000 km the Rio Grande separates Texas from Mexico. In Mexico the river is called the Río Bravo.
53604.m: The Rio Grande is the border between Texas and Mexico.

53605.q: In which mountains does the Rio Grande rise?
a: In the Sierra Madre del Sur
53605.e: The Rio Grande rises in the San Juan Mountains, part of the Rocky Mountains in the US state of Colorado. From there it flows south through New Mexico.
53605.m: The Rio Grande begins in the Rocky Mountains of Colorado.

53606.q: Where does the Rio Grande end?
53606.e: After about 3000 km the Rio Grande flows into the Gulf of Mexico near Brownsville and Matamoros. In dry years, because so much water is taken from it, it sometimes barely reaches the sea.
53606.m: The Rio Grande ends in the Gulf of Mexico.

53607.q: What often happens to the Rio Grande in dry years?
53607.e: A lot of water is taken for fields and cities. In dry years, therefore, only a little arrives at its mouth in the Gulf of Mexico.
53607.m: Because water is taken from it, the lower Rio Grande is often very weak.

53608.q: Which national park in Texas lies on a big bend of the Rio Grande?
53608.e: Big Bend National Park is named after the big bend of the Rio Grande. There the river has cut deep canyons into the desert mountains.
53608.m: Big Bend National Park lies on the great bend of the Rio Grande.

53609.q: What does the Spanish name “Rio Grande” mean?
53609.e: “Río” means river and “grande” means big. At about 3000 km it is one of the longest rivers in North America.

53610.q: Which sea separates the Baja California peninsula from the Mexican mainland?
53610.e: Between Baja California and the mainland lies the Gulf of California, also called the Sea of Cortez. On the other side of the peninsula lies the open Pacific.
53610.m: The Gulf of California separates Baja California from the mainland.

53611.q: Roughly how long is the Baja California peninsula?
53611.e: Baja California is about 1200 km long but, depending on the spot, only about 40 to 320 km wide. This makes it one of the longest peninsulas in the world.
53611.m: Baja California is a very long, narrow peninsula.

53612.q: Which whales give birth to their young in the lagoons of Baja California?
53612.e: Every year grey whales travel thousands of kilometres from the Arctic to the warm lagoons of the peninsula. There they give birth to their calves in winter.
53612.m: Grey whales have their young in the lagoons of Baja California.

53613.q: Which border city in the north of Baja California lies right next to San Diego?
53613.e: Tijuana lies on the border with the USA just south of San Diego in California. The border crossing there is one of the busiest in the world.
53613.m: Tijuana is Baja California's border city with the USA.

53614.q: Which place with a famous rock arch lies at the southern tip of Baja California?
53614.e: Cabo San Lucas lies at the very south of the peninsula, where the Pacific and the Gulf of California meet. The rock arch El Arco in the sea is well known.
53614.m: Cabo San Lucas lies at the southern tip of Baja California.

53615.q: Into how many Mexican states is the Baja California peninsula divided?
53615.e: The north forms the state of Baja California, with its capital Mexicali. The south is the state of Baja California Sur, with its capital La Paz.
53615.m: Baja California consists of two states.

53616.q: Why is the Gulf of California also called the “Aquarium of the World”?
a: Because a great many different sea creatures live there
Because the largest aquarium was built there
Because the water there is completely still
Because swimming is not allowed there
53616.e: Whales, dolphins, sea lions and hundreds of kinds of fish, among others, live in the Gulf. The ocean explorer Jacques Cousteau gave it this name.
53616.m: The Gulf of California is famous for its many sea creatures.

53617.q: Which landscape covers large parts of Baja California?
53617.e: Baja California is very dry and mostly covered by desert. Huge cacti grow there, such as the cardón, one of the largest cacti in the world.
53617.m: Baja California is a land of deserts and cacti.

53618.q: Which large mountain range runs through western Canada?
53618.e: The Rocky Mountains stretch from Canada into the USA. Canada's highest mountain, Mount Logan, however, lies in the Saint Elias Mountains in Yukon.
53618.m: The Rocky Mountains lie in western Canada.

53619.q: On which date does Canada celebrate its national day, Canada Day?
53619.e: On 1 July 1867 the country of Canada was formed when several colonies joined together. Canada Day marks this, much as Switzerland celebrates on 1 August.
53619.m: Canada celebrates its national day on 1 July.

53620.q: Which two continents does the Central American land bridge connect?
53620.e: Central America is a narrow strip of land between Mexico and Colombia. It connects North America with South America.
53620.m: Central America is the land bridge between North and South America.

53621.q: How many countries are there on the mainland of Central America?
53621.e: Central America includes Guatemala, Belize, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Panama. That makes seven countries.
53621.m: There are seven countries on the Central American land bridge.

53622.q: In which Central American country is English the official language?
53622.e: Belize was a British colony until 1981 and used to be called British Honduras. That is why English is the official language there, while the other countries use Spanish.
53622.m: Belize is the only Central American country with English as its official language.

53623.q: Which is the smallest Central American country by area?
53623.e: At about 21,000 km², El Salvador is about half the size of Switzerland. It is the only Central American country with no coast on the Caribbean Sea.
53623.m: El Salvador is the smallest country in Central America.

53624.q: Which is the largest Central American country by area?
53624.e: At about 130,000 km², Nicaragua is the largest country in Central America. It is a good three times the size of Switzerland.
53624.m: Nicaragua is the largest country in Central America by area.

53625.q: What is the largest lake in Central America called?
53625.e: With over 8000 km², Lake Nicaragua (Cocibolca) is the largest lake in Central America. Sharks even live in it, swimming in from the sea up a river.
53625.m: Lake Nicaragua is the largest lake in Central America.

53626.q: About how long ago did the land bridge between North and South America close?
53626.e: Volcanic activity and the rising of the Earth's crust gradually created a land connection. It was closed about 3 million years ago.
53626.m: In terms of Earth's history, the Central American land bridge is young, about 3 million years old.

53627.q: What happened to many animal species when the Central American land bridge closed?
a: They all died out at once
53627.e: Animals could now walk from North to South America and back. This process is called the Great American Interchange.
53627.m: North and South America exchanged many animal species over the new land bridge.

53628.q: Why are there so many volcanoes in Central America?
a: One tectonic plate dives beneath another
The sea is especially warm there
The area lies on the equator
53628.e: Off the Pacific coast, the Cocos Plate dives beneath the Caribbean Plate. Rock melts in the process and magma rises to the surface.
53628.m: Volcanoes often form where tectonic plates dive beneath each other.

53629.q: Which people built the temple city of Tikal in northern Guatemala?
53629.e: Tikal was one of the largest Maya cities and flourished over 1000 years ago. The ruins lie in the rainforest and are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
53629.m: Tikal is a famous Maya city in the rainforest of Guatemala.

53630.q: What is Guatemala's currency, the quetzal, named after?
53630.e: The quetzal is a bird with long, shimmering green tail feathers. It is Guatemala's national bird and gave the currency its name.
53630.m: Guatemala named its currency after its national bird, the quetzal.

53631.q: What is Tajumulco, the highest mountain in Central America, in Guatemala?
53631.e: The volcano Tajumulco is about 4220 m high. It lies in western Guatemala, where there are many volcanoes.
53631.m: The highest mountain in Central America is the volcano Tajumulco.

53632.q: Which Central American country has the most inhabitants?
53632.e: Guatemala has about 18 million inhabitants (as of 2024). That is about twice as many as Switzerland.
53632.m: Guatemala is the most populous country in Central America.

53633.q: What is the name of Guatemala's former capital, which is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
53633.e: Antigua Guatemala was the capital until earthquakes caused great damage in 1773. Its colonial buildings are now World Heritage.
53633.m: Antigua Guatemala is an old colonial city and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

53634.q: Apart from Spanish, which languages do many people in Guatemala speak?
53634.e: A large part of the population belongs to Indigenous Maya peoples. There are over 20 different Mayan languages, for example K'iche'.
53634.m: Many people in Guatemala speak a Mayan language.

53636.q: What is Costa Rica especially famous for around the world?
53636.e: A great many kinds of animals and plants live in a small area, such as sloths, toucans and frogs. About a quarter of the country is protected.
53636.m: Costa Rica is famous for its nature and variety of species.

53637.q: What is Costa Rica's currency called?
53637.e: The currency is called the Costa Rican colón. It is named after Christopher Columbus, in Spanish Cristóbal Colón.
53637.m: In Costa Rica people pay with the colón.

53639.q: What is the forest at Monteverde in Costa Rica, which is almost always in the clouds, called?
53639.e: In the mountains of Monteverde, clouds often hang between the trees. The plants take water directly from the mist.
53639.m: A cloud forest is a mountain forest that is often in the clouds.

53641.q: Which country handed control of the canal over to Panama at the end of 1999?
53641.e: The USA had built the canal and run it for a long time. On 31 December 1999 it passed completely to Panama.
53641.m: Since the end of 1999 the Panama Canal has belonged entirely to Panama.

53642.q: How are ships taken over the difference in height in the Panama Canal?
53642.e: Lock chambers fill with water and lift the ships up to Gatún Lake, about 26 m high. On the other side they lower them again.
53642.m: Locks raise and lower ships in the Panama Canal.

53643.q: Roughly how long is the Panama Canal?
53643.e: The canal is about 82 km long. That is roughly the distance from Zurich to Lucerne and on to Sarnen.
53643.m: The Panama Canal is about 80 kilometres long.

53644.q: Which South American country borders Panama?
53644.e: To the east Panama borders Colombia, to the west Costa Rica. Panama is therefore the link between Central and South America.
53644.m: Panama's neighbour in South America is Colombia.

53645.q: Where is the Pan-American Highway, the long road through the Americas, interrupted?
a: in the jungle of the Darién
53645.e: Between Panama and Colombia lies a swampy rainforest area with no road. This gap is called the Darién Gap.
53645.m: The Pan-American Highway has a gap in the Darién.

53646.q: Which is the largest island in the Caribbean?
53646.e: Cuba covers about 110,000 km², a good two and a half times the size of Switzerland. The island is long and narrow.
53646.m: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean.

53647.q: Which group of islands does Cuba belong to?
53647.e: The large islands in the north of the Caribbean form the Greater Antilles. Cuba is the westernmost of them.
53647.m: Cuba belongs to the Greater Antilles.

53648.q: Who led the revolution that triumphed in Cuba in 1959?
53648.e: In 1959 Fidel Castro and his followers overthrew the dictator Batista. Afterwards Cuba became a socialist state.
53648.m: The Cuban Revolution of 1959 was led by Fidel Castro.

53649.q: Which plant was grown on large plantations in Cuba for centuries?
53649.e: For a long time Cuba was one of the largest sugar producers in the world. In the past, enslaved people were forced to work on the sugar cane plantations.
53649.m: Sugar cane was long Cuba's most important product.

53650.q: Roughly how far is Cuba from the USA at the narrowest point of the Straits of Florida?
53650.e: The Straits of Florida separate Cuba from Florida. At the narrowest point they are only about 150 km wide.
53650.m: Cuba is only about 150 kilometres from Florida.

53651.q: What can you still see especially often on the streets of Havana in Cuba?
53651.e: After the 1959 revolution Cuba could hardly import any new cars. That is why many colourful cars from the 1950s are still driving around.
53651.m: Many old cars still drive around Havana.

53652.q: Which cars still shape the street scene in Havana today?
53652.e: After 1959 hardly any new cars came into the country. That is why many Cubans still drive American cars from the 1950s.
53652.m: Many vintage cars from the 1950s drive around Havana.

53653.q: From which period do many buildings in Havana's old town date?
a: From the time of the Vikings
53653.e: The old town, Habana Vieja, with its fortresses shows buildings from the Spanish colonial period. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1982.
53653.m: Havana's old town dates from the Spanish colonial period.

53654.q: What is the Malecón in Havana?
53654.e: The Malecón is about 8 km long and runs along the coast. In the evening many people meet there.
53654.m: The Malecón is Havana's famous seafront road.

53655.q: Which sprinter from Jamaica holds the world record in the 100 metres (as of 2025)?
53655.e: In 2009 in Berlin, Usain Bolt ran the 100 m in 9.58 seconds. This record had still not been broken in 2025.
53655.m: Usain Bolt from Jamaica is the fastest person over 100 metres.

53656.q: From which country did Jamaica become independent in 1962?
53656.e: On 6 August 1962 Jamaica became independent from Great Britain. It remained a member of the Commonwealth, however.
53656.m: Jamaica has been independent from Great Britain since 1962.

53657.q: Which mountains in Jamaica are famous for their coffee?
53657.e: A very expensive coffee grows in the cool, damp Blue Mountains in the east of the island. Blue Mountain Peak is over 2200 m high.
53657.m: Blue Mountain coffee comes from Jamaica's mountains.

53658.q: Where does Jamaica rank in size among the islands of the Greater Antilles?
53658.e: Only Cuba and Hispaniola are bigger. At about 11,000 km², Jamaica is about a quarter the size of Switzerland.
53658.m: Jamaica is the third-largest island of the Greater Antilles.

53659.q: Why were many people amazed by the bobsleigh team from Jamaica in 1988?
a: Because there is no snow in Jamaica
Because it was made up only of children
Because it competed without a bobsleigh
53659.e: A bobsleigh team from warm Jamaica was a big surprise at the 1988 Winter Olympics in Calgary. The story was told in the film “Cool Runnings”.
53659.m: Jamaica competed in bobsleigh for the first time in 1988.

53660.q: Which two countries share the island of Hispaniola?
53660.e: The west of the island belongs to Haiti, the larger east to the Dominican Republic.
53660.m: Haiti and the Dominican Republic share the island of Hispaniola.

53661.q: Who gave the island of Hispaniola its name in 1492?
53661.e: Columbus called the island “La Isla Española”, the Spanish island. This became the name Hispaniola.

53662.q: What is the capital of Haiti?
53662.e: Port-au-Prince lies on a large bay in the west of the island. It is Haiti's largest city.
53662.m: The capital of Haiti is Port-au-Prince.

53663.q: Haiti became independent in 1804. What was special about this?
a: It was the first country with a railway
It was the first monarchy in the Americas
53663.e: Enslaved people rose up against French colonial rule. Haiti thus became the first country to emerge from a successful slave revolt.
53663.m: Haiti emerged in 1804 from a successful slave revolt.

53664.q: Which two official languages does Haiti have?
53664.e: Haiti was a French colony. Almost everyone speaks Haitian Creole, a creole language with many French words.
53664.m: In Haiti people speak French and Haitian Creole.

53665.q: Which natural disaster hit Haiti especially hard in January 2010?
53665.e: On 12 January 2010 a powerful earthquake destroyed large parts of the capital. Many countries, including Switzerland, sent help.
53665.m: A severe earthquake shook Haiti in January 2010.

53666.q: What is the official language of the Dominican Republic?
53666.e: The eastern part of the island was a Spanish colony. That is why Spanish is spoken there.
53666.m: In the Dominican Republic people speak Spanish.

53667.q: What political status does Puerto Rico have?
53667.e: Puerto Rico has belonged to the USA since 1898, but it is not a state. It is a territory with its own government.
53667.m: Puerto Rico is a territory of the United States.

53668.q: What is the capital of Puerto Rico?
53668.e: San Juan lies on the north coast. The old town with the El Morro fortress dates from Spanish times.
53668.m: The capital of Puerto Rico is San Juan.

53669.q: Which two official languages does Puerto Rico have?
53669.e: Puerto Rico was Spanish for about 400 years and then became part of the USA. In everyday life most people speak Spanish.
53669.m: Spanish and English are the official languages of Puerto Rico.

53670.q: Which citizenship do people from Puerto Rico have?
53670.e: Since 1917 people from Puerto Rico have been citizens of the USA. However, they cannot vote in presidential elections while they live on the island.
53670.m: People from Puerto Rico have been US citizens since 1917.

53671.q: What is the climate like on the Caribbean island of Puerto Rico?
53671.e: Puerto Rico lies in the tropics. It is warm all year round, and rainforest even grows in the mountains.
53671.m: It is warm all year round in Puerto Rico.

53672.q: Which small animal is a symbol of Puerto Rico and calls loudly “ko-kee” at night?
53672.e: The coquí is a tiny tree frog. Its name imitates the call of the males, which you can hear everywhere at night.
53672.m: The little coquí frog is a symbol of Puerto Rico.

53673.q: Which natural hazard especially threatens Puerto Rico in late summer?
53673.e: Hurricanes form over the warm Atlantic in late summer. In 2017 Hurricane Maria caused great damage in Puerto Rico.
53673.m: Puerto Rico is often hit by hurricanes.

53674.q: What does the Spanish name “Puerto Rico” mean in English?
53674.e: “Puerto” means harbour and “rico” means rich. Originally this was the name of the capital, later of the whole island.

53676.q: Which animals are famous on the beach of Big Major Cay in the Bahamas?
53676.e: Domestic pigs live on this small island and swim out into the sea towards boats. They are a tourist attraction.
53676.m: Pigs swim in the sea at Big Major Cay.

53677.q: Into which two groups are the Lesser Antilles divided?
53677.e: The eastern islands lie in the path of the trade wind and are called the islands above the wind (in English, the Leeward and Windward Islands). The islands off Venezuela are the islands below the wind, known in English as the Leeward Antilles.
53677.m: The Lesser Antilles consist of the islands above and below the wind.

53678.q: Which kingdom do the ABC islands of Aruba, Bonaire and Curaçao belong to?
53678.e: The three islands off the coast of Venezuela were Dutch colonies. Today they belong to the Kingdom of the Netherlands in different ways.
53678.m: Aruba, Bonaire and Curaçao belong to the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

53679.q: Which currency do people pay with on the Caribbean island of Martinique?
53679.e: Martinique is an overseas region of France and part of the EU. That is why the euro is used there.
53679.m: On Martinique people pay with the euro.

53680.q: Which musical instrument was developed in Trinidad from old oil drums?
53680.e: In the 1930s and 1940s musicians in Trinidad hammered oil drums into shape so that they produced notes. This is how the steelpan came about.

53681.q: Which largest island of the Lesser Antilles lies just off Venezuela?
53681.e: Trinidad covers about 4800 km² and lies only a few kilometres off the coast of South America. Together with Tobago it forms one country.
53681.m: Trinidad is the largest island of the Lesser Antilles.

53682.q: What destroyed a whole town on the Caribbean island of Martinique in 1902?
a: An eruption of the volcano Mont Pelée
53682.e: When Mont Pelée erupted, a glowing cloud of gas and ash raced down the mountain. The town of Saint-Pierre was destroyed and almost all of its roughly 28,000 people died.
53682.m: The volcano Mont Pelée destroyed a town on Martinique in 1902.

53683.q: What shape does the chain of the Lesser Antilles have on the map?
53683.e: The islands line up in an arc from the north-east down to South America. Geographers call this an island arc.
53683.m: The Lesser Antilles form an island arc.

53684.q: Why are there volcanoes on many islands of the Lesser Antilles?
a: The water there is very salty
There is a lot of rain there
53684.e: At the eastern edge of the Caribbean, Atlantic ocean crust dives beneath the Caribbean Plate. Rising magma forms volcanic islands.
53684.m: The volcanoes of the Lesser Antilles are formed by sinking crust.

53685.q: Which two countries share the small island of Saint-Martin?
53685.e: The island has been divided since 1648. The north is French; the south is Dutch and is called Sint Maarten.
53685.m: Saint-Martin is divided between France and the Netherlands.

53686.q: Who is the Caribbean Sea named after?
53686.e: The Caribs were an Indigenous people who lived on the Lesser Antilles and on the coast of South America. The Europeans named the sea after them.
53686.m: The Caribbean Sea bears the name of the Carib people.

53687.q: Which continent borders the Caribbean Sea to the south?
53687.e: To the south lie the coasts of Colombia and Venezuela. To the west the sea borders Central America.
53687.m: South America lies to the south of the Caribbean Sea.

53688.q: Between which islands is the deepest point of the Caribbean Sea?
53688.e: The Cayman Trench between Cuba and Jamaica is up to about 7700 m deep. Two tectonic plates meet there.
53688.m: The deepest point of the Caribbean lies between Cuba and Jamaica.

53689.q: Between which two seas does the island of Cuba lie?
a: Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean Sea
53689.e: Cuba lies on the northern edge of the Caribbean. The Yucatán Channel between Mexico and Cuba connects the Caribbean Sea with the Gulf of Mexico.
53689.m: Cuba lies between the Caribbean and the Gulf of Mexico.

53690.q: Roughly how many times would the area of Switzerland fit into the Caribbean Sea?
53690.e: The Caribbean Sea covers about 2.75 million km², Switzerland about 41,000 km². 2,750,000 ÷ 41,000 gives about 67.
53690.m: The Caribbean Sea is about 65 times the size of Switzerland.

53691.q: What do hurricanes mainly need in order to form?
53691.e: Hurricanes form over sea water of at least about 26 °C. The warm water evaporates and gives the storm energy.
53691.m: Warm sea water is the engine of a hurricane.

53692.q: What is special about the Mesoamerican Reef off Belize and Mexico?
a: It is the second-largest barrier reef
It lies in a freshwater lake
It is made only of stones
53692.e: The reef stretches for over 1000 km from Mexico to Honduras. After the Great Barrier Reef in Australia, it is considered the second-largest reef system in the world.
53692.m: The Mesoamerican Reef is considered the second-largest barrier reef in the world.

53693.q: How did the Great Blue Hole, a deep blue underwater hole off Belize, form?
a: A cave collapsed and was flooded by the sea
A volcano blasted a hole in the ground
Divers dug it out for tourists
53693.e: The Great Blue Hole formed in the Ice Age as a cave on land. Its roof collapsed, and when the sea level rose the hole filled with water.
53693.m: The Great Blue Hole is a collapsed, flooded cave.

53694.q: Which group of living things do corals belong to?
53694.e: Corals are small cnidarians called polyps. Reef corals build a limestone skeleton, and over a long time reefs form from it.
53694.m: Corals are animals, even though they look like plants.

53695.q: What lives in the tissue of many reef corals and supplies them with food?
53695.e: The algae are called zooxanthellae and carry out photosynthesis. They give the corals sugar and their colours.
53695.m: Reef corals live in a partnership with tiny algae.

53696.e: If the sea gets too warm, the corals expel their coloured lodgers and turn white. If the heat lasts, they die.
53696.m: When the water is too warm, corals bleach and can die.

53697.q: Which introduced predatory fish threatens the coral reefs of the Caribbean?
53697.e: The lionfish comes from the Indo-Pacific and has hardly any enemies in the Caribbean. It eats a great many young reef fish.
53697.m: The lionfish is an introduced pest in the Caribbean.

53698.q: What does the hawksbill turtle mainly eat in the coral reefs?
53698.e: The hawksbill turtle has a pointed, beak-like head. It uses it to pull sponges out of cracks in the reef.
53698.m: The hawksbill turtle feeds mainly on sponges.

a: In the Indian Ocean off India
In the North Sea off Norway
53699.e: The Bahamas are a group of islands in the Atlantic south-east of Florida. They consist of about 700 islands.
53699.m: The Bahamas lie in the Atlantic off Florida.

53700.q: Which part of the economy is most important for the Bahamas?
53700.e: Millions of visitors come every year, many on cruise ships. Tourism brings in most of the income.
53700.m: The Bahamas live mainly from tourism.

53701.q: What is the colourful street festival with music and costumes in the Bahamas called?
53701.e: Junkanoo is celebrated mainly on 26 December and New Year's Day. Groups parade through the streets with drums, cowbells and costumes.
53701.m: Junkanoo is the big street festival of the Bahamas.

53702.q: Where does almost all the electricity in Costa Rica come from?
53702.e: For years Costa Rica has produced almost all its electricity from hydropower, geothermal energy, wind and sun. As in Switzerland, hydropower is the most important.
53702.m: Costa Rica gets almost all its electricity from renewable sources.

53703.q: What is Tortuguero National Park on Costa Rica's Caribbean coast known for?
a: There is a large salt lake there
53703.e: On the beaches of Tortuguero, green turtles and other species dig their nests. The name means roughly “place of the turtles”.
53703.m: Sea turtles lay their eggs in Tortuguero.

53704.q: Which active volcano in Guatemala erupted devastatingly in June 2018?
53704.e: When Fuego erupted, glowing clouds of gas and ash raced into the valley. Several villages were buried.
53704.m: The Volcán de Fuego is one of Guatemala's most active volcanoes.

53705.q: Which woman from Guatemala received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1992?
53705.e: Rigoberta Menchú belongs to the K'iche' people. She campaigned for the rights of the Indigenous population.
53705.m: Rigoberta Menchú received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1992.

53706.q: How was Gatún Lake, in the middle of the Panama Canal, created?
53706.e: During construction, the Chagres River was dammed. This created a large artificial lake that the ships sail across.
53706.m: Gatún Lake is an artificially dammed lake.

53707.q: Which country first tried, without success, to build the Panama Canal in the 1880s?
53707.e: Ferdinand de Lesseps, who built the Suez Canal, led the project. Diseases such as yellow fever and malaria, and money problems, made it fail.
53707.m: France was the first to fail at building the Panama Canal.

53708.q: What was the town of Port Royal in Jamaica notorious for in the 17th century?
a: As a place of witch hunts
As the capital of the Incas
As a camp for gold diggers
53708.e: Port Royal lay on a spit of land off what is now Kingston. In the 1692 earthquake a large part of the town slid into the sea.
53708.m: Port Royal was a notorious pirate town in the 17th century.

53709.q: What is ackee, part of Jamaica's national dish?
53709.e: Ackee is a fruit that, when cooked, looks rather like scrambled egg. It is eaten with salted dried fish.
53709.m: Jamaica's national dish is ackee and saltfish.

53711.q: What has been washing up in large amounts on Caribbean beaches since about 2011?
53711.e: Huge mats of the brown seaweed sargassum drift in the Atlantic and land on the coasts. As they rot, they smell unpleasant.
53711.m: For some years brown seaweed has been a burden on Caribbean beaches.

53712.q: Why are coral reefs important for the coasts of the Caribbean?
53712.e: Reefs act like natural breakwaters. In storms they protect beaches and villages from flooding.
53712.m: Coral reefs protect the coasts from strong waves.

53713.q: Which French Caribbean island is shaped like a butterfly on the map?
53713.e: Guadeloupe consists of two main islands, Basse-Terre and Grande-Terre. Together they look like the wings of a butterfly.

53714.q: Which spice is shown on the flag of Grenada?
53714.e: Grenada is called the “Spice Isle” and is one of the largest producers of nutmeg. That is why the flag shows a nutmeg.
53714.m: Grenada is the Spice Isle with a nutmeg on its flag.

53716.q: Which light blue gemstone is found only in the Dominican Republic?
53716.e: Larimar is a sky-blue stone of volcanic origin. So far, deposits are known only in the south-west of the Dominican Republic.
53716.m: Larimar is a blue stone found only in the Dominican Republic.

53717.q: Which country does the so-called Panama hat originally come from?
53717.e: The hats are woven from palm fibres in Ecuador. They got their name because they were sold via Panama and worn by workers on the canal.
53717.m: The Panama hat actually comes from Ecuador.

53718.q: After independence, Haiti built a huge mountain fortress. What for?
a: To protect against the French returning
As a holiday palace for the king
53718.e: The Citadelle Laferrière was built on a mountain at the beginning of the 19th century to protect Haiti against a return of the French. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
53718.m: The mountain fortress was meant to protect Haiti from the French.

53719.q: Which tropic runs through Brazil, very close to São Paulo?
53719.e: The southern tropic is called the Tropic of Capricorn. It passes just by São Paulo, while the equator crosses northern Brazil.
53719.m: The equator and the Tropic of Capricorn run through Brazil.

53720.q: Which official language is spoken in Brazil?
53720.e: Brazil was a colony of Portugal for a long time. That is why Portuguese is the official language there, while most neighbouring countries speak Spanish.

53721.e: Since 1994 people in Brazil have paid with the real. The peso, for example, is the currency of Argentina.
53721.m: In Brazil people pay with the real.

53722.q: From which country did Brazil declare its independence in 1822?
53722.e: Brazil was a colony of Portugal for over 300 years. On 7 September 1822 it declared itself independent.
53722.m: Brazil became independent from Portugal in 1822.

53723.q: What is the Pantanal in South America?
53723.e: In the rainy season, a large part of the Pantanal plain is under water. Many animals live there, such as jaguars, caimans and capybaras.
53723.m: The Pantanal is the largest inland wetland on Earth.

53724.q: What is the seat of the Argentine president in Buenos Aires, known for its colour, called?
53724.e: Casa Rosada means “pink house”. It stands on the Plaza de Mayo in the centre of Buenos Aires.
53724.m: Argentina's president works in the pink Casa Rosada.

53725.q: What kind of landscape is the Pampas in South America?
53725.e: The Pampas is a flat grassland with few trees. Its name comes from the Quechua language and means “plain”.
53725.m: The Pampas is a wide, flat grassland.

53726.q: Why is the Pampas good for farming?
a: It lies right on the equator
There is never any winter there
It lies very high in the Andes
53726.e: The Pampas has deep, fertile soils and a temperate climate. That is why a lot of wheat, maize and soya is grown there.
53726.m: Its fertile soils make the Pampas Argentina's breadbasket.

53727.q: Which strait separates the South American mainland from Tierra del Fuego?
53727.e: The Strait of Magellan is named after Ferdinand Magellan, who sailed through it in 1520. The Drake Passage lies further south, between Cape Horn and Antarctica.
53727.m: The Strait of Magellan lies between the mainland and Tierra del Fuego.

53728.q: Why are there many large observatories in the Atacama Desert?
a: Clear, dry air and hardly any light pollution
Because it never gets dark there
Because the stars are closer there
53728.e: In the high, dry desert there are almost no clouds and hardly any artificial light. That is why the European Southern Observatory (ESO), for example, runs telescopes there.
53728.m: The clear air of the Atacama is ideal for observatories.

53729.q: Which sought-after raw material for batteries is extracted in the Salar de Atacama?
53729.e: Under the salt flat of the Salar de Atacama lies salty water with a lot of lithium. Lithium is needed for batteries in mobile phones and electric cars.
53729.m: Lithium for batteries is extracted in the Salar de Atacama.

53730.q: Which metal is mined in the huge Chuquicamata mine in Chile's Atacama Desert?
53730.e: Chuquicamata is one of the largest open-pit copper mines in the world. Chile is the world's most important supplier of copper.
53730.m: A lot of copper is mined in the Atacama.

53731.q: Which people built the ruined city of Machu Picchu?
53731.e: The Incas built Machu Picchu high in the Andes in the 15th century. The Aztecs and Maya lived in Central America.
53731.m: Machu Picchu is an Inca city.

53732.q: Machu Picchu was voted into a famous selection in 2007. Which one?
a: The New Seven Wonders of the World
The Seven Wonders of the Ancient World
The largest cities in the world
The highest mountains of the Andes
53732.e: In a worldwide vote in 2007, Machu Picchu was chosen as one of the New Seven Wonders of the World. It had already been a UNESCO World Heritage Site for longer.
53732.m: Machu Picchu is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.

53733.q: How big is Lake Titicaca compared with Lake Geneva?
a: More than ten times as big
53733.e: Lake Titicaca covers about 8300 square kilometres, Lake Geneva about 580. So it is more than ten times as big.
53733.m: Lake Titicaca is much bigger than Lake Geneva.

53734.q: In which lake is the Isla del Sol, the Island of the Sun of the Incas?
53734.e: “Isla del Sol” means “Island of the Sun”. According to Inca legend, the sun god appeared here, and the first Inca ruler is said to have come from here.
53734.m: The Isla del Sol in Lake Titicaca is the Incas' Island of the Sun.

53735.q: What is the plateau in the Andes on which Lake Titicaca lies called?
53735.e: The Altiplano is a plateau at about 3500 to 4000 metres. It stretches across parts of Peru, Bolivia, Chile and Argentina.
53735.m: Lake Titicaca lies on the Altiplano plateau.

53736.q: According to the constitution, which city is the capital of Bolivia?
53736.e: Sucre is Bolivia's constitutional capital. The government and parliament, however, sit in La Paz.
53736.m: Sucre is Bolivia's capital, La Paz the seat of government.
