54843.e: A hurricane's energy comes from warm, evaporating sea water. Over land this energy source is missing, and the storm loses strength.
54843.m: Without warm sea water, a hurricane loses its strength.

54844.q: Which US city was widely flooded by Hurricane Katrina in 2005?
54844.e: Hurricane Katrina brought a storm surge that broke the levees in New Orleans. Large parts of the city were under water.
54844.m: Hurricane Katrina flooded the city of New Orleans in 2005.

54845.q: From what wind speed does a tropical cyclone count as a hurricane?
54845.e: A hurricane has at least force 12 on the Beaufort scale. That means wind speeds of about 119 km/h or more.
54845.m: A hurricane brings winds of at least about 119 km/h.

54846.q: From which kind of clouds do most strong tornadoes form?
54846.e: Supercells are large thunderstorms with a rotating updraught. Strong tornadoes can form from this rotation.
54846.m: Strong tornadoes usually form from rotating supercells.

54847.q: What is the strength of a tornado usually classified by?
a: By the month in which it occurs
54847.e: The wind in a tornado can rarely be measured directly. That is why the Fujita scale ranks tornadoes by the damage they cause; the strongest get level 5.
54847.m: Tornadoes are ranked by their damage.

54848.q: What makes a tornado different from a hurricane?
a: A tornado is much smaller and usually lasts only minutes
A tornado is much bigger and lasts for weeks
A tornado only forms over the sea
54848.e: A tornado is usually only a few dozen to a hundred metres wide and often lasts only minutes. A hurricane is hundreds of kilometres across and can last for days.
54848.m: A tornado is small and short-lived; a hurricane is huge and long-lived.

54849.q: What is a tornado that forms over a lake or the sea called?
54849.e: A waterspout is a whirlwind over a body of water. Waterspouts are occasionally seen over Swiss lakes too.
54849.m: A tornado over water is called a waterspout.

54850.q: Where is the best place to shelter during a tornado?
a: In the cellar or a windowless inner room
In a car on the road
54850.e: The main dangers are flying debris and shattering glass. A low-lying room without windows offers the best protection.
54850.m: In a tornado, shelter in the cellar or a room without windows.

54851.q: What wind speeds can the strongest tornadoes reach?
54851.e: Radar has measured wind speeds of over 400 km/h in the strongest tornadoes. That makes them some of the most violent winds on Earth.
54851.m: The strongest tornadoes bring winds of over 400 km/h.

54852.q: What is the tube-shaped cloud that reaches down to the ground in a tornado called?
54852.e: In a tornado, a rotating tube of cloud forms that looks like a funnel. It becomes visible through water vapour, dust and debris.
54852.m: The trunk of a tornado is a funnel cloud.

54853.q: What caused major flooding in Switzerland in August 2005?
a: A storm surge from the sea
54853.e: In August 2005 it rained very heavily for days on the north side of the Alps. Rivers burst their banks, and the damage came to about 3 billion francs.
54853.m: Days of heavy rain led to major floods in Switzerland in 2005.

54854.q: Why were the yearly floods of the Nile useful to the ancient Egyptians?
a: They brought fertile mud to the fields
They filled the pyramids with water
They brought gold from the mountains
54854.e: Every year the Nile flood left behind nutrient-rich mud. On it, farmers could grow rich harvests.
54854.m: The Nile flood brought the Egyptians fertile mud.

54855.q: Why do tarmac and concrete surfaces make floods worse?
54855.e: On sealed ground, rain runs straight off instead of soaking into the soil. So a lot of water reaches streams and rivers all at once.
54855.m: Sealed ground makes rain run off quickly and worsens floods.

54856.q: What measure is used today on many Swiss rivers to reduce the risk of flooding?
a: Cutting down all the trees on the banks
Building houses right on the banks
54856.e: When rivers are restored to a more natural state, they are widened and get floodplains. There, flood water can spread out without flooding settlements.
54856.m: Rivers with more space can take in flood water better.

54857.q: What is a sudden flood after very heavy rain called?
54857.e: In a flash flood, the water rises a lot in a short time. This is especially dangerous in narrow valleys and dried-up stream beds.
54857.m: A flash flood comes suddenly after heavy rain.

54858.q: Which country had floods in 2022 after an extremely strong monsoon, affecting about 33 million people?
54858.e: An extremely strong monsoon caused huge floods in Pakistan in 2022. More than two million people lost their homes.

54859.q: What is a flood retention basin for?
a: It holds back water during floods and releases it slowly
It supplies drinking water to cities
It is used as a swimming pool in summer
54859.e: A retention basin fills up during heavy rain and stores the water for a while. That way the river downstream swells less.
54859.m: Retention basins catch flood water and release it slowly.

54860.q: What is meant by a drought?
a: A long period with far too little rain or snow
A period with especially heavy snow
54860.e: In a drought, much less rain falls than usual for weeks or months. The soil dries out and plants suffer from lack of water.
54860.m: A drought is a long period with far too little rain.

54861.q: Which region on the southern edge of the Sahara suffered severe droughts in the 1970s and 1980s?
54861.e: In the Sahel, far too little rain fell for years. The droughts led to famines in which very many people died.
54861.m: The Sahel was hit by severe droughts in the 1970s and 1980s.

54862.q: What is it called when desert-like areas spread because of drought and overuse?
54862.e: In desertification, soils lose their fertility. The causes are droughts, but also overgrazing and deforestation.
54862.m: Desertification means that desert-like areas are spreading.

54863.q: In the drought summer of 2018, the Swiss Army transported water by helicopter. What for?
a: For indoor swimming pools in cities
54863.e: In 2018 many Alpine pastures had no water left for the livestock. So the army flew water to the animals on the pastures.
54863.m: In the drought summer of 2018, the army brought water to cows on the Alpine pastures.

54864.q: What is the drought and dust storm disaster on the Great Plains of the USA in the 1930s called?
54864.e: Long dry spells and poor farming methods made the topsoil dry out. The wind carried it away in huge dust storms.
54864.m: The Dust Bowl was a drought with dust storms in the USA in the 1930s.

54865.q: What do farmers measure to spot a drought early?
54865.e: Soil moisture shows how much water is available to plants in the ground. If it drops sharply, crop failures threaten.
54865.m: Soil moisture shows whether plants have enough water.

54866.q: What problem does a long drought cause for shipping on the Rhine?
a: Ships can carry less because the water level is low
54866.e: When the water is low, cargo ships have less depth to float in. So they may only take part of their load.
54866.m: When the water is low, Rhine ships can carry less cargo.

54867.q: Which climate phenomenon in the Pacific often leads to droughts in Australia and Indonesia?
54867.e: During El Niño, the eastern Pacific warms up unusually strongly. This shifts the rain areas, and the western Pacific becomes drier.
54867.m: El Niño often brings droughts to Australia and Indonesia.

54868.q: What is the most common natural cause of forest fires?
54868.e: Lightning can set dry wood or grass alight. However, most forest fires are caused by people.
54868.m: Lightning is the most common natural cause of forest fires.

54869.q: Which three things does a fire need to burn?
54869.e: These three conditions are called the fire triangle. If one of them is missing, the fire goes out.
54869.m: A fire needs fuel, oxygen and heat.

54870.q: In which canton are there especially many forest fires, often in winter and spring when the dry north föhn blows?
54870.e: On the south side of the Alps, the north föhn dries out leaves and soil a great deal. That is why the risk of forest fires in Ticino is often already high in winter.
54870.m: In Ticino the risk of forest fires is especially high when the north föhn blows.

54871.q: Why is the risk of forest fires especially high in very hot and dry summers?
a: Grass, leaves and wood have dried out
54871.e: Without rain, plants and soil dry out and burn easily. In the heatwave summer of 2003, for example, large forest fires raged in Valais.
54871.m: Dryness makes forests catch fire easily.

54872.q: In which country did huge bushfires rage during the “Black Summer” of 2019 and 2020?
54872.e: After a long drought, huge areas of bush and forest burnt in Australia. Countless wild animals such as koalas died.
54872.m: In the Black Summer of 2019 and 2020, large parts of Australia burnt.

54873.q: What is a firebreak in a forest for?
a: It is meant to stop a fire spreading
It is used as a playground
54873.e: A firebreak is a strip with no trees or bushes. Because nothing can burn there, the fire is stopped.
54873.m: A firebreak stops a fire because nothing burns there.

54874.q: What role do fires play in some ecosystems?
a: Some plants need fire for their seeds to sprout
Fire makes the soil infertile for ever
54874.e: Some plants, such as certain pines or eucalyptus species, only open their seed capsules in heat. After the fire, the seedlings find plenty of light and ash as fertiliser.
54874.m: Some plants only sprout after a fire.

54875.q: How are forest fires often fought on the steep slopes of the Swiss mountains?
a: With helicopters dropping water from containers
54875.e: Fire engines can hardly reach steep terrain. Helicopters collect water from lakes or rivers and release it precisely over the fire.
54875.m: In the mountains, forest fires are often put out with helicopters.

54876.q: Which type of avalanche causes the most fatal accidents among skiers and ski tourers?
54876.e: In a slab avalanche, a whole layer of snow breaks away at once. It is usually triggered by the victims themselves.
54876.m: Slab avalanches are the most dangerous for winter sports fans.

54877.q: In which town is the WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF located?
54877.e: The SLF in Davos researches snow and avalanches. In winter it publishes the daily avalanche bulletin for Switzerland.
54877.m: Switzerland's avalanche bulletin comes from the SLF in Davos.

54878.q: How many levels does the European avalanche danger scale have?
54878.e: The scale goes from level 1 (low) to level 5 (very high). Many accidents already happen at level 3 (considerable).
54878.m: The avalanche danger scale has five levels.

54879.q: Roughly from what slope angle can slab avalanches be triggered?
54879.e: Most slab avalanches release on slopes of about 30 degrees or steeper. The steeper the slope, the greater the danger.
54879.m: From about 30 degrees of slope, avalanches become a danger.

54880.q: Which device helps find people buried by an avalanche quickly?
54880.e: An avalanche transceiver sends a radio signal that other devices can locate. A shovel and a probe are also part of the emergency kit.
54880.m: An avalanche transceiver helps locate buried people quickly.

54881.q: Within what time should people buried by an avalanche ideally be freed so that their chance of survival is high?
54881.e: Most buried people survive the first few minutes. After that, the chance of survival drops quickly, mainly because of lack of oxygen.
54881.m: For avalanche victims every minute counts, especially the first 15.

54882.q: What happened in the avalanche winter of 1999 in the Alps?
a: Many avalanches buried houses and roads
54882.e: In February 1999 an extreme amount of snow fell in a short time. People died in Galtür in Austria and in Evolène in Valais.
54882.m: The avalanche winter of 1999 claimed many victims in the Alps.

54883.q: What naturally protects many mountain villages in Switzerland from avalanches?
54883.e: The trees hold the snow in place on the slope and slow down small avalanches. That is why protection forests are specially protected in Switzerland.
54883.m: Protection forests hold the snow in place and protect villages from avalanches.

54884.q: What most often triggers a landslide?
54884.e: Rainwater soaks the ground and makes it heavy and slippery. As a result, the slope loses its grip.
54884.m: Heavy rain is the most common trigger of landslides.

54885.q: Which village in the canton of Schwyz was buried by a huge rockslide in 1806?
54885.e: On 2 September 1806, a huge mass of rock broke away from the Rossberg. It buried Goldau and several hamlets, and almost 500 people died.
54885.m: The Goldau rockslide of 1806 was one of the worst natural disasters in Switzerland.

54886.q: Which village in the Bregaglia was hit by debris flows in 2017 after a rockslide on Piz Cengalo?
54886.e: In 2017 about three million cubic metres of rock fell from Piz Cengalo. The debris flows that followed reached the village of Bondo in the Grisons.
54886.m: Bondo was hit by debris flows after a rockslide in 2017.

a: A fast stream of water, mud and rock
A hiking trail in the mountains
54887.e: A debris flow pours like a thick sludge down stream beds into the valley. In Switzerland it is also called a “Rüfe”.
54887.m: A debris flow is a stream of water, mud and stones.

54888.q: Which village in the Lötschental in Valais was mostly buried by a glacier collapse in May 2025?
54888.e: Large amounts of ice and rock broke off the Birch Glacier and buried the village of Blatten. Because the residents had been evacuated a few days earlier, almost all of them survived.
54888.m: Blatten in the Lötschental was buried by ice and rock in 2025.

54889.q: Which village in the Grisons had to be evacuated in 2023 because of a sliding mountainside?
54889.e: The slope above Brienz/Brinzauls has been moving down into the valley for years. When a large rockfall threatened in 2023, all the residents had to leave the village.
54889.m: Brienz/Brinzauls in the Grisons sits on a sliding slope.

54890.q: Why are mountain slopes in the Alps becoming less stable because of climate change?
54890.e: Permafrost is permanently frozen ground that holds rock and rubble together like putty. When it thaws, rockfalls and landslides can become more frequent.
54890.m: Thawing permafrost makes mountain slopes less stable.

54891.q: Why does cutting down forests on slopes increase the risk of landslides?
a: The tree roots no longer hold the soil in place
54891.e: Roots anchor the soil and soak up water. Without trees, the soil becomes looser and slides away more easily when it rains.
54891.m: Tree roots hold the soil in place on slopes.

54892.q: On which day does the siren test take place in Switzerland every year?
a: On the first Wednesday in February
On the first Monday in May
On the last Friday in December
54892.e: The annual siren test checks whether the roughly 5000 sirens are working. It takes place on the first Wednesday in February.
54892.m: The siren test is always on the first Wednesday in February.

54893.q: What is the federal government's app that warns of disasters and emergencies called?
54893.e: The Alertswiss app sends out alarms, warnings and information from the authorities. It adds to the sirens and the radio.
54893.m: Alertswiss warns people of disasters on their mobile phones.

54894.q: What should you do when the sirens sound the general alarm?
a: Listen to the radio and follow the authorities' instructions
Run straight into the nearest forest
Get into the car and drive away
54894.e: The general alarm is a rising and falling wail. It means you should get information and follow the instructions of the authorities.
54894.m: When the sirens sound, listen to the radio and follow the authorities' instructions.

54895.q: What do sensors on the seabed measure in a tsunami early warning system?
54895.e: When a tsunami wave passes over a sensor, the pressure of the water column rises slightly. The data is sent to warning centres via buoys and satellites.
54895.m: Pressure sensors on the seabed detect tsunami waves.

54896.q: What is the most warning time an earthquake early warning system can give?
54896.e: Earthquakes cannot be predicted. An early warning system detects the fast first waves and warns before the destructive waves arrive, which gives only a few seconds' head start.
54896.m: Earthquake early warning systems give only seconds of warning.

54897.q: How many danger levels do the federal government's natural hazard warnings in Switzerland use?
54897.e: The warnings go from level 1 (no or low danger) to level 5 (very high danger). They apply, for example, to severe weather, floods or avalanches.
54897.m: The federal natural hazard warnings have five levels.

54898.q: How do experts monitor a volcano to warn of an eruption?
a: They measure earthquakes, ground uplift and gases
They count the visitors at the crater rim
They measure the length of the days
54898.e: When magma rises, there are often small earthquakes and the ground swells up. The amount of gas escaping can also change.
54898.m: Earthquakes, ground uplift and gases show that a volcano is becoming active.

54899.q: When does the water alarm sound in Switzerland?
a: When a dam is in danger of breaking
54899.e: The water alarm warns people living below large dams. It consists of low continuous tones and means you must leave the danger area immediately.
54899.m: The water alarm warns of the danger of a dam breaking.

54900.q: Which country has the fifth-largest population in the world as of 2025?
54900.e: According to the UN, Pakistan has about 255 million inhabitants. Its population is growing very fast.
54900.m: Pakistan is one of the five most populous countries in the world.

54901.q: Which country has the second-largest population in Africa as of 2025?
54901.e: Ethiopia has about 135 million inhabitants. It is also the most populous landlocked country in the world.
54901.m: Ethiopia has the second-largest population in Africa.

54902.q: Which country is third on the list of the most populous countries as of 2025?
54902.e: The USA has about 340 million inhabitants. That puts it well behind the two Asian giants, but ahead of all other countries.
54902.m: The USA is the third-largest country by population.

54903.q: Which is the most populous country in Africa?
54903.e: As of 2025, Nigeria has well over 230 million inhabitants. No other country in Africa has so many people.
54903.m: Nigeria has the most people in Africa.

54904.q: Which is the most populous country in South America?
54904.e: Brazil has about 210 million inhabitants. That is about half of all the people in South America.
54904.m: Brazil is the most populous country in South America.

54905.q: Which country has the fourth-largest population in the world as of 2025?
54905.e: Indonesia has about 285 million inhabitants, living on thousands of islands. It is the most populous country in Southeast Asia.
54905.m: Indonesia is the island nation with the fourth-largest population in the world.

54906.q: Which country has the most people who speak Spanish as their mother tongue?
54906.e: Mexico has about 130 million inhabitants, and almost all of them speak Spanish. Spain itself has only about 49 million inhabitants.
54906.m: Mexico is the largest Spanish-speaking country in the world.

54907.q: Which country has the most inhabitants in the European Union?
54907.e: Germany has about 83 million inhabitants. France comes second with about 68 million.
54907.m: Germany is the most populous country in the EU.

54908.q: Roughly how many people live in Switzerland (as of 2025)?
54908.e: According to the Federal Statistical Office, Switzerland has had over 9 million inhabitants since 2024. The population grows mainly through immigration.
54908.m: Over 9 million people live in Switzerland today.

54909.q: From how many inhabitants does the UN call a city a megacity?
54909.e: The UN calls cities with their surrounding areas megacities when they have 10 million inhabitants or more. Most have only grown this big in recent decades.
54909.m: A megacity has more than 10 million inhabitants.

54910.q: How many cities with at least one million inhabitants does Switzerland have?
54910.e: Switzerland's largest city, Zurich, has about 440,000 inhabitants. So Switzerland does not have a single city of a million people.
54910.m: Switzerland has no city with a million inhabitants.

54911.q: On which continent are most megacities?
54911.e: More than half of all people live in Asia, and cities are growing especially fast there. That is why most megacities are in Asia.
54911.m: Most of the world's megacities are in Asia.

54912.q: Which megacity lies on two continents, in Europe and in Asia?
54912.e: Istanbul lies on both sides of the Bosporus. One part belongs to Europe, the other to Asia.
54912.m: Across the Bosporus, Istanbul links Europe and Asia.

54913.q: Which megacity on the Gulf of Guinea is Nigeria's largest city?
54913.e: Lagos lies on a lagoon on the Atlantic coast. Well over 15 million people live in the metropolitan area, and the city is growing very fast.

54914.q: In which country is the megacity Shenzhen, which grew from a small town in just 40 years?
54914.e: Shenzhen lies in southern China, north of Hong Kong. From 1980 the city grew at great speed and today has over 17 million inhabitants.
54914.m: Shenzhen in China grew into a megacity very quickly.

54915.q: Which African megacity lies on the Nile?
54915.e: Cairo is the capital of Egypt and lies on the Nile just before the delta. Over 20 million people live in the metropolitan area.
54915.m: Cairo is the great megacity on the Nile.

54916.q: Which megacity on the west coast of the USA is the centre of the film industry?
54916.e: In the Hollywood district of Los Angeles, many films have been made for over a hundred years. The metropolitan area has over 12 million inhabitants.
54916.m: Los Angeles is the film city on the west coast of the USA.

54917.q: Which megacity is the capital of the Philippines?
54917.e: Manila is the capital of the Philippines. The Metro Manila area has over 13 million inhabitants.
54917.m: Manila is the capital of the Philippines.

54918.q: Which urban area was considered the largest in the world for decades?
54918.e: According to UN figures up to 2018, the Greater Tokyo area was by far the largest urban area in the world. A UN report from 2025 counts differently, using a new method.
54918.m: Tokyo was long considered the largest urban area in the world.

54919.q: Roughly what share of Japan's population lives in the Greater Tokyo area?
54919.e: Japan has about 124 million inhabitants, of whom over 35 million live in the Greater Tokyo area. That is almost a third of the whole population.
54919.m: Almost a third of Japanese people live in the Greater Tokyo area.

54920.q: According to the UN report of 2025, which city is the largest in the world?
54920.e: The UN report World Urbanization Prospects 2025 counts cities using a new method. According to it, Jakarta in Indonesia is the largest city, with about 42 million people.
54920.m: According to the UN's 2025 report, Jakarta is the largest city in the world.

54921.q: Which large city has grown together with Tokyo and is part of the Greater Tokyo area?
54921.e: Yokohama lies south of Tokyo on Tokyo Bay. With about 3.7 million inhabitants, it is Japan's second-largest city.
54921.m: Yokohama is part of the Greater Tokyo area.

54922.q: Which natural hazard is a particular threat to the Greater Tokyo area?
54922.e: Japan lies where several tectonic plates meet. The Great Kanto earthquake of 1923 destroyed large parts of the city.
54922.m: Tokyo lies in an area with many earthquakes.

54923.q: Roughly how many people live in Tokyo Prefecture (as of 2025)?
54923.e: Tokyo Prefecture is the administrative unit of the capital and has about 14 million inhabitants. Together with the neighbouring prefectures, though, the metropolitan area is much bigger.
54923.m: About 14 million people live in Tokyo Prefecture alone.

54924.q: On which Japanese island is Tokyo?
54924.e: Honshu is Japan's largest island. Osaka, Kyoto and Hiroshima are also there.
54924.m: Tokyo is on Honshu, Japan's largest island.

a: a core city with its suburbs
54925.e: An agglomeration consists of a core city and the surrounding municipalities that have grown together with it. The Zurich agglomeration, for example, includes many municipalities around the city.
54925.m: An agglomeration is a city together with its suburbs.

54926.q: What does population density tell you?
54926.e: Population density shows how many people live on one square kilometre on average. You divide the number of inhabitants by the area.
54926.m: Population density measures inhabitants per square kilometre.

54927.q: A city has 120,000 inhabitants and a density of 4000 inhabitants per km². How big is its area?
54927.e: You divide the inhabitants by the density: 120,000 : 4000 gives 30. So the city covers 30 km².
54927.m: Inhabitants divided by density gives the area.

54928.q: An island covers 50 km² and has 300 inhabitants per km². How many people live there?
54928.e: You multiply the density by the area: 300 times 50 gives 15,000 inhabitants.
54928.m: Density times area gives the number of inhabitants.

54929.q: Which country has the highest population density in the world?
54929.e: In the city state of Monaco, almost 40,000 people live on about 2 km². That makes almost 20,000 inhabitants per km².
54929.m: Monaco is the most densely populated country in the world.

54930.q: Which country is the most sparsely populated?
54930.e: In Mongolia only about 2 people live per km². Large parts of the country are steppe and desert.
54930.m: Mongolia is the most sparsely populated country in the world.

54931.q: Which larger country has an especially high density of over 1000 inhabitants per km²?
54931.e: Bangladesh is about three and a half times the size of Switzerland but has about 175 million inhabitants. No other larger country is so densely populated.
54931.m: Bangladesh is one of the most densely populated countries in the world.

54932.q: Which canton has the highest population density in Switzerland?
54932.e: Basel-Stadt is very small and consists almost entirely of city. Over 5000 people live there per km².
54932.m: Basel-Stadt is the most densely populated canton.

54933.q: Why do most people in Australia live on the coast?
a: The interior is covered in glaciers.
Building is banned in the interior.
The interior lies below sea level.
54933.e: Most of Australia's interior, the Outback, is desert and steppe. That is why most people live in the coastal cities.
54933.m: Australia is dry inside and densely populated on the coasts.

54934.q: Where does almost the whole population of Egypt live?
a: in the Nile valley and the Nile delta
in the middle of the Sahara
54934.e: Over 90 per cent of Egypt's area is desert. Almost all the people live where the Nile brings water.
54934.m: In Egypt, people live almost only along the Nile.

54935.q: What does a population pyramid show?
54935.e: A population pyramid shows how many men and women there are in each age group. The youngest are at the bottom, the oldest at the top.
54935.m: A population pyramid shows the age structure of a population.

54936.q: What shape is the population pyramid of a country with a great many children?
54936.e: With many births, the bottom bar is the widest. Towards the top the chart gets narrow, because fewer people reach old age.
54936.m: Many children make a pyramid with a wide base.

54937.q: What shape is the population pyramid when there are fewer children than adults?
54937.e: In the urn shape, the bottom part is narrower than the middle. Without immigration, the population ages and shrinks.
54937.m: An urn shape shows an ageing population.

54938.q: Which country has an urn-shaped population pyramid because of very few births?
54938.e: Japan has had few births for decades and has a very high life expectancy. That is why its population has been shrinking since about 2010.
54938.m: Japan has an ageing and shrinking population.

54939.q: What shape is a population pyramid when the population stays the same?
54939.e: In the bell shape, the bottom bars are about the same width. About as many children are born as are needed to keep the number the same.
54939.m: A bell shape shows a stable population.

54940.q: Without immigration, roughly how many children per woman are needed for a population to stay the same size?
54940.e: Two children replace the parents. The extra tenth makes up for the fact that not all children grow up themselves and that slightly more boys than girls are born.
54940.m: About 2.1 children per woman keep a population stable.

54941.q: On average, how many children did a woman in Switzerland have in 2024?
54941.e: According to the Federal Statistical Office, the birth rate in 2024 was about 1.3 children per woman (1.29). That is the lowest figure ever recorded.
54941.m: Women in Switzerland have fewer than two children on average.

54942.q: Which country has one of the highest birth rates in the world?
54942.e: In Niger, a woman has about 6 children on average. The population is very young.
54942.m: Niger has one of the highest birth rates in the world.

54943.q: Which age group is growing especially fast in Switzerland?
54943.e: The baby boom generation is reaching retirement age, and life expectancy is rising. That is why there are more and more people over 65.
54943.m: The Swiss population is getting older and older.

54944.q: What is a typical pull factor that draws people to the city?
54944.e: Pull factors are advantages that make a place attractive. The city attracts people with work, schools and hospitals, for example.
54944.m: Pull factors draw people to a new place.

54945.q: What is the movement of people from the countryside to the cities called?
54945.e: Many people leave villages because there is more work and there are more schools and hospitals in the city. This movement is called rural flight.
54945.m: Rural flight means people moving from the countryside to the city.

54946.q: According to a UN forecast from 2018, what percentage of people will live in cities in 2050?
54946.e: In 2018 the UN estimated that about two thirds of humanity would live in cities by 2050. The growth is happening mainly in Asia and Africa.
54946.m: By 2050 about two thirds of people will live in cities.

54947.q: What is a typical push factor that drives people away from the countryside?
a: lack of work in the countryside
54947.e: Push factors drive people away from where they live, for example poverty, drought or lack of work. Good hospitals, schools and wages in the city, on the other hand, attract people.
54947.m: Push factors drive people away from where they live.

54948.q: What is it called when people move out of the core city into the suburbs?
54948.e: In suburbanisation, people move to the area around the city where there is more space. Many then commute into the city to work.

54949.q: What are people who travel regularly back and forth between home and work called?
54949.e: Commuters live in one place and work in another. In Switzerland, most working people commute to a different municipality.
54949.m: Commuters travel every day between home and work.

54950.q: What is it called when settlements spread out into the countryside in a disorderly way?
54950.e: With urban sprawl, houses are built scattered outside the town and village centres. In Switzerland, the Spatial Planning Act tries to slow this down.
54950.m: Urban sprawl means disorderly building out into the countryside.

54951.q: On which continent does the smallest share of people live in cities?
54951.e: In Africa, still less than half of the people live in cities. But cities there are growing fastest today.
54951.m: In Africa a large share of people still live in the countryside.

a: a poor neighbourhood with simple huts
a nature park on the edge of town
54952.e: A slum is a residential area with very basic housing and little infrastructure. Slums often spring up on the edge of a city without permission.
54952.m: A slum is a very poor area of a city.

54953.q: What are the poor neighbourhoods on the hillsides of Rio de Janeiro called?
54953.e: In Brazil, informal settlements are called favelas. In Rio, many of them are on steep hills.
54953.m: Brazil's poor neighbourhoods are called favelas.

54954.q: In South Africa, what are the residential settlements called that were built for Black people during apartheid?
54954.e: During apartheid, Black people had to live in separate settlements on the edge of cities. These townships still exist today; Soweto is the best known.
54954.m: Townships are residential areas from the apartheid era in South Africa.

54955.q: In which city is Kibera, one of the largest slums in Africa?
54955.e: Kibera is in Nairobi, the capital of Kenya. Hundreds of thousands of people live there in a small space.
54955.m: Kibera is a large slum in Nairobi.

54956.q: In which Indian city is Dharavi, one of the largest slums in Asia?
54956.e: Dharavi lies in the middle of Mumbai. It has many small workshops, for example for recycling, pottery and leather.
54956.m: Dharavi is a huge slum in Mumbai.

54957.q: According to the UN, roughly how many people worldwide live in slums and informal settlements?
54957.e: The UN's human settlements programme estimates that over a billion people live in slums and informal settlements. That is about one in every seven or eight people.
54957.m: About a billion people live in slums.

54958.q: What is especially often missing in slums?
54958.e: Slums usually grow without planning. That is why there are often no sewage pipes, no clean drinking water and no safe electricity supply.
54958.m: Slums often lack sewers and clean water.

54959.q: Why do many people move from the countryside to the slums on the edge of cities?
a: They hope to find work in the city
They want to go on holiday there
There are no taxes in the city
54959.e: Many people cannot find work in the countryside. In the city they hope for a better life, but often they can only afford a simple hut.
54959.m: Many people come to the slums looking for work.

54960.q: Which UN organisation deals with cities and housing?
54960.e: UN-Habitat is the United Nations programme for human settlements. It works for better housing conditions and sustainable cities.
54960.m: UN-Habitat is the UN organisation for cities.

54961.q: Which language has the most native speakers in the world?
54961.e: Over 900 million people speak Mandarin Chinese as their mother tongue. No other language has so many native speakers.
54961.m: Mandarin has the most native speakers in the world.

54962.q: Which language is spoken by the most people overall, as a mother tongue and a foreign language together?
54962.e: About 1.5 billion people speak English, most of them as a second or foreign language. It is the most important language for science and international exchange.
54962.m: English is the most widespread language in the world.

54963.q: After Mandarin, which language has the second-most native speakers?
54963.e: Spanish is the mother tongue of about 480 million people. It is spoken in Spain and in most countries of Latin America.
54963.m: Spanish has the second-most native speakers in the world.

54964.q: What is the official language of Indonesia?
54964.e: After independence, Indonesian became the common official language. Alongside it, people speak hundreds of regional languages.
54964.m: In Indonesia, the official language is Indonesian.

54965.q: Apart from English, which language is an official language in Canada?
54965.e: Canada has two official languages. French is spoken mainly in the province of Québec.
54965.m: Canada has English and French as official languages.

54966.q: Apart from English, which language is an official language of India's central government?
54966.e: Hindi is written in the Devanagari script and is spoken mainly in the north of India. Altogether there are hundreds of languages in India.
54966.m: Hindi is an official language of India.

54967.q: Which of these languages is NOT an official language of the UN?
54967.e: The UN has six official languages: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish. German is not one of them.
54967.m: The UN has six official languages, and German is not one of them.

54968.q: In which African country is French an official language?
54968.e: Senegal was a French colony. Kenya, Ghana and Nigeria, on the other hand, were British colonies and have English as an official language.
54968.m: In Senegal, French is an official language.

54969.q: Which world language is the official language in Angola and Mozambique?
54969.e: Angola and Mozambique were Portuguese colonies until 1975. That is why the language of the former colonial power is still the official language today.
54969.m: In Angola and Mozambique, Portuguese is the official language.

54970.q: Which language is widely spoken in East Africa, for example in Tanzania?
54970.e: Swahili is an official language in Tanzania and Kenya. Many people in East Africa use it as a shared common language.
54970.m: Swahili is the most important common language of East Africa.

54971.q: In Switzerland, what is the town where a canton's government sits called?
54971.e: Every canton has a capital, where the government and parliament meet. Liestal, for example, is the capital of the canton of Basel-Landschaft.
54971.m: The cantonal capital is the main town of a canton.

54972.q: Which city is the capital of Australia?
54972.e: Canberra was specially planned as the capital, as a compromise between the rivals Sydney and Melbourne. Parliament has met there since 1927.
54972.m: Canberra is the capital of Australia.

54973.q: Which city is the capital of Turkey?
54973.e: Atatürk made Ankara the capital of the new republic in 1923. Ankara lies in the interior of Anatolia.
54973.m: Ankara is the capital of Turkey.

54974.q: Which city is the capital of Malaysia?
54974.e: Kuala Lumpur is the capital of Malaysia and is known for the Petronas Towers. The ministries, however, now work in the new city of Putrajaya.
54974.m: Kuala Lumpur is the capital of Malaysia.

54975.q: Which is the largest city in Vietnam?
54975.e: Ho Chi Minh City, formerly Saigon, is the largest city and economic centre of Vietnam. The capital, however, is Hanoi in the north.
54975.m: Ho Chi Minh City is bigger than the capital, Hanoi.

54976.q: Which city is the capital of Pakistan?
54976.e: Islamabad was built as a new capital in the 1960s. Pakistan's largest city is the port of Karachi.
54976.m: Islamabad is the capital of Pakistan.

54977.q: Which city is the seat of government of the Netherlands, even though Amsterdam is the capital?
54977.e: According to the constitution, Amsterdam is the capital. But the government, parliament and king work in The Hague.
54977.m: The Hague is the seat of government of the Netherlands.

54978.q: Which city is the capital of China?
54978.e: Beijing is the capital of the People's Republic of China. The Forbidden City, the former imperial palace, is there.
54978.m: Beijing is the capital of China.

54979.q: Which city is the capital of South Korea?
54979.e: Seoul lies on the Han River in the north-west of South Korea. Pyongyang, on the other hand, is the capital of North Korea.
54979.m: Seoul is the capital of South Korea.

54980.q: Which city is the capital of Iran?
54980.e: Tehran lies at the foot of the Alborz mountains in the north of Iran. Baghdad is the capital of Iraq.
54980.m: Tehran is the capital of Iran.

54981.q: Which capital is considered the coldest capital in the world?
54981.e: Ulaanbaatar, the capital of Mongolia, lies at about 1350 m in the interior of the country. In winter, temperatures often drop below minus 30 degrees.
54981.m: Ulaanbaatar is the coldest capital in the world.

54982.q: Which city is the capital of Nepal?
54982.e: Kathmandu lies in a valley in the Himalayas at about 1400 m. Many expeditions to Mount Everest start from Nepal.
54982.m: Kathmandu is the capital of Nepal.

54983.q: Which city is the capital of Thailand?
54983.e: Bangkok is the capital and largest city of Thailand. It is known for its temples and floating markets.
54983.m: Bangkok is the capital of Thailand.

54984.q: Which city is the capital of Kazakhstan?
54984.e: Astana has been the capital of Kazakhstan since 1997, taking over from Almaty. From 2019 to 2022 the city was called Nur-Sultan.
54984.m: Astana is the capital of Kazakhstan.

54985.q: Which city is the capital of Nigeria?
54985.e: Abuja was newly planned in the middle of the country and has been the capital since 1991. Before that, the capital was on the coast.
54985.m: Abuja is the capital of Nigeria.

54986.q: In which capital does the African Union have its headquarters?
54986.e: Addis Ababa is the capital of Ethiopia and lies at about 2350 m. The African Union has its headquarters there.
54986.m: The African Union has its headquarters in Addis Ababa.

54987.q: Which city is the seat of government of South Africa?
54987.e: South Africa has three capitals: Pretoria for the government, Cape Town for parliament and Bloemfontein for the highest court.
54987.m: Pretoria is the seat of government of South Africa.

54988.q: Which capital lies on the Congo River directly opposite Brazzaville?
54988.e: Kinshasa, the capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Brazzaville are separated only by the river. Kinshasa is a megacity with over 15 million inhabitants.
54988.m: Kinshasa and Brazzaville face each other across the Congo.

54989.q: Which city is the capital of Morocco?
54989.e: Rabat lies on the Atlantic coast and is the seat of the king and the government. Casablanca is bigger and is the economic centre.
54989.m: Rabat is the capital of Morocco.

54990.q: Which city is officially the capital of Tanzania?
54990.e: Dodoma lies inland and is the official capital. The port city of Dar es Salaam, however, is much bigger.
54990.m: Dodoma is the capital of Tanzania.

54991.q: Which city is the capital of Ghana?
54991.e: Accra lies on the Gulf of Guinea and is Ghana's largest city. Lomé is the capital of neighbouring Togo.
54991.m: Accra is the capital of Ghana.

54992.q: Which city is the capital of Uruguay?
54992.e: Montevideo lies on Uruguay's south coast on the Río de la Plata. Well over a third of the country's inhabitants live in the capital.
54992.m: Montevideo is the capital of Uruguay.

54993.q: Which capital was newly built in just a few years and opened in 1960?
54993.e: Brasília was newly planned in the interior of Brazil. From the air, its layout looks like an aeroplane.
54993.m: Brasília is a planned capital from 1960.

54994.q: Which city is the highest seat of government in the world?
54994.e: La Paz in Bolivia lies at about 3600 m above sea level. The government sits there, while the constitutional capital is Sucre.
54994.m: La Paz is the highest seat of government in the world.

54995.q: Which city is the capital of Colombia?
54995.e: Bogotá lies in the Andes at about 2600 m. Caracas is the capital of neighbouring Venezuela.
54995.m: Bogotá is the capital of Colombia.

54996.q: Which city is the capital of Cuba?
54996.e: Havana lies on Cuba's north coast. Its old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
54996.m: Havana is the capital of Cuba.

54997.q: Which city is the capital of Chile?
54997.e: Santiago lies in a valley in front of the Andes. More than a third of all Chileans live in the Greater Santiago area.
54997.m: Santiago is the capital of Chile.

54998.q: Which city is the capital of Peru?
54998.e: Lima lies on the Pacific coast and was founded by the Spanish in 1535. Cusco was once the capital of the Inca Empire.
54998.m: Lima is the capital of Peru.

54999.q: Which country finished building the Panama Canal after a French attempt had failed?
54999.e: A French company led by Ferdinand de Lesseps gave up the construction in the 1880s, partly because of diseases such as malaria and yellow fever. The USA took over in 1904 and completed the canal.
54999.m: The USA finished the Panama Canal after the French had failed.

55000.q: Why does the Panama Canal need locks?
a: Because the canal passes through a lake that lies higher up
Because the Pacific is much saltier
Because otherwise the ships would go too fast
Because the canal lies below sea level
55000.e: Locks raise the ships about 26 metres up to Gatún Lake and lower them again on the other side. A canal at sea level through the mountains would have been too difficult to build.
55000.m: In the Panama Canal, locks lift ships up to a lake that lies higher up.

55003.q: What was opened at the Panama Canal in 2016 so that bigger ships can pass through?
55003.e: The expansion created new, wider and longer locks, which opened in June 2016. Since then, much bigger container ships can fit through the canal.
55003.m: The 2016 expansion gave the Panama Canal bigger locks.

55004.q: Where does the water that fills the locks of the Panama Canal come from?
a: From freshwater lakes fed by rain
55004.e: Every time a ship passes through the locks, fresh water from Gatún Lake flows into the sea. During severe droughts, as in 2023, the number of crossings therefore had to be limited.
55004.m: The Panama Canal's locks need a lot of rainwater from reservoirs.

55005.q: Before the Panama Canal was built, which point did ships from New York to San Francisco have to sail around?
55005.e: Without a canal, the sea route went around the southern tip of South America at Cape Horn. The Panama Canal shortens this journey by about 13,000 kilometres.
55005.m: The Panama Canal saves ships the long detour around Cape Horn.

55006.q: Which port handles the most containers in the world (as of 2024)?
55006.e: The port of Shanghai in China has been the largest container port in the world since 2010. It handles well over 40 million standard containers a year.
55006.m: Shanghai has the largest container port in the world.

55007.q: In which country is Dubai with its huge port?
55007.e: Dubai is part of the United Arab Emirates. Its port, Jebel Ali, is the largest in the Middle East.
55007.m: Dubai is in the United Arab Emirates.

55008.q: Which city has Germany's largest seaport?
55008.e: The port of Hamburg lies on the Elbe, about 100 kilometres from the North Sea. It is the largest port in Germany.

55009.q: Which city state in Southeast Asia has one of the largest container ports in the world?
55009.e: Singapore is well placed on one of the most important shipping routes between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific. Its port is one of the busiest in the world.
55009.m: Singapore is a city state with a huge container port.

55010.q: Which port is the second-largest in Europe?
55010.e: The port of Antwerp in Belgium lies on the Scheldt. Since merging with Zeebrugge, it has been called Antwerp-Bruges.
55010.m: Antwerp in Belgium has the second-largest port in Europe.

55011.q: Which large Greek port has been mostly owned by a Chinese shipping company since 2016?
55011.e: In 2016 the Chinese state shipping company COSCO took a majority stake in the port of Piraeus near Athens. For China, Piraeus is an important gateway to Europe.
55011.m: The port of Piraeus is mostly owned by a Chinese shipping company.

55012.q: In which year was the Swiss merchant navy founded to secure supplies during the war?
55012.e: In the Second World War, Switzerland depended on its own ships to import food and raw materials. That is why ocean-going ships have sailed under the Swiss flag since 1941.
55012.m: Ocean-going ships have sailed under the Swiss flag since 1941.

55013.q: Which port is the largest container port in the USA (as of 2024)?
55013.e: The port of Los Angeles lies on the Pacific coast right next to the port of Long Beach. A large part of trade with Asia passes through it.
55013.m: Los Angeles has the largest container port in the USA.

55014.q: What are shipping containers usually made of?
55014.e: Containers are built from sturdy steel. That way they can withstand wind, weather and salt water and can be stacked high on top of each other.
55014.m: Shipping containers are made of steel.

55015.q: Who is considered the inventor of the modern shipping container?
55015.e: In 1956 the American transport businessman Malcolm McLean sent a ship with standardised containers to sea for the first time. This cut transport costs enormously.
55015.m: Malcolm McLean put the container on a ship in 1956.

55016.q: Roughly how long is a standard 20-foot container?
55016.e: A foot is about 30 centimetres, so 20 feet is about 6 metres. The big 40-foot container is about 12 metres long.
55016.m: A 20-foot container is about 6 metres long.

55017.q: Roughly how many standard containers (TEU) can the largest container ships carry (as of 2025)?
55017.e: The largest container ships, such as the “MSC Irina”, are about 400 metres long. They can carry over 24,000 standard containers.
55017.m: The largest container ships carry over 24,000 standard containers.

55018.q: Which container ship blocked the Suez Canal for days in March 2021?
55018.e: The “Ever Given” ran aground in the Suez Canal and got stuck sideways. For six days, hundreds of ships queued up, which disrupted world trade.
55018.m: In 2021 the “Ever Given” showed how important the Suez Canal is for world trade.

55019.q: In which Swiss city does MSC, the world's largest container shipping company, have its headquarters (as of 2025)?
55019.e: The Mediterranean Shipping Company (MSC) has been the world's largest container shipping company since 2022. Its headquarters are in Geneva, even though Switzerland has no coastline.
55019.m: The world's largest container shipping company is based in Geneva.

55020.q: What is the large crane that lifts containers off ships in a port called?
55020.e: A container gantry crane runs on rails along the quay and reaches far out over the ship. It lifts the containers one by one onto land or on board.
55020.m: Container gantry cranes load and unload containers in ports.

55021.q: What is a big advantage of standardised containers?
a: They fit on ships, trains and lorries
They float even without a ship
They never need to be locked
They are made of wood and so are light
55021.e: Because all containers have the same dimensions, they can be moved quickly between ship, train and lorry. The goods themselves do not need to be unpacked.
55021.m: Standardised containers switch quickly between ship, train and lorry.

55022.q: Roughly what share of world trade (by volume) is transported by ship?
55022.e: According to the UN trade organisation UNCTAD, over 80 per cent of traded goods by volume are transported by sea. Ships are the cheapest way to move large quantities.
55022.m: Most of world trade travels by ship.

55023.q: Which strait connects the Sea of Marmara with the Aegean Sea?
55023.e: The Dardanelles are in Turkey near the Gallipoli peninsula. Together with the Bosporus, they form the sea route from the Black Sea to the Mediterranean.
55023.m: The Dardanelles lead from the Sea of Marmara to the Aegean.

55024.q: Through which strait is a large part of the oil from the Persian Gulf shipped?
55024.e: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman. About a fifth of the oil used worldwide is transported through this strait.
55024.m: The Strait of Hormuz is the bottleneck for oil from the Persian Gulf.

55025.q: Which strait lies between the Malay Peninsula and the island of Sumatra?
55025.e: The Strait of Malacca connects the Indian Ocean with the South China Sea. It is one of the busiest shipping routes in the world.
55025.m: The Strait of Malacca connects the Indian Ocean with the Pacific region.

55026.q: Which strait separates the island of Sicily from the Italian mainland?
55026.e: At its narrowest point, the Strait of Messina is only just over 3 kilometres wide. Ferries link Sicily with Calabria here.
55026.m: The Strait of Messina lies between Sicily and Calabria.

55027.q: What is the narrowest part of the English Channel between England and France called?
55027.e: The Strait of Dover is only about 33 kilometres wide. The Channel Tunnel between England and France runs beneath it.
55027.m: At the Strait of Dover, England and France are closest together.

55028.q: Which strait between Denmark and Sweden has been crossed by a long bridge since 2000?
55028.e: The Øresund Bridge connects Copenhagen in Denmark with Malmö in Sweden. Part of the link runs through a tunnel under the sea.
55028.m: The Øresund Bridge connects Denmark and Sweden.

55029.q: Which strait separates Asia from North America?
55029.e: The Bering Strait lies between Russia and Alaska. At its narrowest point it is only about 82 kilometres wide.
55029.m: The Bering Strait lies between Russia and Alaska.

55030.q: Which strait at the southern tip of South America is named after a Portuguese navigator?
55030.e: In 1520 Ferdinand Magellan was the first European to sail through this strait in Chile. It connects the Atlantic with the Pacific.
55030.m: The Strait of Magellan is named after the navigator Ferdinand Magellan.

55031.q: In which city does OPEC, the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, have its headquarters?
55031.e: OPEC was founded in Baghdad in 1960. Since 1965 its headquarters have been in Vienna.
55031.m: OPEC has its headquarters in Vienna.

55032.q: How many litres does a barrel, the usual unit of measurement for oil, hold?
55032.e: A barrel holds about 159 litres. Oil prices are usually given in US dollars per barrel.
55032.m: One barrel of oil is about 159 litres.

55033.q: Which country has the largest proven oil reserves in the world (as of 2024)?
55033.e: Venezuela has huge deposits of heavy oil, especially in the Orinoco region. That puts it just ahead of Saudi Arabia.
55033.m: Venezuela has the largest oil reserves in the world.

55034.q: Which country has produced the most oil since 2018 (as of 2024)?
55034.e: Thanks to new extraction methods such as fracking, oil production in the USA rose sharply. Since 2018 it has been the world's largest oil producer.
55034.m: The USA produces the most oil today.

55035.q: What did oil form from over millions of years?
a: From dead plankton in the sea
55035.e: Tiny sea creatures sank to the seabed and were covered by mud. Under pressure and heat, they slowly turned into oil.
55035.m: Oil formed from the remains of tiny sea creatures.

55036.q: What happens in an oil refinery?
a: Crude oil is processed into petrol, diesel and heating oil
People search the ground for new oil
Oil is burnt to make electricity
Oil is stored under the sea
55036.e: In a refinery, crude oil is heated and separated into different parts. Switzerland still has one refinery, in Cressier in the canton of Neuchâtel.
55036.m: A refinery turns crude oil into petrol, diesel and heating oil.

55037.q: Which gas is natural gas mainly made of?
55037.e: Natural gas consists mostly of methane. When it burns, it produces heat, water and carbon dioxide.
55037.m: Natural gas consists mainly of methane.

55038.q: What is done to natural gas so that it can be transported as LNG in tanker ships?
a: It is cooled down a lot until it becomes liquid
It is pressed into solid cubes
It is heated until it glows
55038.e: At about minus 162 degrees Celsius, natural gas becomes liquid and takes up about 600 times less space. LNG stands for “liquefied natural gas”.
55038.m: LNG is natural gas that has been cooled until it is liquid.

55039.q: Which country has the largest natural gas reserves in the world (as of 2024)?
55039.e: Russia has the largest proven natural gas deposits, mainly in Siberia. Iran and Qatar come next.
55039.m: Russia has the largest natural gas reserves in the world.

55040.q: Which country produces by far the most coal (as of 2024)?
55040.e: China produces more than half of the world's coal. A large part of it is burnt in power stations to make electricity.
55040.m: China is the world's largest coal producer.

55041.q: What makes lignite (brown coal) different from hard coal?
a: It is younger and gives less energy
It only forms in the sea
55041.e: Lignite is geologically younger and contains more water than hard coal. That is why it gives less energy per kilogram when burnt.
55041.m: Lignite is younger and has less energy than hard coal.

55042.q: Which raw material was mined in many collieries in Germany's Ruhr region?
55042.e: In the Ruhr region, miners brought hard coal up from deep underground for over 150 years. The last colliery, in Bottrop, closed in 2018.
55042.m: The Ruhr region grew big through hard coal.

55043.q: Which fossil fuel releases the most CO2 for the energy it produces?
55043.e: Coal consists almost entirely of carbon. When it burns, it produces much more CO2 per amount of energy than natural gas.
55043.m: Coal is the fossil fuel that harms the climate most.

55044.q: What is coke made from hard coal mainly used for?
55044.e: Coke is made by heating hard coal without air. In a blast furnace it provides the heat and helps get iron out of iron ore.
55044.m: Without coke there would be no pig iron from the blast furnace.

55045.q: What is the mining of lignite in huge open pits called?
55045.e: Lignite often lies not very deep. Huge excavators remove the layers of earth above it and dig the coal out directly at the surface.
55045.m: In open-cast mining, coal is dug out of open pits.

55046.q: Which period of Earth's history is named after coal?
55046.e: The Carboniferous lasted from about 359 to 299 million years ago. The name comes from the Latin word “carbo” for coal, because many coal deposits formed then.
55046.m: The Carboniferous is named so because a lot of coal formed in that time.

55047.q: Which country mines most of the world's rare earths (as of 2024)?
55047.e: China produces about two thirds of the world's rare earths and processes an even bigger share. Other countries are therefore heavily dependent on China.
55047.m: China is the biggest supplier of rare earths.

55048.q: What, for example, are rare earth metals needed for?
a: For strong magnets in mobile phones and wind turbines
55048.e: Rare earths such as neodymium are found in strong magnets, for example in electric motors, wind turbines, headphones and mobile phones.
55048.m: Rare earths are found in many modern devices.

55049.q: What is the rare earth metal neodymium especially needed for?
55049.e: Neodymium magnets are the strongest permanent magnets. They are needed, for example, in electric motors, wind turbines and headphones.

55050.q: In which huge salt flat in Bolivia are there large lithium deposits?
55050.e: The Salar de Uyuni is the largest salt flat in the world. Under its salt crust lies brine containing a lot of lithium, which is needed for batteries.
55050.m: There is a lot of lithium in the Salar de Uyuni.

55051.q: Which country produces the most iron ore (as of 2024)?
55051.e: Australia mines huge amounts of iron ore, especially in the Pilbara region. Much of it is shipped to China and made into steel there.
55051.m: Australia is the world's largest iron ore producer.

55052.q: Which country produces the most copper (as of 2024)?
55052.e: Chile has been the world's largest copper producer for decades. Some of the largest copper mines are in the Atacama Desert.
55052.m: Chile is the land of copper.

55053.q: Which country produces the most gold (as of 2024)?
55053.e: According to the US Geological Survey, China produced the most gold in 2024, ahead of Russia and Australia. South Africa used to be in first place for a long time.
55053.m: China is the world's largest gold producer today.

55054.q: Which country without its own gold mines is one of the most important countries for refining gold?
55054.e: Switzerland has some of the largest gold refineries in the world, several of them in Ticino. A large share of the gold traded worldwide is purified here and cast into bars.
55054.m: Much of the world's gold is made into bars in Switzerland.

a: A large farm that usually grows only one crop
A small vegetable garden behind the house
A forest that is not used
55055.e: On plantations, crops such as coffee, tea, bananas or oil palms are grown over large areas. Usually it is a monoculture, meaning only a single kind of plant.
55055.m: A plantation is a large farm usually growing only one kind of plant.

55056.q: Which country produces the most palm oil (as of 2024)?
55056.e: Indonesia and Malaysia together produce most of the palm oil, with Indonesia clearly in the lead. Much rainforest was cleared for new plantations.
55056.m: Indonesia is the world's largest palm oil producer.

55057.q: Which plant provides the most vegetable oil worldwide?
55057.e: The oil palm gives a lot of oil per area and is therefore the most important oil plant in the world. Palm oil is found in many foods, soaps and cosmetics.
55057.m: No plant provides as much oil as the oil palm.

55058.q: Which plant do the fibres for denim come from?
55058.e: Jeans are woven from denim, a tough cotton fabric. Cotton grows in warm countries and needs a lot of water to grow.

55059.q: On which continent is by far the largest part of the world's rice harvested?
55059.e: About nine tenths of the world's rice grows in Asia, mainly in China and India. Rice is a staple food for more than half of humanity.
55059.m: Most of the world's rice grows in Asia.

55060.q: Which country produces the most tea (as of 2024)?
55060.e: China is where tea comes from and is still the largest producer today. India and Kenya come next.
55060.m: China is the world's largest tea producer.

55061.q: Which country harvests the most soya beans (as of 2024)?
55061.e: Brazil has overtaken the USA as the largest soya producer. Much of the harvest is exported as animal feed, and rainforest and savannah are cleared for new fields.
55061.m: Brazil is the world's largest soya producer.

55062.q: What is a disadvantage of monocultures on plantations?
a: The soil becomes more and more fertile
55062.e: When the same plant grows everywhere, a pest finds a huge amount of food and can spread quickly. In addition, the soil gets worn out, and a lot of pesticide is used.
55062.m: In monocultures, pests have an easy time.

55063.q: In which climate zone is coffee grown?
55063.e: Coffee needs warmth, lots of rain and no frost. That is why it grows in the so-called coffee belt between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn.
55063.m: Coffee grows in the coffee belt of the tropics.

55064.q: Which Asian country is the second-largest coffee producer in the world (as of 2024)?
55064.e: Vietnam mainly grows the Robusta variety. That puts it second, behind Brazil.
55064.m: After Brazil, Vietnam is the second-largest coffee country.

55065.q: Which two types of coffee are grown most worldwide?
55065.e: Arabica is considered milder and tends to grow in the highlands. Robusta is stronger, contains more caffeine and can cope with more heat.
55065.m: The most important coffee types are called Arabica and Robusta.

55066.q: Which food does Switzerland export even more of by value than cheese or chocolate?
55066.e: Switzerland does not grow any coffee itself, but it roasts imported beans and sells them abroad, for example in capsules. In recent years these exports have been worth about 3 billion francs a year.
55066.m: Switzerland exports roasted coffee worth billions of francs.

The roots of the coffee plant
55067.e: The coffee plant bears red fruits called coffee cherries. Each fruit usually contains two seeds, which are roasted and sold as coffee beans.
55067.m: Coffee beans are the seeds of the coffee cherry.

55068.q: Which country harvests the most bananas (as of 2024)?
55068.e: India harvests the most bananas in the world. But almost all of them are eaten in the country itself.
55068.m: India harvests the most bananas but eats almost all of them itself.
